questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A consumer from State A filed a $100,000 products liability action in federal court against a manufacturer incorporated and with its principal place of business in State B. The consumer claimed that a flaw in the manufacturer's product had resulted in severe injuries to the consumer. In its answer, the manufacturer asserted a third-party complaint against the product designer, also incorporated and with its principal place of business in State B. Believing that the consumer had sued the wrong defendant, the manufacturer claimed both that the designer was solely responsible for the flaw that had led to the consumer's injuries and that the manufacturer was not at fault.
The designer is aware that the manufacturer did not follow all of the designer's specifications when making the product.
Which of the following arguments is most likely to achieve the designer's goal of dismissal of the third-party complaint?

choices.A: The court does not have subject-matter jurisdiction over the third-party complaint, because both the manufacturer and the designer are citizens of State B.
choices.B: The manufacturer failed to obtain the court's leave to file the third-party complaint.
choices.C: The manufacturer's failure to follow the designer's specifications caused the flaw that resulted in the consumer's injuries.
choices.D: The manufacturer's third-party complaint failed to state a proper third-party claim.

questions.explanation:
Third-party practice
(impleader)
Proper
(derivative liability)
π

Original claim
Impleader

Improper

Original claim
Impleader
Nonparty

A defendant may add a nonparty to a suit through third-party practice (ie, impleader). However, the third-party complaint must be based on derivative liability—ie, it must assert that the nonparty is liable to the defendant for all (ie, indemnity) or part (ie, contribution) of the plaintiff's claim. A third-party complaint should therefore be dismissed if it asserts that the nonparty is directly liable to the plaintiff or liable to the defendant for another claim.

Here, the defendant-manufacturer's third-party complaint against the nonparty-designer asserts that the plaintiff-consumer sued the wrong party. Since the manufacturer is claiming that the designer is solely responsible for the consumer's injuries—ie, directly liable to the consumer—the best argument to dismiss the third-party complaint is that it fails to state a proper third-party claim.

(Choice A) The court has subject-matter jurisdiction over the third-party complaint through supplemental jurisdiction because it (1) shares the same facts as the consumer's claim, (2) does not destroy diversity between the consumer and manufacturer, and (3) is made by a defendant.

(Choice B) A defendant must obtain the court's leave (ie, permission) to file a third-party complaint if more than 14 days have passed since the defendant served his/her original answer. But since this third-party complaint was asserted within the manufacturer's answer, leave of court was not required.

(Choice C) An argument that the manufacturer failed to follow the designer's specifications is a factual allegation. But the truth of this allegation is irrelevant because the court will accept a complaint's factual allegations as true and ignore the opposing party's (designer's) allegations when assessing if the complaint states a proper claim.

📌 Educational Objective

Third-party practice (ie, impleader) allows a defendant to add a nonparty who may be liable to the defendant for all or part of the plaintiff's claim (ie, derivative liability).

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 14 (third-party practice).
questions.zh-question:
一名来自A州的消费者在联邦法院对一家在B州注册成立且主要营业地在B州的制造商提起了10万美元的产品责任诉讼。消费者声称制造商产品的一个缺陷导致其受到严重伤害。制造商在其答辩状中，对产品设计师（同样在B州注册成立且主要营业地在B州）提出了第三方诉讼请求。制造商认为消费者告错了被告，声称设计师对导致消费者受伤的缺陷负有全权责任，而制造商没有过错。
设计师知道制造商在生产产品时并未完全遵循设计师的所有规格。
以下哪项论点最有可能实现设计师驳回第三方诉讼请求的目标？

zh-choices.A: 法院对该第三方诉讼请求不具有事项管辖权，因为制造商和设计师都是B州公民。
zh-choices.B: 制造商未能获得法院许可来提交第三方诉讼请求。
zh-choices.C: 制造商未能遵循设计师的规格导致了造成消费者受伤的缺陷。
zh-choices.D: 制造商的第三方诉讼请求未能提出适当的第三方诉讼主张。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第三方诉讼（third-party practice / impleader）只能拉进一个对被告负有派生责任的非当事人，不能拿来硬说“你才是真正侵权人”。

三秒认题路径：

被告拉人进来 → 看是否派生责任 → 只说“你是主责” → 不是 indemnity/contribution → 选 D

核心法律规则

被告可以用 第三方诉讼（impleader） 把非当事人拉进来，但前提是这个人要对被告承担 派生责任（derivative liability），也就是对原告这笔请求的全部或部分向被告负责，比如 赔偿（indemnity） 或 分担（contribution）。
如果第三方起诉书只是说“原告告错人了，真正该负责的是第三人”，这叫直接责任，不是第三方诉讼的正确用途，所以要被驳回。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 14（第三方诉讼规则）——锁定结论：只有“对被告派生负责”的人，才能被 impleader 拉进来。

思维导图

原告消费者
主张产品缺陷伤害
→
被告制造商
想把责任甩给第三人
→
第三人设计者
是否对制造商负派生责任？
关卡 1：第三方人是否要对“被告”负责？
YES：indemnity / contribution → 可以考虑 impleader。
NO：只是“你才是真凶” → 卡死：不是 proper third-party claim。
本题事实怎么落？
题干：制造商说设计者“对消费者伤害全责”，这是在主张直接责任，不是在主张设计者要对制造商负派生责任。
结论：第三方诉状写错类型，最强删帖理由就是 failed to state a proper third-party claim。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然设计者没按规格做，制造商就能把它拉进来一起打官司。
但考试真正问的是：第三方诉讼能不能用来找“对被告负责”的人，不是能不能找“真正该对原告负责”的人。
司法考试看的是「能不能用第三方诉讼救济被告」，而不是「设计者到底有没有做错」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干第三方设计者被说成“对消费者直接负责”，这不是对制造商的派生责任，所以第三方诉状本身就写歪了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 司法管辖误判

✕ A: 把 subject-matter jurisdiction 当成争点了，真正问题是诉讼类型写错。

❌ 法律适用 | 留改期限误判

✕ B: 盯着 leave of court，但本题第三方诉状是时限内提出的。

❌ 事实误判 | 事实真伪偷换

✕ C: 把“制造商没照规格做”当成抗辩，法院先看的是第三方起诉书写没写对。

这题建议用什么方法？

先问第三方主张是不是派生责任，再看有没有把“真正责任人”错当成 impleader 对象。

考场速记

记住一句：第三方诉讼（impleader）只认“对被告负责”，不认“对原告负责”。
看到题干在说“你才是真正侵权人”，先警觉：这通常不是 proper third-party claim。
以后做题就抓这条：派生责任才进门，直接责任就出局。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A woman and her wife believed that a company providing credit scores intentionally lowered their scores because they are a same-sex couple. The couple's lawyer discovered 10 other individuals who had their credit scores lowered by the same company. These individuals claim that their scores were lowered based on their race.
The lawyer filed suit in federal court on behalf of the couple and the 10 other individuals against the company for violating a federal statute. One provision of the statute forbids racial discrimination and another provision prohibits sexual-orientation discrimination. The couple are the only plaintiffs named in the complaint. The lawyer moved to certify the case as a class action.
Which of the following would be an invalid argument for the company to challenge class action certification?

choices.A: The class does not share common questions of law or fact.
choices.B: The class is not numerous.
choices.C: The company does not discriminate against any class when calculating credit scores.
choices.D: The named couple's claim is not typical of the class.

questions.explanation:
Certification requirements for class action
(FRCP 23)
Prerequisites
  • Numerosity: class is so numerous that joinder of all members is impracticable
  • Commonality: class shares common questions of law or fact
  • Typicality: claims or defenses of named parties are typical of class AND
  • Adequacy: named parties will fairly & adequately protect class's interests
Case suitable for class action
  • Separate actions would create risk of (1) inconsistent decisions regarding parties or (2) impairment of absent class members' interests
  • Injunctive or declaratory relief is appropriate because opposing party's actions generally applied to whole class OR
  • Common questions of law or fact predominate over individual questions & class action is superior method to resolve dispute
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure

A class action is a suit filed by one or more named plaintiffs as class representatives on behalf of similarly harmed unnamed plaintiffs.* All actions filed by a purported class representative require certification by the court at the earliest practical time. Plaintiffs seeking class action certification must establish—and the defendant can challenge certification on—all of the following prerequisites:

• Numerosity – the class is so numerous that joining all the members as named plaintiffs is impracticable (usually met when there are over 40 members) (Choice B)

• Commonality – the class shares common questions of law or fact (Choice A)

• Typicality – the named plaintiffs' claims are typical of the claims of the class (Choice D)

• Adequacy – the named plaintiffs will fairly and adequately protect the interests of the class

However, the argument that the company does not discriminate against any class when calculating credit scores goes toward the merits of the case—not class action certification. Since the court will not consider the merits of the underlying action when determining whether to certify a class, this is an invalid argument to challenge certification.

*A class action may also be asserted against named defendants on behalf of similarly situated unnamed defendants, but this procedure is extremely rare.

📌 Educational Objective

A party seeking class action certification must establish four prerequisites: numerosity, commonality, typicality, and adequacy. A court deciding whether to certify a class action will not consider the merits of the underlying case.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(a) (prerequisites for class action certification).
  • 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 1476 (2019) (explaining that a court will not examine a case's merits when deciding class action certification).

一名女性和她的妻子认为，一家提供信用评分的公司因为她们是同性伴侣而故意降低了她们的评分。这对伴侣的律师发现，另有10人的信用评分也被同一家公司降低。这些人声称，他们的评分是因其种族而被降低的。

该律师代表这对伴侣以及另外10人，向联邦法院提起诉讼，指控该公司违反了一项联邦法规。该法规的一项条款禁止种族歧视，另一项条款禁止基于性取向的歧视。这对伴侣是起诉状中唯一的具名原告。律师请求将该案认证为集体诉讼。

以下哪项是该公司在质疑集体诉讼认证时提出的无效论点？

zh-choices.A: 该集体不具有共同的法律或事实问题。
zh-choices.B: 该集体人数不足。
zh-choices.C: 该公司在计算信用评分时，未对任何群体进行歧视。
zh-choices.D: 具名伴侣的诉求不具有该集体的典型性。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Class Actions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：公司挑战 class action certification（集体诉讼认证） 时，哪些理由能打 FRCP 23(a)（联邦民事诉讼规则23(a)） 的要件，哪些只是拿案件实体去绕路。

三秒认题路径：

认证问题 → 看四要件 → 找实体抗辩 → 排除 C

核心法律规则

Class action（集体诉讼） 先要过四个门槛：numerosity（人数众多）、commonality（共同性）、typicality（典型性）、adequacy（充分代表性）。考场意思：被告要挑战认证，就得打这些门槛本身。

但法院在决定要不要认证时，does not consider the merits（不看实体胜负）。考场意思：你不能先说“我根本没歧视”，那是在争最后谁赢，不是在争能不能把这案子做成 class action。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(a) — 认证只查四要件，不先裁实体争点。

思维导图

认证门槛 1
numerosity（人数众多）
题干有 12 人，足够让共同起诉不方便。
认证门槛 2
commonality（共同性）
都在争公司算分时是否按受保护特征歧视。
认证门槛 3
typicality（典型性）
名义原告的主张要像整个类成员的主张；这里夫妻二人的主张不靠“公司根本没歧视”来判断。
认证门槛 4
adequacy（充分代表性）
题干没有给出代表利益冲突问题。
卡死点
“公司不歧视” 这是在打实体胜负，不是在打认证门槛，所以不能用来反对 class certification。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：公司既然说自己没有歧视，那就能直接反对认证。

但考试真正问的是：这个理由是不是在打 FRCP 23(a) 的认证要件；不是的话，就别拿来当认证攻击。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 does not discriminate 直接是在争实体责任，不是 class certification（集体诉讼认证） 的四要件，所以这条挑战理由无效。

❌ 概念混淆 | 共同性误判

✕ A: 把 common questions 和实体争点混在一起了，认证看的是是否共享法律或事实问题。

❌ 事实误判 | 人数门槛误读

✕ B: 题干明明已经有 12 人，你却硬说不够 numerous。

❌ 法律适用 | 典型性错位

✕ D: 名义原告是否 typical 要看主张是否同类，不是拿“公司没歧视”来偷换标准。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定 Rule 23(a) 四要件，再把所有“实体对错”类说法一律踢出认证分析。

考场速记

口诀：认证先看四要件，实体胜负先别管；看到 class action certification，先问“人数、共同、典型、充分代表”四个点。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A man sued his supervisor in a federal district court for sexual harassment in violation of federal law. During discovery, the man's attorney served the supervisor with a request to admit that the supervisor made derogatory jokes about the employee at a company party. The supervisor admitted to making the jokes. The man's attorney has now filed a motion with the district court for permission to take the depositions of 15 employees who will testify to hearing the supervisor make the derogatory jokes at the company party.
If the court denies the man's motion, what is the likely explanation?

choices.A: The company did not designate the employees to testify on its behalf.
choices.B: The court may not alter the 10-deposition limit.
choices.C: The depositions would be unreasonably cumulative and duplicative.
choices.D: The employees cannot be deposed because they are not parties in the suit.

questions.explanation:
Limitations on discovery
(FRCP 26(b)(2))
Permissible Court may alter limits upon:
• number of depositions, interrogatories, or requests for admission and
• length of oral depositions
Required Court must limit discovery that:
• is unreasonably cumulative or duplicative
• is obtainable from more convenient, less burdensome, or less expensive source
• contains information that party had ample opportunity to obtain or
• is outside scope of discovery
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

Discovery is the pretrial phase of a lawsuit during which the parties can use various methods to compel disclosure of information related to the case. Information is within the scope of discovery if it is relevant to any party's claim or defense, proportional to the needs of the case, and not privileged. Although the scope of discovery is broad, a federal court must limit the frequency or extent of discovery pursuant to a party's motion or on its own initiative when the discovery sought:

  • is unreasonably cumulative or duplicative
  • can be obtained from a more convenient, less burdensome, or less expensive alternative source
  • contains information that the party has had ample opportunity to obtain by other means or
  • is outside the scope of discovery.

Here, the man seeks to take the depositions of employees who will testify that they heard the supervisor make derogatory jokes about the man. This nonprivileged information is within the scope of discovery since it is relevant and proportional to the man's sexual harassment claim. However, the depositions would be unreasonably cumulative and duplicative because the supervisor admitted to making the jokes in response to the man's request for admission. Therefore, this is the likely explanation if the court denies the man's motion.

(Choice A) An organization (e.g., the company) that has been served with proper written notice of a deposition must designate individuals to testify on its behalf. However, such a designation is irrelevant here since the company is not a deponent in the case.

(Choice B) A federal court may alter the 10-deposition limit if a party requests the court's leave (i.e., permission).*

*Leave of court is also required when (1) the deposition is sought before the initial planning conference, (2) the deponent has already been deposed in the case, or (3) the deponent is in prison.

(Choice D) A party may depose any other party or nonparty—including the employees.

📌 Educational Objective

A court must limit the frequency or extent of discovery when the discovery sought (1) is unreasonably cumulative or duplicative, (2) can be obtained from a more convenient, less burdensome, or less expensive source, (3) contains information that the party has had time to obtain by other means, or (4) is outside the scope of discovery.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(2)(C) (required limitations on discovery).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子因其主管违反联邦法律对其进行性骚扰，而在联邦地区法院提起诉讼。在证据开示（discovery）阶段，该男子的律师向主管送达了一份承认请求书（request to admit），要求其承认在一次公司聚会上对该员工讲过贬损性笑话。主管承认曾讲过这些笑话。该男子的律师现向地区法院提出动议（motion），请求许可（permission/leave）对15名将作证称在公司聚会上听到主管讲贬损性笑话的员工进行录证（take the depositions）。

如果法院驳回该男子的动议，最可能的解释是什么？

zh-choices.A: 该公司未指定这些员工作为其代表进行作证。
zh-choices.B: 法院不得更改10次录证的限制。
zh-choices.C: 这些录证将构成不合理的累积和重复。
zh-choices.D: 这些员工不能被录证，因为他们不是本案的当事人。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery, disclosures, sanctions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：法院能否因为重复取证（cumulative or duplicative discovery）而限制证人沉淀式的重复证言。

三秒认题路径：

请求取证 → 已经认了 → 15人重复 → 过度累赘 → 选 C

核心法律规则

抓住法院必须限制的那一类取证

发现（discovery）考场意思：先问资料是不是相关、比例适当、且不受特权保护；但即使能取，法院也必须限制那些不合理重复（unreasonably cumulative or duplicative）的取证。

更方便、更省事、或更便宜的来源（more convenient, less burdensome, or less expensive source）考场意思：如果同一信息已经能从更省力的方式拿到，法院就会砍掉多余动作。

附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）这里不适用；本题不是上诉题，而是问为什么法院会拒绝一串重复证人。

核心判例： FRCP 26(b)(2)(C) 锁定本题结论：发现一旦变成重复、累赘，法院就应当限缩。

思维导图

题干先给你什么？
事实 1：被告已经在request for admission里承认“自己说过这些侮辱性笑话”。
事实 2：原告还要再传 15 名员工，说他们也听见了。
规则关卡：法院必须砍掉unreasonably cumulative or duplicative 的取证。
卡死点：同一事实已经被承认，再叫 15 个人重复说，没必要。
结论：法院拒绝许可的最可能理由 = 这些证言是重复、累赘的。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然这些员工都亲耳听到，就应该都能被deposition（口供/证言）。
但考试真正问的是：同一个事实已经被被告自己承认了，法官能不能把重复取证砍掉。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 request for admission 已经承认同一笑话，再传 15 个员工只会把同一事实重复一遍，所以法院可因 unreasonably cumulative or duplicative 直接限缩取证。

❌ 概念混淆 | 证人代表误判

✕ A: 误把公司代表作证规则搬来这里，designate individuals 这题根本没在问公司。

❌ 法律适用 | 上限刚性误判

✕ B: 以为 10 次证言上限绝对不能动，但法院本来就能在许可下调整。

❌ 事实误判 | 非当事人偷换

✕ D: 把“不是当事人”当成不能取证，nonparties 也可以被传唤作证。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否已有更省力的来源；一旦同事实已承认，就优先锁定重复、累赘这条限缩规则。

考场速记

记住一句：同一事实已经拿到，就别让 15 个人把它再说一遍。 发现题先找 重复、累赘、可更便宜取得 这三条限缩理由；只有真的缺信息时，才继续扩张取证。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A pedestrian domiciled in State A was crossing a street in State B when he was hit by a car driven by a citizen of a foreign country. Both the pedestrian and the driver suffered injuries.
The pedestrian filed a negligence action against the driver in a federal district court in State B, seeking $100,000 in damages. The driver believes that the pedestrian was crossing the street illegally and is therefore responsible for the accident. The driver seeks an attorney's advice on how best to respond to the action. Assume that State B is a contributory negligence state.
How should the attorney advise the driver to respond?

choices.A: File an answer raising the affirmative defense of contributory negligence and asserting a counterclaim for negligence, seeking damages for the driver's injuries.
choices.B: File an answer raising the affirmative defense of contributory negligence and move for judgment on the pleadings.
choices.C: Move to dismiss for lack of personal jurisdiction, because the driver is not a citizen of State B.
choices.D: Move to dismiss for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction, because the driver is not a U.S. citizen.

questions.explanation:
Contents of answer
Required
  • Admissions & denials
  • Motions not waived
  • Affirmative defenses
  • Compulsory counterclaims
Permitted
  • Permissive counterclaims
  • Crossclaims

A defendant must file an answer in response to a plaintiff's lawsuit unless the suit is dismissed (eg, when the court grants a Rule 12(b) motion).* An answer must include the following items or else they are waived:

  • Admissions or denials for each allegation
  • Motions that have not already been waived
  • Affirmative defenses—ie, assertions that can negate or reduce liability even if every element of the opposing party's claim is proven (eg, contributory negligence)
  • Compulsory counterclaims—ie, claims asserted against an opposing party in response to that party's earlier claim that (1) arise from the same transaction or occurrence as the earlier claim and (2) do not require adding another party over whom the court cannot acquire jurisdiction

Here, the driver has an affirmative defense based on the pedestrian's contributory negligence in illegally crossing the street. The driver also has a compulsory counterclaim because his injuries arose out of the same accident as the pedestrian's claim and no additional party is required. Therefore, the attorney should advise the driver to file an answer raising the affirmative defense and the compulsory counterclaim seeking damages for his injuries.

*The defendant must also serve the answer on the plaintiff. If the plaintiff is represented by an attorney, service must be made on the plaintiff's attorney unless the court orders otherwise.

(Choice B) A court can enter judgment on the pleadings when the undisputed material facts in the pleadings establish that the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. But here, the material facts are disputed since each party claims that the other party was responsible.

(Choice C) Although the driver is not a State B citizen, the court has personal jurisdiction because the driver's minimum contacts with State B—driving on its roads—gave rise to the pedestrian's claim.

(Choice D) Subject-matter jurisdiction based on diversity exists in a suit involving a foreign citizen if (1) he/she is not a permanent resident living in the same state as the opposing party and (2) the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000. Here, both requirements are satisfied.

📌 Educational Objective

An answer must include (1) admissions and denials, (2) motions that have not been waived, (3) affirmative defenses, and (4) compulsory counterclaims.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 8(c) (affirmative defenses).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 13(a) (compulsory counterclaims).

该行人在B州的联邦地区法院对司机提起过失诉讼，索赔10万美元。司机认为行人非法穿越马路，因此应对事故负责。司机就如何最佳应对此诉讼征求律师意见。假设B州是一个采用与有过失原则的州。

律师应建议司机如何回应？

zh-choices.A: 提交答辩状，提出与有过失的积极抗辩，并就司机的伤害提起过失反诉，要求损害赔偿。
zh-choices.B: 提交答辩状，提出与有过失的积极抗辩，并申请基于诉状的判决。
zh-choices.C: 以缺乏对人管辖权为由申请驳回，因为司机不是B州的公民。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Pleadings

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告收到起诉后，应该在答辩状里写什么，尤其是 affirmative defense（抗辩事由）和 compulsory counterclaim（强制反诉），而不是急着去提驳回动议。

三秒认题路径：

被告收诉状 → 先答辩 → 抗辩能写 → 同事故损失 → 强制反诉

核心法律规则

answer（答辩状）：考场意思是，被告通常不能只站着不管，必须先回应原告起诉。答辩里要写 admissions / denials（承认或否认）、没放弃的 motions（动议）、 affirmative defenses（抗辩事由），还有必须并入的 compulsory counterclaims（强制反诉）。

这里的 contributory negligence（共同过失）是典型抗辩：意思是就算原告把撞车事实讲清楚，被告也可以说“你自己也有错，所以我少赔或不赔”。

同一场事故里，被告自己的受伤索赔属于 same transaction or occurrence（同一交易或事件），而且不需要拉进新当事人，所以要并入答辩一起提。

核心判例： 这里不靠判例名，直接按 Fed. R. Civ. P. 8(c) 和 13(a) 走：先写抗辩，再把同一事故里的反诉一并提出。

思维导图

1. 先判断程序姿态
原告已经起诉，被告要先答辩（answer），不是先跑去说自己不是州民。
2. 必写的答辩内容
答辩里要放承认/否认、没放弃的动议、抗辩事由。
3. 本题的抗辩
司机说行人illegal crossing，这就是共同过失抗辩。
4. 本题的强制反诉
司机自己受伤也来自same accident，所以要并入反诉。
5. 不能被带偏的点
不要被foreign citizen、州籍差异这些词吓到，程序问题先看答辩义务。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：司机不是 State B 公民，或者双方都说对方有责任，那是不是该先动议驳回。

但考试真正问的是：被告现在最该做的，是不是先把 affirmative defense（抗辩事由）和 compulsory counterclaim（强制反诉）写进 answer（答辩状）里。

这题看的是“先在程序上怎么回应”，不是“谁在事故里更可怜”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干已给出same accident，司机应在answer（答辩状）里写共同过失抗辩，并把自己受伤的反诉一并提出。

❌ 法律适用 | 终局救济误判

✕ B: 把 judgment on the pleadings 当成首选，但双方事实正吵着呢。

❌ 事实误判 | 州籍偷换

✕ C: 把 not a citizen 误当成没管辖，个人管辖看的是在州内开车的联系。

❌ 概念混淆 | 国籍规则误读

✕ D: 看到 foreign citizen 就慌，但多元管辖看的是金额和居留状态，不是美国国籍。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看被告是否必须答辩，再把“抗辩 + 同事故反诉”一起装进答辩状。

考场速记

记住这句：答辩先行，抗辩必写；同一事故，强制反诉一起提。看到被告受诉后，先想 answer → defenses → compulsory counterclaim，不要先被“动议驳回”带跑。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A purchaser of a luxury car sued the car's manufacturer in a state court in State A. The purchaser claimed that the steering wheel was defective and caused a car accident resulting in over $300,000 in damages. Before the manufacturer responded, the purchaser filed a notice of dismissal.
Two weeks later, the purchaser filed a complaint in a federal court in State B against the manufacturer for the same claim. The manufacturer filed an answer that included a motion to dismiss for lack of venue. The purchaser did not oppose this motion, but she did file a stipulation of dismissal signed by both parties.
One month later, the purchaser filed a complaint in a federal court in State C alleging the same claim asserted in the prior actions. The manufacturer moved to dismiss the suit, arguing that the purchaser was precluded from bringing this suit a third time.
Will the court likely grant the manufacturer's motion to dismiss?

choices.A: No, because a voluntary dismissal is with prejudice only when specified in a court order.
choices.B: No, because the second action was dismissed by a stipulation signed by both parties.
choices.C: Yes, because the purchaser failed to obtain a court order to dismiss the second action.
choices.D: Yes, because the second dismissal occurred in federal court.

questions.explanation:
Two-dismissal rule on voluntary dismissals
First action
Voluntary dismissal
without court order
Second action
on same claim
Voluntary dismissal by
court order or stipulation
Rule does NOT apply(π can refile)
Notice of voluntary
dismissal
Rule applies(π cannot refile)
Voluntary dismissal
with court order
Second action
on same claim
Rule does NOT apply(π can refile)

A plaintiff may voluntarily dismiss a suit for any reason. A voluntary dismissal is generally without prejudice, which allows the plaintiff to sue the defendant again on the same claim. But a voluntary dismissal is with prejudice and operates as an adjudication on the merits when specified in a court order, notice, or stipulation OR the two-dismissal rule applies ((Choice A)). This rule applies when:

  • the plaintiff's first action was voluntarily dismissed without a court order in state or federal court and
  • the plaintiff brought a second action on the same claim in federal court and filed a notice of voluntary dismissal.*

Here, the purchaser dismissed the first action by a notice of dismissal and then dismissed the second action asserting the same claim by a stipulation in federal court. However, the second dismissal did not operate as an adjudication on the merits because it was dismissed by the parties' signed stipulation—not a notice of voluntary dismissal. Therefore, the two-dismissal rule does not apply, and the court will likely deny the manufacturer's motion to dismiss the purchaser's third action.

*The two-dismissal rule's purpose is to prevent the plaintiff from harassing the defendant by perpetually filing and dismissing the same claim. Since a court order or stipulation does not pose this risk, the rule does not apply when the second action is dismissed by these methods.

(Choice C) A voluntary dismissal without a court order is permitted when the plaintiff files (1) a notice of dismissal before the defendant serves an answer or a summary judgment motion or (2) a stipulation of dismissal that has been signed by all parties (as seen here).

(Choice D) The two-dismissal rule requires that the second dismissal occur in federal court and be pursuant to a notice of voluntary dismissal. But here, the second dismissal was pursuant to the parties' signed stipulation, so this rule does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the two-dismissal rule, a voluntary dismissal operates as an adjudication on the merits when the plaintiff (1) voluntarily dismissed an action in federal or state court without a court order and (2) filed a notice of voluntary dismissal in a second action on the same claim in federal court.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 41(a) (voluntary dismissals).
  • 24 Am. Jur. 2d Dismissal, Discontinuance, and Nonsuit § 95 (2019) (explaining that the two-dismissal rule does not apply when the second action was dismissed by the parties' stipulation).
questions.zh-question:
一辆豪车的购买者在A州的州法院起诉了该车的制造商。购买者声称方向盘有缺陷，导致了一起车祸，造成超过30万美元的损失。在制造商回应之前，购买者提交了一份撤诉通知 (notice of dismissal)。
两周后，购买者在B州的联邦法院对制造商提起了相同的诉讼。制造商提交了答辩状 (answer)，其中包括一份以管辖地不当 (lack of venue) 为由的驳回动议 (motion to dismiss)。购买者没有反对该动议，但她提交了一份由双方签署的撤诉协议 (stipulation of dismissal)。
一个月后，购买者在C州的联邦法院提起了诉讼，主张与先前诉讼中相同的请求。制造商提出驳回诉讼的动议 (motion to dismiss)，理由是购买者被禁止第三次提起此诉讼。
法院是否可能批准制造商的驳回动议？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为自愿撤诉 (voluntary dismissal) 只有在法院命令中明确规定时才具有 with prejudice 的效力。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为第二次诉讼是通过双方签署的撤诉协议 (stipulation) 驳回的。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为购买者未能获得法院命令来驳回第二次诉讼。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为第二次撤诉发生在联邦法院。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Adjudication without trial

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：二次自愿撤诉规则（two-dismissal rule）里，第二次撤诉是不是必须是 notice of voluntary dismissal，以及 stipulation 会不会触发“有偏见驳回”。

三秒认题路径：

第一次无命令撤诉 → 第二次同一请求 → 看第二次方式 → 只看 notice 还是 stipulation → 结论：可否再起诉

核心法律规则

自愿撤诉（voluntary dismissal）一般是 without prejudice，所以原告通常还能就同一请求再起诉。二次自愿撤诉规则（two-dismissal rule）会把第二次撤诉变成“按实体裁判”，但前提是：第一次是在无法院命令下撤诉，第二次又是在联邦法院用 notice of voluntary dismissal 撤诉。

如果第二次是靠双方签字的 stipulation of dismissal，考试上就不算这条规则要打击的那种“反复点火又撤火”，所以不会自动变成有偏见驳回。换句话说，stipulation 会把二次撤诉从规则触发点里拿出去。

核心判例： 无须记具体判例名——本题按 Fed. R. Civ. P. 41(a) 直接判断：第二次如果不是 notice，二次撤诉规则通常不启动。

思维导图

先问：第一次是不是 without court order 的自愿撤诉？
是 进入第二次同一请求的检查。
再问：第二次是不是 notice of voluntary dismissal？
是 两次撤诉规则启动 → 可能按实体处理 → 不能再刷第三次
否 这里最关键：如果是 stipulation 或 court order，规则通常不启动。
本题落点：第二次是双方签字的 stipulation of dismissal，不是 notice。
结论 制造不了“二次 notice” → 被告想拦第三次，拦不住 → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：第二次都已经在联邦法院撤掉了，而且原告还反复起诉，应该直接触发二次撤诉规则。

但考试真正问的是：第二次到底是不是 notice of voluntary dismissal；这里是双方签字的 stipulation，所以规则没被点燃。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干关键事实是第二次撤诉靠双方签字的 stipulation of dismissal，不是 notice，所以二次撤诉规则不启动，原告还能继续起诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“有偏见”只看成 court order 才会发生，漏掉了二次撤诉规则也能触发。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间条件误判

✕ C: 误把“没拿到法院命令”当成致命点，但本题的致命点是第二次不是 notice。

❌ 事实误判 | 联邦地点偷换

✕ D: 只盯着“第二次在联邦法院”就下结论，漏看了撤诉方式其实是 signed stipulation。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定第一次撤诉方式，再专看第二次是不是 notice，别被“反复起诉”故事线带跑。

考场速记

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A pharmaceutical company sued its competitor for patent infringement in federal court. The competitor's attorney hired a pharmacist to examine the case and testify as an expert at trial. The pharmacist studied the case and submitted an initial draft of her report to the attorney. After reading the draft report, the attorney noticed that certain facts and data were missing. To correct this issue, the attorney emailed the pharmacist and provided additional facts and data to include in the report. The pharmacist then revised her report based on this additional information.
After receiving this revised report from the competitor's attorney, the pharmaceutical company served a request for production on the attorney to produce the email exchanged with the pharmacist.
Must the attorney produce the email?

choices.A: No, because attorney communications with expert witnesses are privileged.
choices.B: No, because the contents of the email are discoverable through interrogatories served on the pharmacist.
choices.C: Yes, because a draft of an expert report is discoverable.
choices.D: Yes, because the email contained facts and data that the pharmacist relied on to revise her report.

questions.explanation:
Discovery of expert materials
(FRCP 26(b)(4))
Nontestifying
expert
  • Facts known or opinions held by expert not discoverable unless:
    • relate to court-ordered physical/mental examination or
    • exceptional circumstances make it impracticable to obtain information by other means
Testifying
expert
  • Facts known & opinions held by expert discoverable through deposition
  • Drafts of expert reports & disclosures not discoverable
  • Communications between attorney & expert not discoverable unless:
    • relate to expert's compensation or
    • identify facts, data, or assumptions provided by attorney that expert considered in forming opinions
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

Parties can use various discovery methods, including requests for production, to obtain nonprivileged information that is relevant to any claim or defense and proportional to the needs of the case. Materials held by an expert witness expected to testify at trial are discoverable with two exceptions:

  • Drafts of expert reports or disclosures
  • Privileged attorney-expert communications

All attorney-expert communications are privileged unless they (1) relate to the expert's compensation or (2) identify facts, data, or assumptions provided by the attorney that the expert considered or relied on in forming his/her opinions.

Here, the competitor's attorney hired the pharmacist to examine the case and testify as an expert at trial. After reading the pharmacist's draft report, the attorney emailed the pharmacist and provided her with additional facts and data that were missing in the draft. The pharmacist then relied on those facts and data to revise her report, so the email is not a privileged communication (Choice A). Therefore, the attorney must produce the email.

(Choice B) Interrogatories are a discovery request in which a party serves written questions on another party that inquire about any matter within the scope of discovery. However, interrogatories may not be served on a nonparty such as an expert expected to testify at trial. Therefore, the contents of the email are not discoverable through interrogatories served on the nonparty pharmacist.

(Choice C) Drafts of expert reports are not discoverable. Therefore, the attorney would not be required to produce the email on this basis.

📌 Educational Objective

All attorney-expert communications are privileged unless they (1) relate to the expert's compensation or (2) identify facts, data, or assumptions provided by the attorney that the expert considered or relied on in forming his/her opinions.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(4) (discovery of expert materials).

主题：民事诉讼 — 审前程序

一家制药公司在联邦法院起诉其竞争对手专利侵权。竞争对手的律师聘请了一名药剂师审查该案件，并作为专家证人在庭审中作证。该药剂师研究了案件，并向律师提交了报告的初稿。阅读初稿后，律师注意到某些事实和数据缺失。为解决此问题，律师通过电子邮件联系了药剂师，并提供了额外的、需要纳入报告的事实和数据。药剂师随后根据这些额外信息修改了她的报告。
在收到竞争对手律师的这份修改后的报告后，制药公司向该律师送达了一份要求制作（request for production）的请求，要求其出示与药剂师交换的电子邮件。
律师必须出示该电子邮件吗？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为律师与专家证人之间的沟通享有特权（privileged）。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为电子邮件的内容可以通过向药剂师送达书面质询（interrogatories）来获取（discoverable）。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为专家报告的草稿是可获取的（discoverable）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该电子邮件包含了药剂师修改报告所依据的事实和数据。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery of expert materials

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：试验性专家（testifying expert）的律师邮件里，只要装了专家形成意见时考虑过的 facts/data，通常就要交。

三秒认题路径：

专家要出庭 → 律师发邮件 → 填 facts/data → 例外命中 → 要交

核心法律规则

对出庭专家（testifying expert），其掌握的事实和意见可以通过取证拿到，但专家报告草稿（drafts of expert reports）和大多数律师-专家沟通（attorney-expert communications）默认不公开。

考试只盯两个例外：一是报酬（compensation），二是律师提供的 facts、data、assumptions 被专家拿去形成或修改意见。若邮件正好塞了这些材料，保护就被打破。

核心判例： FRCP 26(b)(4) — 这条规则锁定：本题邮件因为传了专家修改报告时依赖的 facts/data，所以要生产。

思维导图

收到的是律师发给出庭专家的邮件吗？
是 先看对象：testifying expert，不是普通证人，也不是随便的内部沟通。
默认 attorney-expert communications 通常受保护，drafts 也通常不公开。
但这里 邮件里给了专家缺失的 facts and data，而专家后来拿去改报告。
卡死点：这不再是“纯保密沟通”，而是落进 FRCP 26(b)(4) 的例外。
结论 邮件要生产，答案选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是律师和专家之间的邮件，那就天然保密，或者只要最后没有把报告草稿交出去就没事。

但考试真正问的是：这封邮件是不是把律师提供的 facts/data 送进了专家脑子里，而且专家确实靠它改了意见。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 email 里给了专家缺失的 facts/data，且专家就是靠它修订报告，所以落进例外，要生产。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 privileged 当成绝对保护，忽略了专家沟通的法定例外。

❌ 事实误判 | 非当事人偷换

✕ B: 想用询问书绕到非当事人专家身上，但题目问的是邮件，不是对 pharmacist 发 interrogatories。

❌ 法律适用 | 草稿规则错套

✕ C: 看到 draft 就以为一切都免交，可本题争点是邮件里的 facts/data，不是草稿本身。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“出庭专家 + 律师传 facts/data + 专家实际依赖”这三连，再看 privilege 例外有没有被打穿。

考场速记

记忆口诀：律师-专家邮件默认保密，但一旦给了专家形成意见的 facts/data，就要交。

顺手记住：drafts of expert reports 不公开；compensation 和 facts/data/assumptions 是两大破口。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A pharmaceutical retailer sued a drug manufacturer in federal court for antitrust and unfair-competition violations under federal and state law. After the parties completed discovery, the retailer submitted a pretrial narrative statement designating a broad set of facts and issues to be tried. The manufacturer disputed the statement and submitted a much narrower one. At the final pretrial conference, the court entered its final order, ruling in favor of the retailer's broader statement as the one the court would read to the jury during voir dire and would use to define the facts and issues to be tried.
The manufacturer's attorney is concerned that trying many of the facts and issues listed in the pretrial order would reveal litigation strategies important in other actions pending against the manufacturer.
What is the best way for the manufacturer's attorney to seek relief from the court's ruling on the pretrial statement?

choices.A: Appeal from the final pretrial order, arguing that it is overbroad on its face.
choices.B: Object in the trial court and appeal any adverse ruling on the objection.
choices.C: Object in the trial court and file a motion to delay the trial.
choices.D: Object in the trial court and move to modify the order to prevent manifest injustice.

questions.explanation:
A federal district court judge may hold one or more pretrial conferences with the parties' attorneys or unrepresented parties. At these conferences, the judge has broad discretion to address and act on a wide range of issues to help expedite litigation, improve the trial's quality, and facilitate settlement. At the final pretrial conference, the judge will enter a final pretrial order that formulates a plan for trial.* The court may modify this order only to prevent manifest injustice.

Here, the federal district court entered its final order at the final pretrial conference. In that order, the court adopted the retailer's broad narrative statement to use during voir dire and to define the facts and issues to be tried. Since the manufacturer's attorney wants to narrow this narrative statement, the best way to seek relief is to object in the trial court and move to modify the order to prevent manifest injustice.

*A final pretrial conference must be held as close to the start of trial as is reasonable and must be attended by at least one attorney who will conduct the trial for each party or by any unrepresented party.

(Choice A) Under the final-judgment rule, an appeal cannot be taken before a final judgment has been entered unless limited exceptions apply. A final pretrial order is not a final judgment and none of the exceptions apply, so an immediate appeal is unjustified.

(Choice B) The manufacturer's attorney must move to modify the order at the trial court level to preserve the issue for appeal, where the order will be reviewed for abuse of discretion. A mere objection will not suffice.

(Choice C) A motion to delay the trial will not help the manufacturer's attorney seek relief from the final pretrial order. Instead, the attorney should move to modify the order to prevent manifest injustice.

📌 Educational Objective

At the final pretrial conference, a federal district court judge will issue a final pretrial order that formulates a plan for trial. The court may modify this order only to prevent manifest injustice.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(e) (final pretrial conference and orders).
  • 6A Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 1527.1 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining how a party can modify or seek relief from a pretrial order).
questions.zh-question:
一家药品零售商根据联邦和州法律，在联邦法院就反垄断和不正当竞争行为起诉了一家药品制造商。在双方当事人完成证据开示程序后，零售商提交了一份审前叙述性陈述，其中指定了待审理的一系列广泛的事实和争议点。制造商对该陈述提出异议，并提交了一份范围窄得多的陈述。在最终审前会议上，法院作出了最终命令，裁定采纳零售商范围更广的陈述，作为法院将在陪审员遴选程序中向陪审团宣读，并用以界定待审理事实和争议点的版本。

制造商的律师担心，审理审前命令中列出的许多事实和争议点，会泄露在该制造商面临的其他未决诉讼中至关重要的诉讼策略。

制造商的律师就法院关于审前陈述的裁决寻求救济的最佳方式是什么？

zh-choices.A: 对最终审前命令提起上诉，主张其内容明显过于宽泛。
zh-choices.B: 在初审法院提出异议，并对任何关于该异议的不利裁决提起上诉。
zh-choices.C: 在初审法院提出异议，并申请动议推迟审判。
zh-choices.D: 在初审法院提出异议，并申请动议修改该命令，以防止出现明显的非正义。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Case management

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：最终审前命令（final pretrial order）能不能立刻上诉；答案是不能，正确动作是先在原审法院提异议，再申请修改。

三秒认题路径：

final pretrial order → 先看能否上诉 → 不是终局判决 → 走原审法院修改 → 防止 manifest injustice

核心法律规则

最终审前命令（final pretrial order）是法官在final pretrial conference后用来安排审判的命令，考试意思：它不是终局判决，所以通常不能直接上诉。

如果当事人觉得命令写太宽，正确做法是先在trial court里object，再move to modify，而且修改门槛是prevent manifest injustice，考试意思：要让法官改，不是先冲去上诉法院。

联邦民事诉讼规则 16(e)（Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(e)）把这个门槛锁得很死：终局审前命令只有在防止明显不公时才可修改。

核心判例：题目依托 Rule 16(e) 的常规考法——最终审前命令只可为防止明显不公而修改，因此先在原审法院申请修改，而不是直接上诉。

思维导图

看到的是 final pretrial order，先问：它是终局判决吗？
NO不能立刻按一般上诉走。
再问：有没有法定中间上诉例外？
NO题干没有 injunction、certification 或其他特别例外。
最后看 collateral-order doctrine：
① 重要问题？有。
② 与案外问题分离？大体可以。
③ effectively unreviewable？卡死在这里：终审后仍可救济，所以不能马上上诉。
结论：先去原审法院 object + move to modify → 选 D。
一句话记：pretrial order 先别想上诉，先想“能不能让本院改”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：litigation strategies 一旦泄露就回不来了，所以应该马上上诉。

但考试真正问的是：这份命令在法律程序上能不能事后救回来，不是你感觉它会不会造成麻烦。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干是final pretrial order，规则只允许在原审法院申请修改以防止明显不公；先异议再move to modify才是正路。

❌ 法律适用 | 终局上诉误判

✕ A: 把final pretrial order当成可直接上诉的终局判决了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只异议不修改

✕ B: 只object 还不够，没把修改请求送进原审法院。

❌ 事实误判 | 拖延策略偷换

✕ C: delay the trial 只是拖时间，不是修正审前命令。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先分清是不是终局，再找原审法院可用的修改路径。

考场速记

记住一句：审前命令先看能不能改，不先看能不能上诉。 需要上诉例外时，再想口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”，对应 injunction、certification、class action 等法定中间上诉例外。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A manufacturer sued its competitor in federal district court for allegedly violating the manufacturer's patent. The competitor filed an answer that claimed the patent was invalid and asserted a counterclaim for damages. During a bench trial, the competitor presented overwhelming evidence showing that the manufacturer's chief executive officer (CEO) had used deceptive methods to obtain the patent. At the close of evidence, the judge issued findings of fact and conclusions of law, and the court entered judgment in favor of the competitor.
The competitor was worried that the manufacturer would declare bankruptcy and be unable to pay the judgment, so the competitor moved to amend its counterclaim to add the manufacturer's CEO as a party. It also requested that the court alter the judgment to require the CEO to pay the judgment in the event the manufacturer files for bankruptcy. The district court immediately granted the competitor's motion, and the CEO appealed.
The applicable statute of limitations governing the competitor's counterclaim has yet to expire.
Is the appellate court likely to affirm the district court's action?

choices.A: No, because the district court violated the CEO's due process rights by not allowing him to respond to the counterclaim.
choices.B: No, because the manufacturer did not consent in writing to the competitor's amendment.
choices.C: Yes, because the applicable statute of limitations for the competitor's counterclaim against the CEO has not expired.
choices.D: Yes, because the CEO should have been aware of the pending lawsuit.

Amend once as matter of course
Amend to add issues tried by consent
Amend with opposing party’s consent or court’s permission

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure

Under FRCP 15, a party may amend his/her pleading (eg, counterclaim) with the opposing party's written consent or the court's permission before, during, or after trial. The court's permission should be freely granted when justice so requires and the amendment will not violate due process. In Nelson v. Adams USA, Inc., the Supreme Court held that a court violates due process when it allows a new party to be added in an amended pleading but does not permit the new party to respond.*

Here, the district court permitted the competitor to amend its counterclaim to add the manufacturer's CEO as a party. The court then violated the CEO's due process rights by not giving him an opportunity to respond before altering the judgment to hold him personally liable in the event the manufacturer declares bankruptcy. Therefore, the appellate court will likely reverse and remand to give the CEO an opportunity to respond.

*Under FRCP 15(a), a new party may respond within the time remaining to respond to the original pleading or within 14 days after being served with the amended pleading—whichever is later.

(Choice B) The manufacturer did not need to consent in writing to the competitor's amendment. That is because a federal court can permit amendments to pleadings without the opposing party's consent and should do so when justice requires—so long as the amendment complies with due process (not seen here).

(Choice C) Although the applicable statute of limitations has not expired, the court violated the CEO's due process rights by amending the counterclaim and altering the judgment without allowing him a chance to respond.

(Choice D) The fact that the CEO should have been aware of the pending lawsuit does not change the due process requirement that he be given an opportunity to respond to the competitor's amended counterclaim.

📌 Educational Objective

A court should freely allow parties to amend their pleadings when justice so requires and due process will not be violated. When a court grants a party's motion to amend a pleading to add a new party, due process requires that the new party be given an opportunity to respond.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(b) (amending pleadings during and after trial).
  • Nelson v. Adams USA, Inc., 529 U.S. 460, 465–67 (2000) (explaining that due process requires that a new party be given an opportunity to respond to an amended pleading).

一家制造商在联邦地区法院起诉其竞争对手，指控其侵犯了该制造商的专利。竞争对手提交了答辩状，声称该专利无效，并提出了损害赔偿的反诉。在一次法官审理中，竞争对手出示了压倒性的证据，证明制造商的首席执行官（CEO）使用了欺骗性手段来获取该专利。在证据出示阶段结束时，法官发布了事实认定和法律结论，法院作出了有利于竞争对手的判决。

竞争对手担心制造商会宣布破产而无法支付判决款项，因此，竞争对手动议修改其反诉，将制造商的CEO增列为当事人。它还请求法院变更判决，要求在制造商申请破产的情况下，由CEO支付判决款项。地区法院立即批准了竞争对手的动议，CEO提起了上诉。

管辖竞争对手反诉的适用诉讼时效尚未届满。

上诉法院是否可能维持地区法院的行为？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为诉状在审判后不得修改。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为地区法院侵犯了CEO的正当程序权利。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为适用的诉讼时效尚未届满。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为CEO理应知晓该未决诉讼。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Pleadings

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：FRCP 15 允许改诉状，但把新当事人加进来后，法院不能立刻改判让他承担责任，必须先给他回应机会。

三秒认题路径：

改诉状 → 加新人 → 先回应 → 才能判责 → 不然撤回

核心法律规则

联邦民诉规则 15（FRCP 15） 的意思是：法院通常可以在起诉前后、甚至审理中放行修改诉状，法院许可（court's permission） 考场意思：法官可以同意改，但不是想怎么改都行。

真正卡点是正当程序（due process）：如果修改后的诉状把一个新的人拉进来，这个人必须先有机会答辩、回应、抗辩，不能被直接判成要赔钱的人。

所以这题里，问题不是“能不能改”，而是“改完以后能不能马上把 CEO 绑进判决里”。答案是不能。

核心判例： Nelson v. Adams USA, Inc. — 法院允许把新当事人加进来后，若不给他回应机会就直接让他担责，违反正当程序。

思维导图

先看：法院是在“改诉状加人”，还是在“直接判新人的责任”？
这题事实： 竞对申请把 CEO 加进反诉，并要求以后若公司破产就让 CEO 先扛。
规则关卡： 新当事人必须先能回应，否则 due process 过不去。
关键误区： 不是看 statute of limitations 还没过，也不是看他“应该知道有官司”。
结论： 直接改判让 CEO 承担个人责任 → 撤。
考试上看到：new party + no opportunity to respond → 选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然 CEO 明显参与了事实争议，法院又只是“补上他”，那应该可以直接把责任压上去。

但考试真正问的是：把一个新当事人加进去后，程序上有没有先让他答辩的机会。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 把 CEO 加为新当事人后立即改判其个人责任，却没给他回应机会，正好踩中 due process 红线。

❌ 法律适用 | 写成书面同意

✕ B: 把 written consent 当成必需条件了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 期限决定胜负

✕ C: 盯着 statute of limitations，却没看到真正致命的是没让 CEO 回应。

❌ 事实误判 | 知情替代答辩

✕ D: “应该知道”不等于有 opportunity to respond。

这题建议用什么方法？

先问“有没有把新当事人拉进来”，再问“有没有先给他回应机会”，最后才看别的背景事实。

考场速记

记住：FRCP 15 允许改诉状，但新增当事人后必须先能答辩；Nelson 这类题，抓住“新人先回应”就够了。

口诀：“先加人，后让说；没让说，判决撤。”

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A woman from State A contracted with a builder from State B to construct her new home in State A for $500,000. The builder ordered all the necessary materials, including drywall, and built the home to the woman's specifications.
After one year, the drywall throughout the home began to crumble and give off an awful odor. The home became uninhabitable. The woman sued the builder for breach of contract in a federal district court in State A. The builder believes that the drywall supplier from State B should reimburse him for any damages he may owe the woman. The builder has yet to file his answer.
What is the most efficient action the builder can take to seek reimbursement from the supplier?

choices.A: File a crossclaim against the supplier.
choices.B: File a motion to join the supplier as an indispensable party.
choices.C: File a separate lawsuit against the supplier.
choices.D: File a third-party complaint against the supplier.

questions.explanation:
Ways to add parties
Required joinder Requires addition of necessary party to suit
Permissive joinder Allows addition of nonessential party to suit
Intervention Allows nonparty whose interests may be affected to join suit
Impleader Allows defendant to add nonparty who may be liable to defendant for all or part of asserted claim to suit
Interpleader Allows possessor of property to force persons who claim ownership of property to resolve dispute in single suit
Class action Allows party to represent interests of entire class of similarly situated individuals

Impleader (ie, third-party practice) allows a defendant to add a nonparty to a suit who may be liable to the defendant for all or part of the plaintiff's claim. This means that the nonparty would reimburse the defendant for any damages paid to the plaintiff. To initiate impleader, the defendant can file a third-party complaint (1) within 14 days of serving his/her original answer or (2) after this deadline with the court's permission.

Here, impleader is appropriate since the builder (defendant) believes that the supplier (nonparty) should reimburse the builder for any damages he may owe the woman (plaintiff) in the pending suit. Since the builder has not yet filed an answer, the court's permission is not required. Therefore, the most efficient way for the builder to seek reimbursement is to file a third-party complaint against the supplier.

(Choice A) A crossclaim is a claim for relief asserted against a coparty—eg, a defendant against a codefendant. But here, the builder seeks relief from the supplier—a nonparty. As a result, the builder cannot file a crossclaim to obtain relief from the supplier.

(Choice B) The supplier is not an indispensable party and should not be joined as such. That is because the supplier's absence will not (1) prevent the existing parties from obtaining complete relief, (2) prejudice the supplier's interest, or (3) subject an existing party to multiple or inconsistent obligations.

(Choice C) The builder could file a separate lawsuit against the supplier. But since this would be more costly and time-consuming than filing a third-party complaint in the pending action, it is not the most efficient way for the builder to seek reimbursement.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant may add a nonparty to a suit by filing a third-party complaint alleging that the nonparty is liable to the defendant for all or part of the plaintiff's claim. The defendant need only obtain the court's leave if more than 14 days have passed since the defendant served his/her original answer.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 14 (third-party practice).

建筑商可以采取何种最有效的行动来向供应商寻求补偿？

zh-choices.A: 提出动议，请求法院许可追加供应商为第三方被告。
zh-choices.B: 提出动议，将供应商作为不可或缺的当事人追加进来。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告想让“可能对自己负担分担或补偿责任”的非当事人（nonparty）进来，最省事的动作是不是第三方诉讼请求（third-party complaint / impleader）。

三秒认题路径：

被告要追偿 → 找非当事人 → 可能赔自己 → 答案未交 → 第三方诉讼请求

核心法律规则

第三方诉讼（impleader）就是被告把一个非当事人（nonparty）拉进来，主张这个人要对原告的请求全部或部分替被告买单，所以考场上你要找的是“谁该赔被告”，不是“谁跟原告同一锅”。

被告在送达自己的原始答辩（original answer）后14天内可以直接递交第三方诉状（third-party complaint）；超过14天才需要法院许可。题干说 builder 还没交 answer，所以直接起诉供应商就行。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 14 — 规则本身就锁死结论：被告要追偿非当事人，最合适的是 third-party complaint。

思维导图

被告想把供应商拉进来，目的是什么？
看关系：供应商不是共同被告，而是非当事人。
看责任方向：被告说“如果我赔原告，你要替我赔我”——这是第三方诉讼（impleader）。
时间门槛：answer 还没交 → 14天规则未触发，不用先拿法院许可。
结论落点：最省步骤 = 直接提third-party complaint。
答案：选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然被告和供应商有争议，就随便拉一个“相关人”进来。

但考试真正问的是：这个人是不是会对被告负责，也就是能不能让被告把原告这笔账转回去。

别把“想追偿”误看成“必须和原告同案共被告”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干builder 想让 drywall supplier reimbuse him，这正是被告向非当事人追偿的第三方诉状（third-party complaint）场景，而且他还没交 answer，连许可都不用先要。

❌ 概念混淆 | 同案对象误判

✕ A: 把crossclaim拿来错认成对非当事人求偿。

❌ 事实误判 | 必要当事人偷换

✕ B: 供应商不是必须拉进来的indispensable party。

❌ 法律适用 | 另案处理误导

✕ C: 当然能另案起诉，但这不是最省步骤的seek reimbursement方式。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看被告要不要追偿非当事人，再用 answer 是否已提交判断能否直接 implead。

考场速记

记住一句：被告要找“会赔自己的人”，先想 impleader / third-party complaint，再看 14 天答辩窗口。
口诀：“先问是不是非当事人，再问是不是对被告负担。”

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A tech company sued a software firm in a federal district court for allegedly violating federal antitrust laws.
The tech company employs a developer who regularly provides expert testimony for the company in litigation. The developer is advising the company in its suit against the firm, but the company is not going to call the developer as an expert witness in this case. Instead, the company hired an economist to testify as an expert witness about the economic impact caused by the software firm's anticompetitive behavior.
Whom must the tech company disclose to the software firm at least 90 days before trial without waiting for a discovery request?

choices.A: Neither the economist nor the developer.
choices.B: Only the economist.
choices.C: Only the developer.
choices.D: Both the economist and the developer.

questions.explanation:
Required discovery disclosures
(FRCP 26(a))
Type Required disclosures Time to disclose
Initial
disclosures*		 • Persons with relevant information
• Items in party's possession that support claim/defense
• Computation of damages & supporting material
• Relevant insurance policies 		• ≤ 14 days after initial planning conference
• ≤ 30 days after post-conference service or joinder
• As court orders or parties stipulate
Expert
testimony		 • Identity of expert witnesses
• Expert's written report
• If no report, subject matter & summary of testimony 		• ≥ 90 days before trial
• ≤ 30 days after disclosure to rebut evidence
• As court orders or parties stipulate
Pretrial
disclosures*		 • Testifying witnesses
• Deposition testimony to be used at trial
• Documents/exhibits to be used at trial 		• ≥ 30 days before trial
• As court orders

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

*Does not apply to evidence used solely for impeachment.

Parties must disclose certain information during discovery to facilitate litigation. Most of this information is disclosed in response to an opposing party's discovery requests. But three types of disclosures are required without such requests: initial disclosures, pretrial disclosures, and disclosure of expert witness testimony. This requires that the parties disclose the identity of all expert witnesses expected to testify at trial AND provide either:

  • a written report for any witness who was specially hired to provide expert testimony or who regularly gives expert testimony as part of his/her employment duties with the party or
  • a summary of the subject matter, facts, and opinions of the testimony for all other expert witnesses (eg, treating physicians).

A party must disclose this information at least 90 days before trial unless otherwise ordered by the court or stipulated by the parties.*

Here, the tech company hired the economist to testify at trial as an expert witness about the economic impact of the software firm's anticompetitive behavior. As a result, the company must disclose the economist's identity at least 90 days before trial without waiting for a discovery request (Choices A & C). A written report must also be included since the economist was specially hired to provide this expert testimony.

Since the developer regularly gives expert testimony as part of her employment with the tech company, she also would have needed to provide a written report if she was going to testify in this case. However, the developer is only advising the company and is not going to testify. Therefore, the company does not need to disclose the developer's identity (Choices C & D).

*If a party intends to rebut an opposing party's expert witness, expert witness disclosure is required within 30 days after the opposing party discloses its expert witness information.

📌 Educational Objective

A party must disclose the identity of an expert witness expected to testify at trial and provide a written report or summary to the opposing party at least 90 days before trial.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(2) (required disclosure of expert witnesses).
questions.zh-question:
一家科技公司在联邦地区法院起诉一家软件公司，指控其违反了联邦反垄断法。

该科技公司雇佣了一名开发人员，该开发人员在诉讼中定期为公司提供专家证言。该开发人员正在就公司对软件公司的诉讼提供咨询，但公司不打算在本案中传唤该开发人员作为专家证人。相反，该公司聘请了一名经济学家作为专家证人，就软件公司的反竞争行为造成的经济影响作证。

在无需等待证据开示请求的情况下，该科技公司必须在审判前至少90天向软件公司披露哪一位人员？

zh-choices.A: 经济学家和开发人员都不需要。
zh-choices.B: 仅经济学家。
zh-choices.C: 仅开发人员。
zh-choices.D: 经济学家和开发人员都需要。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Mandatory disclosures

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：专家证人（expert witness）在开庭前 90 天的强制披露，和“只是咨询但不上庭”的人要不要一起披露。

三秒认题路径：

专家要上庭 → 90天前 → 披露身份 → 要报告 → 不上庭不用报

核心法律规则

专家证人披露（expert disclosure）的规则很直接：只要这个人是预计要在审判中作证的专家，就要在 审判前至少90天（at least 90 days before trial） 披露其身份。

如果该专家是被专门聘请来出意见，或者本来就经常以专家身份出庭，还要交 书面报告（written report）；如果只是咨询、但不会作证，就不触发这项强制披露。

核心判例： 本题按 FRCP 26(a)(2) 的披露结构直接判断，不需要额外判例扩张；关键是“预计要作证”这条线。

思维导图

先看这个人会不会在审判中作证？
会→ 属 专家证人（expert witness），要披露身份；若属专聘专家，还要书面报告。
结论：至少90天前披露，不等对方要。
不会→ 只是顾问/咨询人，不触发专家披露。
结论：这个人不在必披露名单里。
再问：题干里谁是“要上庭”的专家？
经济学家→ 被专门聘请来讲经济影响，且要在 trial 作证。
开发者→ 只是 advising，不会作证。
最终答案：只披露经济学家，不披露开发者。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：开发者“平时经常当专家”，所以公司是不是也得一起报。

但考试真正问的是：她这次会不会出庭作证。不会作证的人，哪怕有专家身份背景，也不触发这次的强制披露。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 hired an economist to testify，所以必须在审判前至少 90 天披露其身份；他还是专聘专家，故还要书面报告。

❌ 事实误判 | 以为都不上庭

✕ A: 把 Neither 看成“两个都不用报”，但经济学家明明要作证。

❌ 概念混淆 | 把顾问当证人

✕ D: 看到 Both 就想全收，但只有要作证的那位才进披露清单。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“谁会出庭作证”，再看他是普通专家还是专聘专家，最后决定要不要 90 天前披露和书面报告。

考场速记

口诀：先问“会不会作证”，再问“是不是专聘专家”；会作证就披露身份，专聘就再交报告。

记住：FRCP 26(a)(2) 看的是“未来要上庭的人”，不是“后台帮忙的人”。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A buyer from State A and a seller from State B entered into a contract in which the buyer agreed to purchase a parcel of State B land from the seller for $200,000. However, the seller did not disclose to the buyer that the seller co-owned the land with his mother, who is from State A. The seller's mother was never mentioned in the contract, and she never authorized the sale of the land. The buyer paid the seller $200,000 pursuant to the contract but was prevented from taking possession of the land by the seller's mother.
The buyer sued the seller in federal court in State B to obtain possession of the land. The seller has filed a motion to dismiss the buyer's lawsuit for failing to join the seller's mother in the action.
Should the court grant the seller's motion to dismiss the case?

choices.A: No, because although the seller's mother is a required party to the lawsuit, dismissing the case would leave the buyer with no adequate remedy.
choices.B: No, because the seller's mother is not a required party to the lawsuit.
choices.C: Yes, because although the seller's mother is a required party to the lawsuit, joining her in the action would destroy subject-matter jurisdiction.
choices.D: Yes, because although the seller's mother is a required party to the lawsuit, the State B federal court lacks personal jurisdiction over her.

questions.explanation:
Required joinder of parties
(FRCP 19)
Is absent person a required party?
Person's absence will:
  • prevent complete relief to existing parties
  • prejudice absent person’s interest OR
  • result in multiple or inconsistent obligations
Yes ↓
Is joinder feasible?
  • Personal jurisdiction over required party
  • subject-matter jurisdiction preserved AND
  • proper venue remains
No ↓
Is it equitable to proceed without required party?
  • Judgment would impose slight prejudice
  • court can avoid or lessen prejudice
  • judgment would be adequate AND
  • plaintiff has no other adequate remedy
Proceed
with suit
Join
required
party
Proceed
without
required
party
Dismiss suit
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure

Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 19—the required (ie, compulsory) joinder rule—provides a three-step process for determining whether an absent party must be joined in a lawsuit. The first step considers whether the absent party is a required party because:

  • complete relief cannot be granted without that party's presence
  • the party's absence will subject the other parties to a substantial risk of multiple or inconsistent obligations or
  • the party's absence will impair his/her ability to protect an interest related to the lawsuit—as seen here with the seller's mother since she has a co-ownership interest in the land (Choice B).

The second step considers whether it is feasible to join the required party. Joinder is feasible when:

  • the court can obtain personal jurisdiction over the required party
  • subject-matter jurisdiction remains after joinder and
  • proper venue remains.

Here, the court can obtain personal jurisdiction over the seller's mother because the suit arises from her minimum contacts with State B—her ownership of State B land (Choice D). But joining her as a party would destroy subject-matter jurisdiction because she and the buyer are both citizens of State A (no diversity) and the claim arises under state law (no federal question). Therefore, joinder is not feasible.

When joinder is not feasible, the third step considers whether equity allows the action to proceed without the required party or compels a dismissal. Here, dismissal is required—and the seller's motion should be granted—because:

  • a judgment would severely prejudice the mother's interest in the land
  • the court cannot reasonably lessen or avoid this prejudice
  • in the mother's absence, the judgment would be inadequate since she could later sue to enforce her ownership rights and
  • the buyer can pursue an adequate remedy by refiling this action in state court (Choice A).
📌 Educational Objective

If a required party cannot be feasibly joined, the court must decide whether the party is indispensable and the suit should be dismissed or may proceed without them.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 19 (required joinder of parties).

买方向B州的联邦法院起诉卖方，以获得对该土地的占有权。卖方已提出动议，以未将卖方的母亲列为诉讼当事人为由，请求驳回买方的诉讼。

法院是否应批准卖方请求驳回案件的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为卖方的母亲是该诉讼的必要当事人，且B州的联邦法院可以对她行使属人管辖权。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为卖方的母亲并非该诉讼的必要当事人。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为尽管卖方的母亲是该诉讼的必要当事人，但将其列为诉讼当事人并不可行。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为卖方的母亲是该诉讼的必要当事人。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：FRCP 19 必要当事人（required party）能不能因合并后破坏 subject-matter jurisdiction 而必须被法院直接驳回。

三秒认题路径：

少了她不行 → 先看必要性 → 再看能否合并 → 会毁管辖 → 只能驳回

核心法律规则

先问这个缺席人是不是 required party（必要当事人）：如果不加她就不能完整救济、会伤到她自己的利益，或让别人面临重复/矛盾义务，就要继续往下查。

第二步看 joinder feasible（可合并） 不可合并：要同时满足 personal jurisdiction（人身管辖）、subject-matter jurisdiction（标的管辖） 还保得住、proper venue（适当审判地） 仍成立。

如果合并会把联邦管辖弄没了，法院就不能硬拉进来；再看是否能公平地无她继续审，但如果她的产权会被严重伤到，而且原告还有州法院这个路，通常就要 dismiss（驳回）。

核心判例： 无需额外判例；本题直接按 FRCP 19 的三步法判断，关键是“加进去会不会毁掉标的管辖”。

思维导图

1）她是不是必要当事人（required party）？
看三种风险：不能完整救济；伤到她的共有产权；让双方将来互相打架。
本题卡点：母亲是共有权人，不在场就无法把土地处分干净。
2）能不能把她加进来？
先查三件事：人身管辖、标的管辖、venue。
本题卡点：她与买方同属 State A，会把多元管辖打掉。
3）如果一加就毁管辖，法院怎么办？
不能就地补洞，只能看是否公平地继续审。
本题结论：继续审会严重伤到她的土地利益，所以应驳回。
答案走向
正确结论：她是必要当事人，但不可行地加入会毁掉 subject-matter jurisdiction，所以法院应准许驳回。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：母亲没签合同、也没授权，所以先把卖方和买方的合同纠纷判完再说。

但考试真正问的是：她有没有共有产权，少了她能不能把土地争议一次解决；答案是不能。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题最容易被“她没在合同里”骗走，但 Rule 19 看的不是合同署名，而是她有没有会被判决直接碰到的财产利益。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 母亲是土地共有权人，所以她是必要当事人；但一旦把她加进来，双方同属 State A，diversity jurisdiction 会消失，法院只能准许驳回。

❌ 事实误判 | 救济不足偷换

✕ A: 抓住“无其他救济”就放行，但这里先卡在必须把她加进来，不能直接跳到衡平。

❌ 概念混淆 | 必要性漏判

✕ B: 把共有权人当成路人，忽略了她的产权会被判决直接碰到。

❌ 法律适用 | 人身管辖误套

✕ D: 盯着 personal jurisdiction，但本题真正卡住的是加她以后会毁掉联邦管辖。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先判必要当事人，再查能否合并，最后看合并是否会把管辖打没。

考场速记

记住 Rule 19 的顺序：先看是不是必要当事人，再看能不能合并，最后看要不要驳回。

口诀：“先必要，后可并；一并毁管辖，就别硬拉进。”

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant sued in federal court seeks information from a nonparty witness.
Which of the following discovery devices can the defendant use to obtain this information?

choices.A: Interrogatory.
choices.B: Mental exam.
choices.C: Oral deposition.
choices.D: Request for admissions.

questions.explanation:
Methods of discovery
Depositions
  • Written or oral examination of party or witness under oath
  • 10 per side
Interrogatories
  • Written questions served on party
  • Serve up to 25
  • Written responses due within 30 days of service
Request for
production
  • Request served on party (or subpoena served on nonparty) to produce & allow inspection of documents, electronic information, tangible items, or land
  • No limit
  • Written response due within 30 days of service
Requests for
admission
  • Requests served on other party to admit truth of facts within scope of discovery
  • No limit
  • Written response due within 30 days of service
Physical/mental
exams
  • Order by court or parties' agreement for physical or mental examination of party if those conditions are in controversy

Discovery is the pretrial phase of a lawsuit during which the parties can obtain information related to the case from other parties and nonparties through various methods. A deposition is a discovery method in which a party conducts a written or oral examination of a party or nonparty under oath and outside of court. Therefore, the defendant can use an oral deposition to get information from the nonparty witness—and, if necessary, can obtain a subpoena to compel the nonparty's attendance.

(Choice A) Interrogatories are written questions served on another party that may inquire about any matter within the scope of discovery—but they cannot be served on a nonparty.

(Choice B) A court can only order a physical or mental exam of a party by a suitably licensed or certified examiner if that party's physical or mental condition is in controversy.

(Choice D) A request for admissions is a discovery method in which a party requests that another party admit the truth of specified facts within the scope of discovery. But this method cannot be used against a nonparty.

📌 Educational Objective

During discovery, the parties can use various methods to obtain information and evidence concerning the case from other parties and nonparties. A deposition is a discovery method in which a party conducts a written or oral examination of a party or nonparty under oath and outside of court.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 30–31 (depositions).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：取证（discovery）里，想从非当事人（nonparty）拿信息，哪种工具可以用。

三秒认题路径：

非当事人 → 取信息 → 看工具 → 能否对外人用 → 选 deposition

核心法律规则

口头证言询问（oral deposition）考场意思：可以对party或nonparty做书面或口头询问，而且是在庭外、宣誓下进行。

询问书（interrogatories）考场意思：只能发给party，不能直接问非当事人。

承认请求（request for admissions）考场意思：也是只对另一方当事人用，不是拿来问外人的。

核心规则： Fed. R. Civ. P. 30–31 — depositions 可以问 party 也可以问 nonparty，所以这题选它。

思维导图

题干先问：要从 nonparty witness 拿信息，哪种发现工具能直接用？
看 A： interrogatory 只能给 party → 不能问外人
看 B： mental exam 只针对当事人的身心状况 → 题干没这个问题
看 C： oral deposition 可对 party / nonparty 做宣誓询问 → 命中
看 D： request for admissions 只能要求对方承认事实 → 不能对 nonparty 用
卡死结论：能问非当事人的，是 oral deposition，所以答案是 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然都是 discovery，那四个工具应该都能向外人要信息。

但考试真正问的是：这一个工具能不能对 nonparty 直接用，不是“能不能最后拿到信息”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干点明要从 nonparty witness 取信息，oral deposition 可以对非当事人进行庭外宣誓询问。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 interrogatory 当成能问外人的工具了。

❌ 法律适用 | 身心检查误判

✕ B: 看到 mental exam 就套进取证题，但题干根本不是身心争议。

❌ 事实误判 | 对象偷换

✕ D: 把 admissions 误当成能要求 nonparty 承认事实。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看对象是不是 nonparty，再逐个筛掉只能对 party 用的工具。

考场速记

记住一句：deposition 能问 party 也能问 nonparty；interrogatories 和 requests for admissions 都只对 party。

一眼看见“nonparty witness”，先想 oral deposition，再想 subpoena 补到场。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An insurance company from State A paid out $500,000 to a dentist from State B after she filed a claim for property damage allegedly caused by a spontaneous fire. After further investigation, however, the insurance company concluded that the dentist intentionally set the fire to recover the insurance money.
The insurance company sued the dentist in a federal court in State B to recover the $500,000 it had paid her. In its complaint, the insurance company claimed that the dentist "intentionally devised a plan to defraud the insurer and obtain money by false pretenses."
The dentist filed a pre-answer motion to dismiss the complaint for failure to state a claim on which relief may be granted.
Will the dentist likely succeed on her motion to dismiss?

choices.A: No, because the complaint contains a short and plain statement of the claim showing that the insurance company is entitled to relief.
choices.B: No, because the dentist must file an answer before she can make this motion.
choices.C: Yes, because a federal court cannot hear claims based on fraud.
choices.D: Yes, because claims based on fraud must be stated with particularity.

questions.explanation:
Specificity of pleadings
Claim Pleading requirements
General rule
  • Complaint – short & plain statement of claim showing plaintiff is entitled to relief
  • Answer – short & plain statement of admissions, denials, defenses & claims against other parties
Fraud/mistake/mental condition
  • Malice, intent, knowledge, or other mental condition may be alleged generally
  • Circumstances giving rise to fraud/mistake must be stated with particularity
Conditions precedent
  • Assertion that conditions precedent occurred may be alleged generally
  • Denial that conditions precedent occurred must be stated with particularity
Damages
  • General damages may be alleged generally
  • Special damages must be specifically stated

A complaint is the pleading that starts a civil lawsuit and states the basis for the plaintiff's claim. It generally must contain a short and plain statement of the claim showing that the plaintiff is entitled to relief. However, Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 9(b) sets forth different pleading requirements for a complaint alleging mistake or fraud (as seen here) or mental conditions. Such complaints:

• may allege generally the defendant's malice, intent, knowledge, or other mental condition—eg, stating that the defendant acted intentionally—but

• must state with particularity the circumstances giving rise to the claim—eg, specifying the time, place, and nature of the alleged fraud.

Here, the insurance company's complaint alleged that the dentist "intentionally devised a plan to defraud the insurer and obtain money by false pretenses." But it failed to state the circumstances giving rise to the fraud claim, like when and how the dentist set fire to her office (Choice A). As a result, the complaint failed to state a claim on which relief may be granted, and the dentist will likely succeed on her motion to dismiss.*

*However, the court will likely allow the insurance company to amend its complaint to correct the defect since amendments are liberally allowed in federal court.

(Choice B) FRCP 12 allows a defendant to make several motions before filing his/her answer—including a motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim on which relief may be granted (as seen here).

(Choice C) Federal courts can hear most state law claims—including fraud claims—when their subject-matter jurisdiction is based on diversity jurisdiction. The only state law claims that may not be heard in federal court are those involving probate matters (eg, authenticating wills) or domestic relations (eg, issuing divorces).

📌 Educational Objective

A complaint must contain a short and plain statement of the claim showing that the plaintiff is entitled to relief. When a complaint alleges mistake, fraud, or a mental condition, (1) the defendant's intent or other mental condition may be alleged generally but (2) the circumstances giving rise to the claim must be stated with particularity.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 9(b) (heightened pleading standards).

一家来自A州的保险公司，在一名来自B州的牙医就据称由自燃火灾引起的财产损失提出索赔后，向其支付了50万美元。

然而，经过进一步调查，该保险公司得出结论，该牙医是为骗取保险金而故意纵火。

该保险公司在B州的联邦法院起诉了该牙医，要求返还其已支付的50万美元。在其诉状中，该保险公司声称，该牙医“故意策划欺诈保险公司，并以欺诈手段获取金钱。”

该牙医提交了一项答辩前动议，以诉状未能陈述可据以获得救济的诉请为由，请求驳回该诉状。

该牙医的驳回动议是否可能成功？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为诉状包含了对诉请的简明陈述，表明保险公司有权获得救济。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该牙医必须先提交答辩状，然后才能提出此项动议。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为联邦法院不能审理基于欺诈的诉请。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为基于欺诈的诉请必须具体陈述。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Complaint

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：欺诈（fraud）类主张不能只写“故意骗我”，还要把事情发生的时间、地点和方式写清楚。

三秒认题路径：

Complaint → fraud → 9(b) → 细节不足 → 选 D

核心法律规则

起诉状（complaint）一般只要有简短而明白的陈述（short and plain statement），说明原告有权获得救济就行。但一旦主张是欺诈（fraud）、错误（mistake）或某些精神状态，FRCP 9(b)就要求把“发生了什么事”写得更具体。也就是说，intent 可以大概写，但导致欺诈的具体情节（circumstances）必须写到时间、地点、方式。

核心判例： 本题按 FRCP 9(b) 的高度起诉标准来判断：只写“故意设计骗局”不够，缺少具体事实就会被驳回。

思维导图

先看起诉状写了什么？
一般规则：short and plain statement 就够。
但本题碰到：fraud（欺诈） → 触发 FRCP 9(b)
可一般写：intent、knowledge、malice
卡死点：不能只写“故意骗钱”
必须具体写：时间 + 地点 + 方式 + 事情怎么骗的
所以本题结果？
只写“intentionally devised a plan to defraud” → 细节不够
结论：可以用 12(b)(6) 驳回 → 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然起诉状已经说了“故意诈骗”，那不是已经够了吗？

但考试真正问的是：fraud 这个类别有没有触发 9(b) 的特别要求；这里缺的是具体情节，不是主观故意。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「事实故事听起来像不像真的有诈」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干只写intentionally devised a plan to defraud，却没交代骗术如何发生；FRCP 9(b) 要求欺诈细节写得更具体，所以能驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把一般起诉标准当成欺诈案件的全部要求了。

❌ 法律适用 | 先后顺序误判

✕ B: 以为先答辩才能动议，忽略了 pre-answer motion。

❌ 事实误判 | 联邦管辖偷换

✕ C: 把“能否审理”偷换成“欺诈要件怎么写”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先识别是否触发特别起诉标准，再看题干有没有把关键事实写到位。

考场速记

记忆口诀：一般起诉看“简短明白”，fraud / mistake 额外看“具体细节”。见到“故意骗人”先别急着选对，要再找时间、地点、方式。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
Several female students enrolled at a public university sued the university in federal district court for violating a federal law that prohibits gender-based discrimination. The female students allege that the university provided them with substandard athletic facilities in comparison to those provided to its male students. The complaint requests a permanent injunction against the university to prevent it from discriminating against female students. The university has denied any allegations of gender discrimination.
Prior to the current litigation, an email between the university's athletic director and women's basketball coach revealed that the university refused requests to update its female athletic facilities because female sports provided the university with substantially less revenue than male sports.
The university has initiated an investigation into the allegations in the students' complaint and has asked its attorney for advice whether the email must be provided as part of the university's initial disclosures.
What is the university's best argument to withhold the email from its initial disclosures?

choices.A: A party need not make initial disclosures until it has fully investigated the case.
choices.B: Initial disclosures need not be provided without a discovery request.
choices.C: Permanent-injunction proceedings are exempt from mandatory initial disclosures.
choices.D: The email supports the female students' claim that the university violated federal law.

questions.explanation:
Required discovery disclosures
(FRCP 26(a))
Type Required disclosures Time to disclose
Initial disclosures*
  • Persons with relevant information
  • Items in party's possession that support claim/defense
  • Computation of damages & supporting material
  • Relevant insurance policies
  • ≤ 14 days after initial planning conference
  • ≤ 30 days after post-conference service or joinder
  • As court orders or parties stipulate
Expert testimony
  • Identity of expert witnesses
  • Expert's written report
  • If no report, subject matter & summary of testimony
  • ≥ 90 days before trial
  • ≤ 30 days after disclosure to rebut evidence
  • As court orders or parties stipulate
Pretrial disclosures*
  • Testifying witnesses
  • Deposition testimony to be used at trial
  • Documents/exhibits to be used at trial
  • ≥ 30 days before trial
  • As court orders

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.
*Does not apply to evidence used solely for impeachment.

Under FRCP 26(a), parties are required to make initial disclosures without a discovery request (Choice B). A party must initially disclose:

  • the names, addresses, and phone numbers of persons with relevant information that the party may use to support its claim or defense
  • all documents, electronically stored information, and tangible things in the party's possession that the party may use to support its claims or defenses
  • any insurance agreement with a company that may be liable for all or part of any judgment and
  • a computation of damages and the materials on which it was based.

All of this information must be disclosed within 14 days after the initial planning conference or by a date set by the court or parties.

Here, the email reveals that the university refused requests to update its female athletic facilities because female sports provided the university with substantially less revenue than male sports. Disclosure of that document would likely support the female students' claim that the university engaged in gender discrimination in violation of federal law. And since a party must only initially disclose documents that support its own (not the opposing party's) claims or defenses, this is the university's best argument to withhold the email thread from its initial disclosures.*

*Even though the university is not required to disclose the email as part of its initial disclosures, the female students can still seek the email through a discovery request if it is within the scope of discovery.

(Choice A) A party must make its initial disclosures based on the information that is reasonably available to it at that time—regardless of whether it has fully investigated the case.

(Choice C) Certain proceedings are exempt from the initial-disclosures requirement because they rarely involve discovery or because initial disclosures are unlikely to contribute to case development. However, permanent-injunction proceedings are not exempt from this requirement.

📌 Educational Objective

A party's initial disclosures must include all documents, electronically stored information, and tangible things in the party's possession that the party may use to support its claims or defenses—not those of the opposing party.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(1)(A) (required initial disclosures).
  • 8A Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2053 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining the initial-disclosures requirement requires parties to disclose information they may use to support their own claims or defenses).

在当前诉讼之前，大学体育主管与女子篮球队教练之间的一封电子邮件显示，大学拒绝了更新其女子体育设施的请求，理由是女子体育为大学带来的收入远低于男子体育。
大学已对学生诉状中的指控展开调查，并已向其律师咨询该电子邮件是否必须作为大学的初步披露（initial disclosures）的一部分提供。
大学不将该电子邮件纳入其初步披露的最佳论点是什么？

zh-choices.A: 当事人无需在案件完全调查清楚之前进行初步披露。
zh-choices.B: 未经证据开示请求（discovery request），无需提供初步披露。
zh-choices.C: 永久禁令（permanent-injunction）程序豁免强制性初步披露（mandatory initial disclosures）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery, disclosures, sanctions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：初始披露（initial disclosures）只要披露本方可能用来支持自己主张或抗辩的材料，不用帮对方找证据。

三秒认题路径：

初始披露 → 看本方 → 不看对方 → 能否拒披 → 选 D

核心法律规则

在联邦民事诉讼规则（FRCP）26(a)下，当事人要在规定时间内做初始披露（initial disclosures），而且无需发现请求（without a discovery request）。考场意思：这是默认要交，不是等对方来要。

但规则只要求披露本方可能用来支持自己主张或抗辩的文件、电子信息和有形物。考场意思：如果材料更像是在帮对方证明案子，你就有理由先不放进初始披露里。

核心判例： 本题不需要专门靠判例记忆；直接抓住 FRCP 26(a) 的“支持本方（support its own claims or defenses）”这一句，就能锁定结论。

思维导图

先问：这份 email 是不是大学 可能用来支持自己抗辩 的材料？
是：要放进初始披露，属于本方会用的证据。
卡死结论：不能以“它对我不利”为理由拒绝。
否：如果它只是帮女学生证明歧视，大学可以先不列入初始披露。
这时女学生仍可再用普通发现请求（discovery request）去要它。
本题落点：email 说“因女队收入低所以不更新设施”→ 更像帮原告证明性别歧视 → 大学可先不做初始披露。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然 email 跟案件有关，大学就应该先交出来。

但考试真正问的是：初始披露看的是本方要用来支持自己主张或抗辩的材料，不是任何“对案子有用”的材料。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 email 支持女学生的歧视主张，而初始披露只管本方会用的材料，所以大学可以先不把它列进去。

❌ 法律适用 | 预调查误判

✕ A: 把 fully investigated 当成前提，规则根本没这道门槛。

❌ 概念混淆 | 请求前提错认

✕ B: 误以为初始披露要等 discovery request，其实它本来就自动发生。

❌ 事实误判 | 例外范围偷换

✕ C: 把 permanent-injunction 说成豁免情形，但这类案件仍要做初始披露。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看披露义务是默认发生还是要等请求，再看材料是帮本方还是帮对方。

考场速记

记忆口诀：初始披露只交“我方会用的”，不替对方找证据。 看到规则题就先抓 support its own claims or defenses 这句。
