questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A customer brought a federal diversity action against a corporation. During discovery, the customer requested information that was stored on hard drives at the corporation's headquarters. The corporation informed the customer that the hard drives had been wiped clean when the corporation switched over to a new information technology firm a few months before the customer filed suit. The customer moved for sanctions.
After a hearing, the court found that the corporation negligently failed to preserve the information contained in the hard drives, but that the corporation did not act intentionally to prevent the customer from accessing the information. The court also found that the information cannot be obtained by any other means and that the loss of this information prejudices the customer's claim.
Based on those findings, what action should the court take?

choices.A: Enter a default judgment in favor of the customer.
choices.B: Instruct the jury at trial that it must presume that the lost information was unfavorable to the corporation.
choices.C: Permit the parties to present evidence at trial regarding the loss of information.
choices.D: Prohibit the corporation from seeking discovery in the lawsuit to put the parties at a similar disadvantage.

questions.explanation:
Sanctions for failure to preserve electronically stored information (ESI)

Party fails to preserve ESI
  • Should have been preserved
  • Reasonable steps not taken to preserve
  • Cannot be replaced or restored
If party acted with intent to deprive, court may:
  • presume ESI was unfavorable
  • instruct jury that it may or must presume ESI was unfavorable
  • dismiss action or enter default judgment
If party otherwise prejudiced requesting party, court may:
  • order measure no greater than necessary to cure prejudice

Sactions may be appropriate if a party failed to preserve electronically stored information (ESI) that:

  • should have been preserved in the anticipation or conduct of litigation
  • is lost because the party failed to take reasonable steps to preserve it and
  • cannot be replaced or restored through additional discovery.

If the court finds that the party intentionally deprived the requesting party of the ESI, the court may:

  • presume that the lost ESI was unfavorable to the party that failed to preserve it
  • instruct the jury that it may or must presume the lost ESI was unfavorable to that party* (Choice B) or
  • dismiss the action or enter a default judgment against that party (Choice A).

These sanctions are not available here because the corporation acted negligently—not intentionally. As a result, the court should only order measures that are no greater than necessary to cure the prejudice caused to the customer—e.g., allow the parties to present evidence at trial regarding the loss of the ESI.

*A court may instruct the jury about the missing evidence and that it may consider this missing evidence in its deliberations. However, an instruction that the jury may or must presume that the lost ESI was unfavorable to the party that failed to preserve it is permissible only if the court finds that the party intentionally deprived the requesting party of the ESI.

(Choice D) It is unlikely that a court would prohibit a party from seeking discovery as a form of sanction as that would frustrate the purpose of discovery—i.e., to uncover facts, narrow the issues in dispute, and otherwise prepare both parties for trial.

📌 Educational Objective

A court may order measures no greater than necessary to cure prejudice caused by a party's failure to preserve electronically stored information that (1) should have been preserved in the anticipation or conduct of litigation, (2) is lost because the party failed to take reasonable steps to preserve it, and (3) cannot be replaced or restored.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(e) (failure to preserve electronically stored information).
  • 8B Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2284.2 (3d ed. 2024) (explaining that certain sanctions can be imposed only if it is shown that a party intentionally deprived another party of electronically stored information).
questions.zh-question:
一位客户对一家公司提起了联邦多元管辖权诉讼。在证据开示期间，客户要求获取存储在公司总部硬盘上的信息。公司告知客户，在客户提起诉讼前几个月，公司更换了新的信息技术公司，届时硬盘已被清空。客户动议要求制裁。

经过听证，法院认定公司因过失未能保存硬盘中包含的信息，但公司并非为了阻止客户获取信息而故意为之。法院还认定，该信息无法通过任何其他方式获得，且该信息的丢失对客户的诉讼主张造成了损害。

基于这些认定，法院应采取何种措施？

zh-choices.A: 做出对客户有利的缺席判决。
zh-choices.B: 在审判中指示陪审团，必须推定丢失的信息对公司不利。
zh-choices.C: 允许双方在审判中就信息丢失一事提交证据。
zh-choices.D: 禁止公司在诉讼中进行证据开示，以使双方处于类似的不利地位。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Enforcement

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：电子存储信息（electronically stored information, ESI）被过失删掉后，法院能下多重的sanction。

三秒认题路径：

ESI被删 → 过失不是故意 → 不能替代 → 只做最小补救 → 选C

核心法律规则

如果一方本应在预期或进行诉讼时保全 电子存储信息（ESI），但没有采取合理措施，且这些信息无法通过其他发现手段恢复，法院可以给出补救性措施。

但如果只是 过失（negligent），考场意思：法院只能下不超过修复偏害所必需的措施（measures no greater than necessary to cure prejudice），不能直接跳到默认判决或必然不利推定。

只有法院认定一方 故意剥夺（intent to deprive） 对方 ESI，才可以用更重的制裁，比如推定该信息对失责方不利、命令陪审团必须或可以作不利推定，甚至 default judgment（缺席判决）。

核心判例： 这里的规则直接对应 Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(e)：本题只查到过失，所以只能做补救，不能上默认判决或不利推定。

思维导图

先看：这是不是 ESI 保全失败（failure to preserve ESI）？
① 本该保全吗？题干说硬盘信息在诉讼前后本应保存。
② 只是不合理疏忽吗？法院已认定是 negligently，不是故意。
③ 能修回来吗？不能；而且损失已经让原告受偏害。
卡死点：没有 intent to deprive，所以不能用“必须不利推定”或“默认判决”这种重罚。
结果法院只能下 最小必要补救，例如允许双方在庭审中就丢失事实发表证据与说明。
答案：C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：信息都被清空了，客户看起来很惨，法院应该狠狠干预。

但考试真正问的是：失去的是 ESI 时，法院能下多重的 程序性补救，不是看谁更倒霉。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的硬盘内容有没有彻底消失」。

因为这里没有故意毁证，B 的“不利推定”和 A 的“默认判决”都太重；D 更离谱，禁掉对方 discovery 反而和 discovery 目的相反。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干已给出 negligently failed to preserve，所以只能用最小必要措施补救偏害；让双方在庭审中就丢失证据发表意见，正好落在规则里。

❌ 概念混淆 | 默认判决误判

✕ A: 把过失删档当成故意毁证，直接冲到 default judgment。

❌ 法律适用 | 不利推定误判

✕ B: 只有 intent to deprive 才能上不利推定，这题没有。

❌ 事实误判 | discovery倒置

✕ D: 想用“让对方也别取证”来对称惩罚，但这会直接伤到 discovery 目的。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否属于 ESI 保全失败，再问有没有故意剥夺；没有故意时，只能选补救而不是重罚。

考场速记

记住一句：过失删 ESI → 只补救；故意毁 ESI → 才能重罚。

口诀：“先看故意，再看补救；没故意，别乱上默认判决和不利推定。”

question_analysis.skill_tested: determine appropriate sanctions for lost ESI

reason.en: Indicates the legal remedy requested for the loss of evidence.
reason.zh: 表明因证据丢失而请求的法律救济。

reason.en: Establishes that the level of culpability was negligence, not intent.
reason.zh: 确定归责程度为过失而非故意。

reason.en: Precludes the court from imposing severe sanctions like default judgment or adverse inference instructions.
reason.zh: 排除法院施加默认判决或不利推定指示等严重制裁的可能性。

reason.en: Satisfies the prerequisite for ordering cures that are no greater than necessary to remedy the harm.
reason.zh: 满足下令采取不超过弥补损害所需必要限度的补救措施的前提条件。

reason.en: Represents a severe sanction that requires a finding of intent to deprive.
reason.zh: 代表一种严厉的制裁手段，要求认定存在剥夺证据的故意。

reason.en: A severe spoliation sanction that is unavailable without a showing of intent.
reason.zh: 若无故意之证明，则无法使用该严厉的证据灭失制裁。

label.zh: 庭审中出示证据灭失情况

reason.en: A curative measure proportional to the prejudice caused by negligent ESI loss.
reason.zh: 与因过失丢失电子存储信息所造成的损害相称的补救措施。

D.text: Prohibit the corporation from seeking discovery

label.zh: 禁止进行证据开示的制裁

reason.en: An inappropriate sanction that frustrates the basic purpose of discovery.
reason.zh: 一种不恰当的制裁，会挫败证据开示的基本目的。

highlights.text: negligently failed to preserve

reason.en: Indicates the level of culpability is negligence, which precludes severe sanctions.
reason.zh: 表明过失的归责程度，排除了严重制裁的适用。

highlights.text: did not act intentionally to prevent the customer from accessing the information

reason.en: Confirms that default judgment or adverse presumption sanctions cannot be ordered.
reason.zh: 确认无法适用缺席判决或不利推定指示等制裁。

highlights.text: prejudices the customer's claim

label.zh: 对申请方主张造成偏见

reason.en: Satisfies the prerequisite to order measures no greater than necessary to cure the prejudice.
reason.zh: 满足下令采取不超过弥补该偏见所需必要限度措施的前提条件。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A plaintiff obtained an ex parte temporary restraining order (TRO) in a federal civil action and posted a bond the same day. One day later, the plaintiff served the defendant with copies of the summons and complaint, the TRO, and supporting documents. The court scheduled a hearing on the preliminary injunction to occur 14 days after the TRO had been issued.
Two days before the hearing, the plaintiff moved to extend the TRO and postpone the hearing for one week on the ground that its principal witness would be unavailable to testify on the scheduled day due to a planned vacation. The defendant opposed the motion and moved to dissolve the TRO.
Is the court likely to grant the defendant's motion to dissolve the TRO?

choices.A: No, because a TRO can be extended once for 14 days.
choices.B: No, because the plaintiff posted a bond and its principal witness's testimony is critical to the hearing.
choices.C: Yes, because the plaintiff's principal witness's vacation is not good cause to extend the TRO.
choices.D: Yes, because the TRO will expire before a rescheduled hearing can be held.

questions.explanation:
Temporary restraining orders
(FRCP 65(b))
Obtaining Movant must provide:
  • specific facts in affidavit or verified complaint clearly showing immediate & irreparable injury, loss, or damage
  • written certification by movant's attorney of efforts to give notice & reasons why it should not be required and
  • security to pay costs & damages sustained by wrongfully restrained party
Extending Limited to 14 days or until preliminary-injunction hearing can take place unless:
  • opposing party consents to extension or
  • good cause exists
Dissolving
  • Party moving to dissolve order must give two days' notice
  • Court must hear & decide motion as promptly as justice requires

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A temporary restraining order (TRO) is a court order that commands a party to do or stop doing a specified action for 14 days or until a preliminary-injunction hearing can take place—whichever occurs first. Once this period expires, the court should dissolve the TRO unless it has already been extended because:

  • the opposing party consented to the extension (not seen here) or
  • there was good cause, which generally requires the movant to show that an unforeseeable event prevents the scheduled hearing from taking place.

Here, the witness's vacation was planned, so the witness's unavailability at the preliminary-injunction hearing was not a surprise. The plaintiff should have known the availability of its principal witness before seeking a TRO and planned accordingly. Since the plaintiff cannot provide good cause for extending the TRO and postponing the preliminary-injunction hearing, the court is likely to grant the defendant's motion to dissolve the TRO.

(Choice A) A TRO can be extended only if the opposing party consents or good cause exists. Therefore, it cannot be automatically extended once for 14 days.

(Choice B) A federal court will issue a TRO only if the movant provides security (eg, a bond) sufficient to pay the costs and damages if the nonmovant is improperly restrained. However, the plaintiff's posting of a bond does not affect whether the court should extend the TRO. Additionally, the critical nature of the principal witness's testimony does not alone establish good cause needed to extend a TRO.

(Choice D) Had the plaintiff provided good cause, the court could have extended the TRO for a "like period," which cannot exceed the period provided in the initial order. Here, the initial TRO period was 14 days, so extending the TRO and postponing the hearing for a week would have been valid had good cause existed.

📌 Educational Objective

A TRO generally applies for 14 days or until a preliminary-injunction hearing can take place—whichever occurs first. A court can extend a TRO beyond this time if (1) the opposing party consents or (2) the movant provides good cause.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(b)(2) (extension of TRO).
  • 11A Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2953 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining how a TRO can be extended beyond 14 days).
questions.zh-question:
在一个联邦民事诉讼中，原告获得了一项单方面的临时限制令 (TRO)，并在同日提交了保证金。一天后，原告向被告送达了传票和起诉状、临时限制令以及支持文件的副本。法院安排在临时限制令签发14天后举行关于初步禁令的听证会。

在听证会前两天，原告提出动议，请求将临时限制令延长并推迟听证会一周，理由是其主要证人因已计划好的假期而无法在预定日期出庭作证。被告反对该动议，并提出解除临时限制令的动议。

法院是否可能批准被告解除临时限制令的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为临时限制令可以延长一次，为期14天。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为原告提交了保证金，并且其主要证人的证词对听证会至关重要。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为原告主要证人的假期不构成延长临时限制令的正当理由。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为临时限制令将在重新安排的听证会举行前失效。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Preliminary injunctions & TROs

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：临时限制令（temporary restraining order, TRO）到期后，能不能因为原告自己早就知道的证人旅行安排而延期。

三秒认题路径：

TRO到期 → 想延期 → 看good cause → 计划内缺席 → 可解散

核心法律规则

临时限制令（temporary restraining order, TRO）一般只管14天，或者直到初步禁令听证（preliminary-injunction hearing）能开，哪个先到算哪个。要想继续延长，必须有对方同意，或者有正当理由（good cause）。

这里的good cause考场意思：不是“我现在很需要”，而是“有个意外事件把原定听证顶掉了”。如果延期理由是原告自己早就能预见的事情，就不够。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries 不适用于本题；本题锁定的是 FRCP 65(b) 下 TRO 延期的正当理由标准。

思维导图

Day 0
ex parte TRO 发出；同日交 bond，这只是发令条件，不解决延期问题。
Day 1
送达 summons、complaint 和支持材料，程序继续往前走。
Day 14
原定听证日；TRO 本来就要到期，除非有 consent 或 good cause。
临近听证前2天
原告说主证人去度假，想延期一周；这是可预见安排，不是意外。
结论
不能把计划内缺席包装成 good cause；被告申请解散，法院应倾向准许。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：证人很关键、还交了 bond，所以法院应该给原告再拖一周。

但考试真正问的是：TRO 到期后有没有 good cause 延长；证人重要不等于理由正当，早就知道的假期也不是意外。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干关键点是主证人休假是已计划事项，这不是不可预见的意外，所以不构成延长 TRO 的 good cause。

✕ B: bond 只管误禁赔偿，不管能否延期；证人关键也不等于正当理由。

❌ 事实误判 | 到期时间偷换

✕ D: 先假设一定来不及续期，但题目真正卡的是有没有 good cause。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看程序时点，再查是否有对方同意或不可预见的 good cause。

考场速记

记住：TRO 默认只活14天；想续命，先问“对方同意没有，或者有没有意外的 good cause”。

一句话口诀：“TRO 到期看两件：同意 or good cause；计划内麻烦，不算正当理由。”

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A pedestrian filed a federal diversity action against a motorcyclist, alleging that the motorcyclist ran a stop sign and hit the pedestrian in a crosswalk outside of a bar.
During discovery, the pedestrian's attorney interviewed a bartender who was working at the bar on the night the accident occurred. The bartender told the attorney that the motorcyclist drank four bottles of beer and two shots of tequila in the hour immediately preceding the accident. The attorney wrote down the bartender's statements in a document.
The motorcyclist requested that the pedestrian produce all documents related to the case, including statements by potential witnesses. In response, the pedestrian's attorney produced several documents and a privilege log of the documents withheld. The privilege log included a description of the document containing the bartender's statements. The motorcyclist filed a motion to compel production of this document.
Should the court grant the motorcyclist's motion?

choices.A: No, because the document is inadmissible at trial.
choices.B: No, because the motorcyclist can obtain the information in the document by other means.
choices.C: Yes, because the document does not contain the attorney's opinions or legal theories.
choices.D: Yes, because the motorcyclist has a right to receive all materials containing information relevant to the case.

questions.explanation:
Work product
(FRCP 26(b)(3))
Type Definition Discoverability
Ordinary Materials created in anticipation of litigation that contain factual information related to case Not discoverable unless requesting party:
• has substantial need for materials and
• cannot obtain information without undue hardship
Opinion Materials created in anticipation of litigation that contain attorney's mental impressions, conclusions, opinions, or legal theories Not discoverable unless:
• material concerns attorney's alleged fraudulent/illegal conduct (rare)
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

During discovery, a party can use various methods (eg, request for production) to obtain nonprivileged information that is (1) relevant to any party's claim or defense and (2) proportional to the needs of the case. As a result, a party generally cannot obtain privileged information—including materials prepared by or for an attorney in anticipation of litigation (ie, work product) (Choice D). Work product falls into one of two categories:

  • Ordinary – materials containing factual information related to the case (eg, a document containing a witness's statements—as seen here)
  • Opinion – materials containing the attorney's mental impressions, conclusions, opinions, or legal theories (eg, a document containing the attorney's trial strategy)

Opinion work product is almost never discoverable.* And ordinary work product is only discoverable if the requesting party shows that it (1) has a substantial need for the materials and (2) cannot obtain the information contained therein without undue hardship—eg, the witness dies before the requesting party can interview him/her.

Here, the motorcyclist cannot demonstrate a substantial need for the document or undue hardship in obtaining the information contained therein. That is because the motorcyclist can easily obtain this information by other means—eg, by having his attorney interview or depose the bartender. Therefore, the court should deny the motorcyclist's motion to compel production of the document.

*Most courts have held that opinion work product is only discoverable in the rare instance when the materials show that the attorney committed fraud or another crime.

(Choice A) The document's admissibility at trial has no effect on whether it is discoverable because the scope of discovery includes inadmissible information and materials.

(Choice C) The document is not opinion work product because it does not contain the attorney's impressions, conclusions, opinions, or legal theories. However, it is ordinary work product that is not subject to discovery.

📌 Educational Objective

Ordinary work product is any material prepared by or for an attorney in anticipation of litigation that contains factual information related to the case. These materials are protected from discovery unless the requesting party shows that it (1) has a substantial need for the materials and (2) cannot obtain the information without undue hardship.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(3) (work product and trial-preparation materials).
  • Hickman v. Taylor, 329 U.S. 495, 511–12 (1947) (explaining the importance of protecting work-product materials from disclosure and when such materials may need to be disclosed).

一名行人对一名摩托车手提起了联邦多元管辖权诉讼（federal diversity action），指控该摩托车手闯红灯并在酒吧外的人行横道上撞到了行人。
在证据开示（discovery）阶段，行人的律师采访了一名在事故发生当晚在该酒吧工作的调酒师。调酒师告诉律师，在事故发生前一小时内，摩托车手喝了四瓶啤酒和两杯龙舌兰酒。律师将调酒师的陈述记录在一份文件中。
摩托车手要求行人出示所有与案件相关的文档，包括潜在证人的陈述。作为回应，行人的律师出示了几份文件，并提交了一份被扣留文件的特权日志（privilege log）。特权日志中包含了对这份记录调酒师陈述的文件的描述。摩托车手提交了一份强制出示该文件的动议（motion to compel production）。
法院是否应批准摩托车手的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为该文件在庭审中不可采纳（inadmissible）。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为摩托车手可以通过其他方式获取该文件中的信息。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该文件不包含律师的意见或法律理论。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为摩托车手有权获得所有包含与案件相关信息的材料。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery Scope and Limits

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通工作成果（ordinary work product）能不能被迫披露，关键看对方有没有重大需要（substantial need）和过度困难（undue hardship）。

三秒认题路径：

律师写下证人陈述 → 预期诉讼材料 → 普通工作成果 → 能否替代取得 → 不能强制披露

核心法律规则

律师为诉讼准备的材料属于工作成果（work product），考场意思：一般不能直接拿走。普通工作成果（ordinary work product）是事实材料，只有在对方证明自己确实需要，而且拿不到才行。

意见工作成果（opinion work product）更难拿，除非极少数欺诈或犯罪情形。这里的文档只是证人说法，不是律师思路，所以要走普通工作成果规则。

核心判例： Hickman v. Taylor — 它把工作成果保护锁死，提醒你：先看是不是律师备战材料，再看有没有重大需要和过度困难。

思维导图

先判定：这是不是工作成果（work product）？
是律师为诉讼写下的证人陈述
再分这是普通工作成果（ordinary work product），因为只有事实，没有律师心里想法
再问对方能否证明重大需要（substantial need） + 过度困难（undue hardship）
本题直接卡死：旁边就能问酒保或传唤作证，effectively 还能拿到，不满足
结论不能强制披露 → 选 B
误区“能不能在庭审用”不是这里的答案；发现规则看的是能不能披露，不是能不能采信

考点陷阱

你可能会想：只要材料对案件有帮助，或者以后可能拿来作证，就应该给对方看。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是律师备战时做出的工作成果（work product），以及对方有没有证明自己真的拿不到别的来源。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 bartender 的口头陈述属于普通工作成果；对方还能直接去问酒保，所以没有重大需要和过度困难。

❌ 概念混淆 | 可采性误判

✕ A: 把 inadmissible 当成不能披露，混了证据可采性和发现范围。

❌ 法律适用 | 意见保护误判

✕ C: 只盯着没有律师心里话，就忽略了它仍是受保护的普通工作成果。

❌ 事实误判 | 相关即公开误判

✕ D: 把 relevant 误当成全都能拿，忽略了工作成果例外。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是工作成果，再问对方能不能从别的渠道轻松拿到同样信息。

考场速记

口诀：“先问是不是诉讼备战材料，再问有没有重大需要 + 过度困难。”

记住：证人说法写进律师笔记里，通常还是保护的；对方能自己去问，就很难强制要走。

reason.en: Establishes federal court jurisdiction, invoking federal procedural rules (FRCP 26).

reason.en: Signals the creation of a document by the attorney, which is protected work product.
reason.zh: 表明律师创建了该文件，该文件属于受保护的工作成果。

reason.en: Identifies the document withheld, starting the dispute over work product protection.

reason.en: Inadmissibility at trial does not bar discovery if the information is relevant and proportional.
reason.zh: 如果在审判中不可采，并不妨碍其在证据开示中被获取，只要其相关且符合比例。

B.text: obtain the information in the document by other means

reason.en: Defeats the 'undue hardship' element required to discover ordinary work product.
reason.zh: 击败了开示普通工作成果所需的“过度困难”要件。

C.text: does not contain the attorney's opinions or legal theories

reason.en: Even if it lacks opinions, ordinary work product is still protected from discovery unless an exception is met.
reason.zh: 即使不包含意见，普通工作成果仍受保护，除非符合例外情况。

D.text: all materials containing information relevant to the case

reason.en: Incorrectly suggests relevance overcomes the work product doctrine.
reason.zh: 错误地暗示相关性可以克服工作成果法则的保护。

highlights.text: The attorney wrote down the bartender's statements in a document.

reason.en: Establishes that the document is attorney work product and subject to conditional protection.
reason.zh: 确立了该文件为律师工作成果，受到有条件的保护。

highlights.text: privilege log

reason.en: Shows the pedestrian properly asserted protection over the document.
reason.zh: 表明原告已对该文件妥善主张了保护。

highlights.text: motion to compel production

reason.en: Triggers court evaluation of whether the requesting party meets the exception requirements.
reason.zh: 触发法院评估请求方是否符合例外情况的要求。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An executive signed an employment contract with a steel plant. The contract contained a noncompete clause that prohibited the executive from working for any of the steel plant's competitors for one year after leaving the plant. The contract also contained a nondisclosure clause that prohibited the executive from disclosing the steel plant's trade secrets and other confidential information. On September 1, 2015, the executive left the steel plant. On August 1, 2016, she began working for one of the steel plant's competitors.
On April 1, 2018, the steel plant filed a complaint against the executive in a federal court for breaching the noncompete clause. On November 1, 2018, the steel plant discovered that the executive divulged its trade secrets to its competitor when she began working there. The steel plant immediately filed a motion with the court to amend its complaint to add a claim for infringement of trade secrets against the executive.
The applicable statute of limitations for each claim is two years from the date the violation allegedly occurred. The laws that establish these statutes of limitations do not mention whether relation back is allowed for these claims.
Should the federal court allow the steel plant to amend its complaint to include the trade secrets claim?

choices.A: No, because the executive did not consent to the amendment.
choices.B: No, because the statute of limitations for the claim has expired.
choices.C: Yes, because a federal court should freely allow amendments to pleadings when justice so requires.
choices.D: Yes, because the amended claim arises from the transaction and occurrence set out in the original pleading.

questions.explanation:
Relation-back doctrine
(FRCP 15(c))
No amendment after statute of
limitations expired unless:
Asserts new claim
Statute of limitations allows relation back
OR
New claim arises from same transaction
or occurrence as original pleading
Changes party
Statute of limitations allows relation back
OR
Concerns same transaction or
occurrence as original pleading and:
  • new party receives notice of suit within
    90 days of original filing and
  • new party knew (or should have known)
    he/she would be sued
Relation back permitted

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

An amended pleading filed after the statute of limitations has expired is permitted only when the relation-back doctrine applies. This doctrine treats the amendment as if it were filed on the same date as the original pleading—ie, the amendment "relates back" to the date of the original pleading. An amendment that asserts a new claim relates back when:

• the statute of limitations for the new claim allows relation back (not seen here) or

• the claim arises out of the conduct or occurrence set forth in the original pleading.

Here, the steel plant filed a motion to amend its complaint to add a trade secrets claim after the statute of limitations had expired on August 1, 2018. But this claim relates back to the date the steel plant filed its claim for breach of the noncompete clause—before the statute of limitations expired. That is because both claims arise from the executive's contract with the steel plant and her employment with the competitor. Therefore, the federal court should allow the steel plant to amend its complaint to include the trade secrets claim (Choice D).

(Choices A & C) The executive's (ie, opposing party's) consent is unnecessary because a federal court can permit amendments to pleadings without the defendant's consent and should do so when justice requires. But if consent is not given, any amendment must be filed before the statute of limitations expires or relate back to the date of the original pleading (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The relation-back doctrine allows an amended pleading to assert a new claim after the statute of limitations has expired when (1) the applicable statute of limitations allows relation back or (2) the claim arises out of the same conduct or occurrence as the original pleading.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(c) (relation back of amended pleadings).
questions.zh-question:
一名高管与一家钢铁厂签订了雇佣合同。该合同包含一项竞业禁止条款，禁止该高管在离开工厂一年内为该钢铁厂的任何竞争对手工作。该合同还包含一项保密条款，禁止该高管披露该钢铁厂的商业秘密和其他机密信息。2015年9月1日，该高管离开了该钢铁厂。2016年8月1日，她开始为该钢铁厂的一家竞争对手工作。

2018年4月1日，该钢铁厂向联邦法院对该高管提起诉讼，指控其违反了竞业禁止条款。2018年11月1日，该钢铁厂发现，该高管在开始为竞争对手工作时，向其泄露了商业秘密。该钢铁厂立即向法院提交动议，请求修改其诉状，以增加一项针对该高管的侵犯商业秘密的诉求。

每项诉求的适用诉讼时效为自称违规行为发生之日起两年。确立这些诉讼时效的法律并未提及这些诉求是否允许关联追溯。

联邦法院是否应允许该钢铁厂修改其诉状以包含商业秘密的诉求？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为该高管未同意该修改。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为该诉求的诉讼时效已过。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为当司法公正有此要求时，联邦法院应自由准许对诉状的修改。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为修改后的诉求源于原始诉状中所述的交易和事件。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Pleadings

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：修正诉状的关系回溯（relation back），也就是过了诉讼时效后新增的请求，能不能按原起诉日期算进去。

三秒认题路径：

过时效 → 改诉状 → 同交易吗 → 能回溯吗 → 选 D

核心法律规则

如果修正起诉状（amended pleading）是在诉讼时效（statute of limitations）过后才提交，能不能加进去，关键看关系回溯（relation back）。这里的考场意思：新主张如果和原告状写的是同一笔交易或发生经过（transaction or occurrence），就当成原告一开始一起提出来了。

FRCP 15(c) 还允许对“新请求”这样回溯；但对“换当事人”会多出通知等要求。本题只是加一个新 claim，不是换被告，所以只看是不是同一交易或经过。

核心判例： FRCP 15(c) 的规则就是：新请求只要来自原起诉状写出的同一事件链，就能按原日期算。

思维导图

先看：新 trade secrets claim 是不是在时效后才加？
是 进入 relation back。
再看：新 claim 是否来自原告状写出的同一 transaction or occurrence？
是 原告状已写同一份 employment contract + 去竞争对手工作这条线。
卡死点：不是看被告同不同意，而是看能不能按原起诉日期算。
结论：可以修正，关系回溯成立 → 选 D
否 就会被时效挡掉。
否 还没过时效时直接改，问题更小。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：都已经过了 two years，那新请求当然晚了。

但考试真正问的是：这个新请求能不能关系回溯到原告状日期，而不是只盯着时效表面到没到点。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 trade secrets claim 和原先的 noncompete claim 都绕着同一份雇佣合同和去竞争对手工作的事实展开，所以新请求可按原起诉日期计算。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把被告是否同意当成门槛，consent 根本不是这题关键。

❌ 事实误判 | 时效起算偷换

✕ B: 只盯着 expired，漏掉了可回溯到原告状日期这一层。

❌ 法律适用 | 自由修正误套

✕ C: 把“法院应当宽松允许修正”当万能钥匙，忽略了过时效后还得先过 relation back。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看时效是否已过，再用同一交易或经过测试新请求能否回溯。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“先看时效，再看回溯；同一交易，能救就救。”

这类题记住：relation back 不是问“新 claim 新不新”，而是问“它是不是原事件链上的另一张牌”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: applying the relation back doctrine to pleadings

reason.en: Indicates the party's request to add a new claim to the litigation.
reason.zh: 表明当事人请求在诉讼中增加新诉求。

reason.en: Sets the time limit for filing the claim, triggering the relation-back analysis.
reason.zh: 设定提起诉讼的期限，从而引发诉状修改回溯效力的分析。

reason.en: Determines whether the amended claim is treated as filed on the date of the original complaint.
reason.zh: 决定修改后的诉求是否被视为在原起诉日提出。

reason.en: The original pleading to which the amendment must relate back.
reason.zh: 修改案必须回溯到的原始诉状。

reason.en: Focuses on defendant's consent, which is not required if the court grants leave or relation back applies.
reason.zh: 错误关注被告的同意，在法院许可或符合回溯原则时并不需要被告同意。

B.text: statute of limitations for the claim has expired

reason.en: Ignores the relation-back doctrine exception for claims arising from the same transaction or occurrence.

reason.en: The basis of the original timely filing which provides the transaction/occurrence context.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A patient brought a diversity action against a doctor in federal court for medical malpractice. The patient alleges that the doctor negligently administered medication to the patient after surgery, which caused further complications. During discovery, the patient's attorney sent the doctor 30 requests for admission. One request stated, "Please admit that the medication administered to the patient poses a higher risk to individuals in the patient's age group." The doctor served a written response 21 days later, in which she specifically denied that the medication poses a higher risk to such individuals.
The case proceeded to trial. The patient offered several of the doctor's records into evidence that demonstrated the doctor knew at the time she prescribed the medication that it was unsafe for individuals in the patient's age group. At the conclusion of trial, the jury returned a verdict for the patient, specifically finding that the patient proved that the medication is unsafe for individuals in the patient's age group. The patient then moved for sanctions against the doctor to pay the reasonable expenses incurred in proving this matter.
Is the court likely to grant the patient's motion?

choices.A: No, because the patient's motion for sanctions after the jury returned its verdict was untimely.
choices.B: No, because the requests for admission exceeded the number allowed.
choices.C: Yes, because requests for admission are proper to obtain the truth about facts.
choices.D: Yes, because the patient proved that the matter was true.

questions.explanation:
Request for admission
  • Definition – request served on other party to admit truth of facts, application of law to facts, opinions, or genuineness of documents
  • Limit – none
  • Response – written response due within 30 days of service

Requests for admission allow a party to ask another party to admit the truth about matters within the scope of discovery relating to facts, the application of law to facts, opinions about either, or the genuineness of documents. This discovery method seeks to expedite litigation and decrease costs by alleviating the need to prove undisputed matters at trial.

If the responding party fails to admit a matter that is later proven true, then the requesting party can move for the responding party to pay reasonable expenses incurred, including attorney's fees, in making that proof. The court must grant this motion unless one of these conditions applies:

  • The court had sustained a prior objection to the request.
  • The admission sought was of no substantial importance.
  • The responding party reasonably believed that it would prevail on the matter.
  • Another good reason existed for the failure to admit.*

Here, the doctor responded to the patient's request for admission by denying that the medication poses a higher risk to individuals in the patient's age group. However, the jury found that the patient proved that this matter was true. And since none of the above conditions apply, the court is likely to grant the patient's motion.

*Courts have found a good reason when the responding party could not reasonably obtain information that would allow it to admit that the matter was true.

(Choice A) The requesting party may move for sanctions after the matter that the responding party failed to admit is proven true. Therefore, the motion here was timely because it was made after the jury's verdict found that the patient's claim that the medication posed a higher risk to individuals in the patient's age group was true.

(Choice B) The requests for admission did not exceed the number allowed since a party may serve an unlimited number of requests for admission.

(Choice C) Requests for admission are proper to obtain the truth about facts. But the reason that the patient's motion will be granted is that he proved the medication is unsafe for individuals in his age group—a fact the doctor denied.

📌 Educational Objective

A party that fails to admit a matter later proven true must generally pay the reasonable expenses incurred in making that proof.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(c)(2) (sanction for failure to admit).
  • 8B Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2290 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining the process to obtain a sanction for failure to admit).

zh-choices.A: 否，因为患者在陪审团作出裁决后提出的制裁（sanctions）动议不及时（untimely）。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为承认请求（requests for admission）的数量超出了允许的范围。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为承认请求（requests for admission）是获取事实真相的适当方式。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为患者证明了该事项属实。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery, disclosures, sanctions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：请求承认（request for admission）被拒后，若该事实后来被证明属实，法院通常要不要让对方赔你证明这件事的合理费用。

三秒认题路径：

请求承认 → 后来证明真 → 对方拒绝承认 → 费用转移 → 通常准许

核心法律规则

在 请求承认（request for admission） 里，对方可以被要求承认事实、法律适用到事实、意见，或文件真实性；答复通常要在 30 天内完成。考试上你要记住：它的作用不是“聊天”，而是把本来没争议的点提前锁死，省掉审判时重复举证。

如果一方拒绝承认的事项，后来又被证明是真的，提出请求的一方可以要求对方支付为证明该事项所花的合理费用，包括律师费。法院一般必须批准，除非有前置异议已被支持、事项不重要、对方有合理胜诉预期，或者有其他正当理由。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(c)(2) 是本题的直接规则来源；它锁定的就是“拒绝承认但后来被证明为真”时的费用转移。

思维导图

先看：对方有没有拒绝承认一个后来被证明为真的事项？
有医生否认“药物对患者年龄组更危险”
再看：这个事实后来有没有被陪审团证明为真？
有陪审团明确认定：该风险陈述为真
最后看：有没有三个常见挡箭牌之一？
没有前置异议未获支持 / 事项不重要 / 合理胜诉预期 / 其他正当理由
结论：费用制裁（sanctions）通常要准许，选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是“sanctions”，那是不是要看 timely、请求数量，或者对方有没有恶意。

但考试真正问的是：对方有没有把后来被证实为真的事项先前拒绝承认。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 陪审团已认定该事项为真，正好触发 拒绝承认后的费用转移；医生没有对应的免责理由，所以法院大概率准许。

❌ 事实误判 | 期限偷换

✕ A: 把 after the verdict 误当成太晚了；其实正是要等事实被证明后再申请。

❌ 法律适用 | 数量误套

✕ B: 以为请求承认有固定上限，其实联邦规则没有这个数量限制。

❌ 概念混淆 | 功能误读

✕ C: 只看到 obtain the truth，却漏掉本题真正要的是“拒绝承认后要不要赔钱”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“先拒绝、后证明真”，再查有没有免罚理由，别被题干里的医疗背景带跑。

考场速记

记住一句话：请求承认（request for admission）被拒后，若后来证明为真，通常就要赔证明这点的合理费用。

速记：拒绝承认 + 后来证真 = 费用转移。

highlights.text: moved for sanctions against the doctor to pay the reasonable expenses incurred in proving this matter

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A company sued a competitor in federal court, alleging that the competitor stole the company's trade secrets regarding its 3D printing technology. The company is concerned that discovery will lead to disclosure of its other trade secrets.
What is the most efficient strategy for the company to protect these trade secrets from disclosure?

choices.A: Assert that its trade secrets are privileged.
choices.B: File a motion for an ex parte temporary restraining order.
choices.C: Obtain a stipulation that limits the scope of discovery.
choices.D: Withhold information relating to its trade secrets.

questions.explanation:
Discovery stipulations (FRCP 29)
Depositions Parties may stipulate that depositions be taken:
  • before any person
  • at any time or place
  • on any notice
  • in any manner
Other discovery
procedures		 Parties may stipulate to modifications:
  • limiting scope of discovery
  • expanding limits set by other rules
  • extending time to complete particular requests*
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.
*Court approval required if extension would interfere with deadlines for completing all discovery, hearing a motion, or trial.

Parties can use various methods of discovery to obtain nonprivileged information that is relevant and proportional to the needs of the case. The broad scope of discovery requires disclosure of evidence that could be used at trial as well as information that may lead to the discovery of such evidence. As a result, it is possible that discovery could lead to the disclosure of the company's other trade secrets.

To protect that information from disclosure, the company could confer with the competitor to reach an agreement that modifies discovery rules and procedures. FRCP 29 allows the parties to stipulate to modifications that:

  • expand the limits imposed by rules governing discovery (eg, increase the number of interrogatories above 25)
  • extend the time to complete particular discovery requests (eg, allow more than 30 days to respond to a request for production) or
  • limit the scope of discovery (eg, bar discovery of certain materials—as the company seeks to do here).

A stipulation would be more efficient and less expensive than pursuing a motion to obtain a court order to modify the scope of discovery. Therefore, a stipulation is the most efficient strategy to prevent disclosure of the company's other trade secrets.

(Choice A) Trade secrets are not privileged, so this assertion could not be used to protect that information.

(Choice B) The company could file a motion for an ex parte temporary restraining order (TRO) to protect its other trade secrets from disclosure. But that would not be the most efficient strategy since an ex parte TRO generally remains in effect for only 14 days or until a preliminary-injunction hearing can take place—whichever occurs first.*

*An ex parte TRO automatically remains in effect for 14 days unless that time period is (1) shortened by the court or (2) extended by the court for good cause or based on the adverse party's consent.

(Choice D) Since the company's other trade secrets are likely discoverable, they cannot be withheld without a stipulation or court order that limits the scope of discovery.

📌 Educational Objective

Discovery stipulations between the parties are an efficient way to modify discovery rules and procedures. They can be used to (1) expand the limits imposed by discovery rules, (2) extend the time to complete particular discovery requests, or (3) limit the scope of discovery.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 29 (discovery stipulations).
  • 23 Am. Jur. 2d Depositions and Discovery § 10 (2019) (explaining stipulations regarding discovery).

一家公司在联邦法院起诉其竞争对手，指控该竞争对手窃取了其关于3D打印技术的商业秘密。该公司担心证据开示会导致其其他商业秘密被披露。

为保护这些商业秘密不被披露，该公司最有效的策略是什么？

zh-choices.A: 主张其商业秘密享有特免权。
zh-choices.B: 提交一项要求发布保护令的动议。
zh-choices.C: 获得一份限制证据开示范围的约定。
zh-choices.D: 拒绝提供与其商业秘密相关的信息。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery stipulations

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：当公司担心 发现程序（discovery） 会挖出其他商业秘密时，最省事的做法是不是先和对方达成 发现协议（discovery stipulation） 来限缩披露范围。

三秒认题路径：

发现要披露 → 怕秘密外流 → 先谈协议 → 限缩范围 → 选 C

核心法律规则

联邦民事诉讼规则第29条（FRCP 29） 允许双方用 发现协议（discovery stipulation） 改规则：可以 限制发现范围、扩大法定上限，也可以延长完成某项请求的时间。对这题来说，公司要挡住“别的商业秘密”被翻出来，最对路的是先和对方协商把范围缩小。

商业秘密（trade secrets） 不是当然特权（privileged）；所以不能靠“我这是特权”一句话直接挡住发现。强制令/临时限制令（TRO） 当然也可能救急，但考试问的是“最有效率”，而协议比上法院更快更省钱。

核心判例： 本题主要锁定 FRCP 29 的规则，不靠单独判例；考场记住：双方 stipulate 比先打动议更省时。

思维导图

起点
公司担心对方用 discovery 追到其他商业秘密
先做
和对方谈 discovery stipulation
可谈内容
limit 发现范围 / expand 上限 / 延长回复时间
卡死点
不是先争“是否特权”，也不是先跑去拿 TRO
答案
最省事：C 先达成限制发现范围的协议

考点陷阱

你可能会想：公司怕秘密泄露，那就赶紧找法院发 TRO（temporary restraining order） 或直接说“这是特权”。

但考试真正问的是：哪条路 最快、最省钱、最贴合发现规则，不是谁看起来更吓人。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 担心 discovery 继续扩散到其他 trade secrets，FRCP 29 允许双方协议直接 limit the scope of discovery，这最省事也最省钱。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 privileged 当万能盾，但商业秘密本身不是特权。

❌ 法律适用 | 救济路径误判

✕ B: 先冲 ex parte TRO 太重了，不是最有效率的第一步。

❌ 事实误判 | 直接拒交偷换

✕ D: 看到秘密就想 withhold，但可发现的材料不能这样硬挡。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找规则工具箱：能协商就先协商，别一上来就把问题升级成法院命令。

考场速记

速记：发现想限范围，先看 FRCP 29 能不能 stipulate；先谈协议，后打动议。记住一句：“Stipulate first, litigate later.”

reason.en: The context in which the trade secrets are at risk of being disclosed.

reason.en: The type of sensitive information the company wants to protect.

reason.en: Incorrectly suggests that trade secrets are immune from discovery under standard privilege rules.
reason.zh: 错误地暗示商业秘密在普通证据特权规则下可以豁免开示。

reason.en: Distractor proposing a temporary and inefficient emergency court order rather than a discovery agreement.
reason.zh: 提出了一个临时且低效的紧急法院命令，而非证据开示协议，属于干扰项。

reason.en: The correct and most efficient method to modify discovery rules by agreement under FRCP 29.
reason.zh: 联邦民事诉讼规则第29条下，双方通过协议修改开示规则的最有效方法。

reason.en: Incorrectly suggests a party can unilaterally refuse to disclose discoverable information without a court order or agreement.
reason.zh: 错误地暗示在没有法院命令或协议的情况下，当事人可以单方拒绝开示可开示的信息。

highlights.text: discovery will lead to disclosure of its other trade secrets

reason.en: Establishes the risk that needs to be mitigated through procedural means.
reason.zh: 确立了需要通过程序手段化解的泄露风险。

highlights.text: most efficient strategy

reason.en: Controls the choice between a party stipulation and a formal court motion.
reason.zh: 决定了在双方协议（stipulation）与正式向法院提交动议（motion）之间的选择。

highlights.text: protect these trade secrets from disclosure

reason.en: The specific objective that the chosen discovery strategy must accomplish.
reason.zh: 所选证据开示策略必须实现的具体目标。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
On March 1, 2017, a woman tripped and fell on a cruise ship, sustaining severe injuries. On February 28, 2018, she brought a diversity action in federal court against the entity she believed owned the cruise ship. The entity was served with process the same day. The entity immediately forwarded the complaint to the office of legal counsel for the corporation that owned the cruise ship.
Two weeks later, the entity filed and served its answer in which it denied ownership of the cruise ship. The entity explained that it was merely a ticketing agency with a name similar to the corporation that owned the ship.
The next day, the woman amended her complaint to substitute the corporation that owned the cruise ship as the defendant and had process served on the corporation. The corporation immediately moved to dismiss the suit, arguing that the statute of limitations had expired.
The applicable statute of limitations for the claim is one year from the date the accident allegedly occurred. The law establishing this statute of limitations does not mention relation back.
Should the court grant the corporation's motion to dismiss?

choices.A: No, because the amended complaint relates back to the date the original complaint was filed.
choices.B: No, because the woman may freely amend her complaint once as a matter of course.
choices.C: Yes, because the amended complaint was filed after the statute of limitations expired.
choices.D: Yes, because the applicable law does not mention relation back.

questions.explanation:
Relation-back doctrine
(FRCP 15(c))
No amendment after statute of limitations expired unless:

Asserts new claim

Statute of limitations allows relation back
OR
New claim arises from same transaction or occurrence as original pleading

Changes party

Statute of limitations allows relation back
OR
Concerns same transaction or occurrence as original pleading and:
• new party receives notice of suit within 90 days of original filing and
• new party knew (or should have known) he/she would be sued
Relation back permitted

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

An amended complaint filed after the statute of limitations has expired is prohibited unless the relation-back doctrine applies. This doctrine treats the amended complaint as if it were filed on the same date as the original complaint. An amendment that changes a defendant "relates back" only if the statute of limitations allows (not seen here) OR when:

  • the amendment concerns the same transaction or occurrence as the original complaint
  • the new party received notice of the suit within 90 days after the original complaint was filed and
  • the new party knew or should have known the suit would have been brought against it but for a mistake about the proper party's identity.

Here, the woman's amended complaint concerns the same cruise ship accident. The corporation that owns the cruise ship received notice when the ticketing agency forwarded the complaint. And the corporation should have known that the suit would have been brought against it but for the woman's mistake about its identity. As a result, the amendment relates back to the date the original complaint was filed on February 28, 2018—before the statute of limitations expired. Therefore, the corporation's motion to dismiss should be denied (Choices C & D).

(Choice B) A party may amend its complaint once as a matter of course—ie, without the court's permission or the opposing party's written consent—within 21 days after being served with an answer. But the amendment must be filed (or relate back to an original pleading filed) before the statute of limitations expires.

📌 Educational Objective

An amended complaint will "relate back" to the date of the original complaint if (1) the same occurrence is at issue, (2) the new party received notice of the suit within 90 days after the original complaint was filed, and (3) the new party knew or should have known the suit would have been brought but for a mistake about its identity.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(c) (relation back of amended pleadings).
  • Krupski v. Costa Crociere S.p.A., 560 U.S. 538, 557 (2010) (holding that the relation-back doctrine applies when a company should have known that it would have been sued had the plaintiff not made a mistake).
questions.zh-question:
2017年3月1日，一名女子在一艘游轮上绊倒摔伤，导致重伤。2018年2月28日，她在联邦法院对她认为拥有该游轮的实体提起了多元化管辖诉讼（diversity action）。该实体于同日被送达传票（served with process）。该实体立即将诉状（complaint）转交给了拥有该游轮的公司的法律顾问办公室。
两周后，该实体提交并送达了其答辩状（answer），否认拥有该游轮。该实体解释说，它只是一个票务代理机构，其名称与拥有该船的公司相似。
次日，该女子修改了她的诉状（amended her complaint），将拥有该游轮的公司替换为被告，并向该公司送达了传票（served process）。该公司立即动议驳回诉讼（moved to dismiss the suit），理由是诉讼时效（statute of limitations）已过。
该索赔适用的诉讼时效为事故发生之日起一年。规定此诉讼时效的法律未提及溯及（relation back）。
法院是否应准许该公司的驳回诉讼动议？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为修改后的诉状可溯及（relates back）到原诉状提交之日。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该女子可以作为当然权利（as a matter of course）自由修改其诉状一次。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为修改后的诉状是在诉讼时效届满后提交的。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为适用法律未提及溯及（relation back）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Pleadings

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：修改起诉状（amended complaint）在诉讼时效（statute of limitations）过期后，能不能靠关系追溯（relation back）把新被告拉回原始起诉日。

三秒认题路径：

时效已过 → 换被告 → 同一事故 → 90天通知 → 可追溯

核心法律规则

FRCP 15(c)的意思很直接：原告在时效过后改诉状，不是一定死掉；如果新主张或新被告和原案是同一transaction or occurrence，而且新被告在原起诉后90天内收到通知，就可能relation back。knew or should have known 的考场意思：这个人应当意识到，原告只是认错了身份，真正该被告的是它。Krupski v. Costa Crociere S.p.A.告诉你：关键看被告是否该知道自己本来就会被告，不是看原告主观多笨。

核心判例： Krupski v. Costa Crociere S.p.A. — 原告把船东认错，但真正船东已及时收到通知并应知会被告，故可追溯。

思维导图

原始起诉 2018/2/28，时效截止前
→
误告被告 把票务代理当船东
→
真实船东 同一事故 + 收到通知
→
90天内通知 代理转交给法务
→
关系追溯成立 改诉状按原日计算
卡点只有一个：新被告有没有被及时通知，并知道自己本来就该被告？
有：同一轮事故 + 90天内通知 + 知道是认错人
结论：改诉状回到原起诉日，时效不拦
别被“已经过了一年”吓住：只要 relation back 成立，时效按原始起诉日算。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然statute of limitations已经过了，而且新被告是后来才加进来的，那就一定输。

但考试真正问的是：relation back能不能把改诉状“拉回去”到原始起诉日；这题不是看形式上什么时候改名，而是看新被告有没有及时收到通知、有没有看出自己本来就该被告。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 同一游轮事故、90天内收到通知、且真实船东应知是认错人，所以改诉状可追溯到2018年2月28日，时效被救回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 自由修改误判

✕ B: 把 once as a matter 当成时效通行证了。

❌ 法律适用 | 只看过期日

✕ C: 只盯着已过时效，忽略了 relation back 这一救命门。

❌ 事实误判 | 没看通知事实

✕ D: 把 does not mention 误读成“绝对不能追溯”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否换被告，再抓“同一事故 + 90天通知 + 认错身份”三件套。

考场速记

记忆口诀：同一事故，90天通知，认错身份，关系追溯。 这题看到“改被告 + 时效过期”，先别急着判死刑，先查 FRCP 15(c)。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A pedestrian sued an out-of-state driver in a federal district court for allegedly hitting the pedestrian in a crosswalk, which the pedestrian claims resulted in $1 million in medical expenses, lost wages, and pain and suffering. The driver filed an answer denying liability.
Which of the following must the pedestrian automatically provide the driver without waiting for a discovery request?

choices.A: A copy of the pedestrian's medical bills for her alleged injuries.
choices.B: A copy of the pedestrian's medical insurance agreement.
choices.C: A list of the cases in which the pedestrian has been a witness over the previous four years.
choices.D: The name of a witness who knows about the driver's past car accidents.

questions.explanation:
Required discovery disclosures
(FRCP 26(a))
Type Required disclosures Time to disclose
Initial disclosures*
  • Persons with relevant information
  • Items in party's possession that support claim/defense
  • Computation of damages & supporting material
  • Relevant insurance policies
  • ≤ 14 days after initial planning conference
  • ≤ 30 days after post-conference service or joinder
  • As court orders or parties stipulate
Expert testimony
  • Identity of expert witnesses
  • Expert's written report
  • If no report, subject matter & summary of testimony
  • ≥ 90 days before trial
  • ≤ 30 days after disclosure to rebut evidence
  • As court orders or parties stipulate
Pretrial disclosures*
  • Testifying witnesses
  • Deposition testimony to be used at trial
  • Documents/exhibits to be used at trial
  • ≥ 30 days before trial
  • As court orders
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.
*Does not apply to evidence used solely for impeachment.

Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(a), parties are required to make initial disclosures, disclosures of expert testimony, and pretrial disclosures even without a discovery request. A party must initially disclose:

  • the name, address, and phone number of persons with relevant information that the party may use to support a claim or defense
  • all documents, electronically stored information, and tangible things in the party's possession that the party may use to support a claim or defense
  • any insurance agreement with a company that may be liable for all or part of any judgment and
  • a computation of damages and the materials on which it was based.

All of this information must be disclosed within 14 days after the initial planning conference or by a date set by the court or parties.* Here, since part of the pedestrian's damages are based on her medical expenses, she must provide the driver with a copy of her medical bills without waiting for a discovery request.

*If a party is added after the initial planning conference, initial disclosures must be made within 30 days after service or joinder of that party.

(Choice B) The pedestrian does not need to provide a copy of her health insurance agreement because her insurance company will not be liable. Instead, the driver must provide his automobile insurance agreement because his insurance company may be liable for the pedestrian's damages.

(Choice C) A testifying expert witness (not seen here) must disclose a written report that lists the cases in which the witness has testified over the past four years. But this is only required if the witness (1) is a specially hired expert or (2) regularly gives expert testimony as part of his/her employment duties with the party.

(Choice D) Testimony from a witness who knows about the driver's past driving habits may be used to impeach the driver's trial testimony. But initial disclosures do not apply to witnesses or evidence used solely for impeachment.

📌 Educational Objective

A party's initial disclosures must include (1) persons and items that the party may use to support a claim or defense, (2) any insurance agreement with a company that may be liable, and (3) a computation of damages and the materials on which it was based.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(1) (required initial disclosures).

在未收到证据开示请求的情况下，该行人必须自动向司机提供以下哪项？

zh-choices.A: 该行人声称受伤所产生的医疗账单副本。
zh-choices.B: 该行人的医疗保险协议副本。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Mandatory disclosures

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：初始披露（initial disclosures）里，哪些材料必须在不等对方要的情况下自动交出来。

三秒认题路径：

FRCP 26(a) → 自动披露 → 医疗账单 → 计算损害 → 选 A

核心法律规则

联邦民事诉讼规则 26(a)（FRCP 26(a)）要求当事人自动披露几类信息：能支持主张或抗辩的人员、能支持主张或抗辩的文件/有形物、保险协议（insurance agreement），以及损害计算（computation of damages）和其依据材料。

考试意思：只要题干在问“without waiting for a discovery request”，你就去找这些初始披露清单，不要先想专家证人或庭审证据规则。

核心判例： 本题不靠判例展开，直接按 FRCP 26(a)(1) 的法条清单做题；医疗账单属于损害计算的依据材料，所以要自动交。

思维导图

先问：这是“自动披露”还是“等对方请求”？
题干触发：受伤 + 医疗费 + 要求“自动提供”
规则关卡：FRCP 26(a) 初始披露清单
卡死点：损害计算及其依据材料 → 医疗账单要交
排除项：保险协议看“可能承担赔偿责任”的公司；专家名单、证人背景、纯弹劾证据都不是这题主轴
结论：选 A，不用等 discovery request。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：B 说的是insurance agreement，好像只要和保险有关都该交。

但考试真正问的是：这个保险协议是不是和可能对判决负责的公司有关；原告自己的健康保险通常不是这里的自动披露对象。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的medical expenses就是损害计算（computation of damages）的依据材料，所以医疗账单必须自动披露。

❌ 法律适用 | 保险对象错位

✕ B: 把原告自己的health insurance当成要交的保险协议，方向错了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 专家披露误判

✕ C: 这是expert witness才会碰到的披露，不是普通当事人的初始披露。

❌ 事实误判 | 弹劾用途偷换

✕ D: 题干问的是支持主张的自动披露，不是只拿来impeach 的证人线索。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否属于 FRCP 26(a) 清单，再把“损害计算”和“保险协议”逐项对号入座。

考场速记

记住一句：初始披露（initial disclosures）要自动交四类东西——人、文件、保险、损害计算；看到医疗账单，先想“这是损害依据”，通常就是 A。

口诀：人-物-保-损，四个字先扫一遍，再决定要不要等对方来要。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
The attorney for a woman who owned a joint bank account with a co-owner filed a motion for a temporary restraining order that would prohibit the bank from releasing funds from the account to the co-owner for 14 days. The motion stated that the attorney had not made an effort to notify the co-owner because the co-owner had threatened to withdraw all of the money in the account and abscond with the money to a foreign country. The attorney certified this information in a document submitted with the motion. The motion was accompanied by an affidavit by the woman asserting that the co-owner made this threat to her personally and that she believes the co-owner will carry it out.
Can the court issue the temporary restraining order without notice to the co-owner?

choices.A: No, because a temporary restraining order cannot issue without notice to the adverse party.
choices.B: No, because the attorney failed to make an effort to give the co-owner notice of the motion for a temporary restraining order.
choices.C: Yes, because a temporary restraining order does not require notice to an adverse party if the order is for no more than 14 days.
choices.D: Yes, because the co-owner's threat justifies the issuance of the temporary restraining order without notice to the co-owner.

questions.explanation:
Preliminary relief
(FRCP 65)
Type Required contents Effect
Preliminary injunction Notice of hearing
  • State reasons issued
  • Reasonably describe acts restrained or required
  • Specify terms
 Persons bound upon receiving actual notice of order:
  • parties to the case
  • parties' officers, agents, employees & attorneys
  • anyone in active concert/participation with above persons
Temporary restraining order Ex parte
(no notice)
Above requirements plus:
  • date & hour issued
  • why injury is irreparable
  • why issued without notice
  • promptly filed with clerk & entered into record
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A temporary restraining order (TRO) is a court order commanding a party to do or stop doing a specified action for 14 days or until a preliminary-injunction hearing can take place, whichever occurs first. This preserves the parties' status quo until the court can fully consider the issue at a hearing. Unlike a preliminary injunction, a TRO may be issued without a hearing or notice to the adverse party (Choice A)—but only if:

  • the movant can establish under written oath (i.e., via affidavit or verified complaint) that she will suffer immediate and irreparable harm before the nonmovant can be heard and
  • the movant's attorney certifies in writing any efforts made to give notice and the reasons why notice should not be required.

Here, the woman's attorney moved for a TRO to prohibit the bank from releasing funds to the co-owner of a joint bank account after the co-owner threatened to withdraw all the money and flee the country. The affidavit accompanying the motion shows that the woman would suffer immediate and irreparable harm prior to a TRO hearing because the co-owner would likely carry out the threat. Therefore, the court can issue the TRO without notice to the co-owner because it is justified by the co-owner's threat.

(Choice B) An attorney need not make an effort to give the adverse party notice of a motion for a TRO for the court to issue the TRO without notice. But if an attorney does make such an effort, it must be certified in writing.

(Choice C) A TRO is generally limited to 14 days, unless good cause exists or the adversary consents. But notice is required regardless of the length of the TRO, unless the requirements set forth above are satisfied.

📌 Educational Objective

A temporary restraining order can be issued without notice or a hearing if (1) the movant establishes under written oath that she will suffer immediate and irreparable harm before the nonmovant can be heard and (2) the movant's attorney certifies in writing any efforts made to give notice and why notice should not be required.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(b) (requirements for ex parte TRO).
  • 11A Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2952 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining the process for issuing an ex parte TRO).

一位与他人共同拥有联名银行账户的女性的律师，提交了一份临时限制令（temporary restraining order）动议，旨在禁止银行在14天内向该联名账户的共同所有人发放资金。该动议指出，律师未曾努力通知该共同所有人，因为该共同所有人曾威胁要提取账户中所有资金并携款潜逃至国外。律师在随动议提交的一份文件中证明了此信息。该动议还附有该女性的一份宣誓书（affidavit），其中声明该共同所有人曾亲自向她发出此威胁，且她相信该共同所有人会付诸实施。
法院能否在不通知该共同所有人的情况下发出该临时限制令？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为未经通知对方当事人（adverse party），临时限制令不得发出。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为律师未能努力向该共同所有人发出关于临时限制令动议的通知。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为如果临时限制令的期限不超过14天，则无需通知对方当事人。
zh-choices.D: 能，因为该共同所有人的威胁证明了在不通知该共同所有人的情况下发出临时限制令的合理性。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Preliminary injunctions & TROs

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：临时限制令（temporary restraining order, TRO）能不能在无通知（without notice / ex parte）的情况下签发。

三秒认题路径：

TRO → 无通知 → 立即损害 → 律师书面证明 → 可签发

核心法律规则

只背这条就够做题

TRO（temporary restraining order）一般只维持 14 天，关键不在天数，而在能否先不通知对方先救急。

按 FRCP 65(b)，法院可以无通知签发 ex parte TRO，前提是：一，宣誓材料要写明申请人会在对方被听取前遭受立即且不可弥补的损害（immediate and irreparable harm）；二，律师要书面证明自己做过哪些通知努力，以及为什么不应要求通知。

所以这题只看一句：immediate and irreparable harm 有，而且律师也把没通知的理由写进书面材料里，法院就能先下 TRO。

规则抓手： FRCP 65(b) 锁定 ex parte TRO 的两步门槛：先看紧急性，再看律师书面证明。

思维导图

要先不通知就签 TRO？
先看 1：是否有立即且不可弥补的损害（immediate and irreparable harm）？
有：对方要把钱全取走并逃到外国，等到开庭就来不及了。
再看 2：律师是否书面证明（certify in writing）通知努力和不通知理由？
有：已提交书面说明，说明未通知的努力与原因。
结论：两个门槛都过 → 法院可无通知签发 TRO → 选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：14 days 这么短，或者“没通知就不公平”，所以应该不能签。

但考试真正问的是：是不是已经满足 FRCP 65(b) 的无通知门槛，不是看你直觉上觉得程序“太突然”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 co-owner threatened to withdraw all the money and flee，配合宣誓书与律师书面说明，正好满足无通知 TRO 的两个门槛。

❌ 概念混淆 | 14日误判

✕ A: 把 cannot issue without notice 当成绝对规则了。

❌ 法律适用 | 通知努力误判

✕ B: 以为没先打招呼就必死，但律师的书面证明已经把理由补上了。

❌ 事实误判 | 天数偷换

✕ C: 只盯着 14 days，忽略了无通知还要看紧急损害与书面证明。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓 TRO 的无通知例外，再核对宣誓书和律师书面证明两项门槛。

考场速记

记住：TRO 不是“必须通知”，而是“能不能在紧急时先不通知”。口诀：“先看急不急，再看律师写没写。”

碰到中间上诉再想另一句：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，但这题不靠上诉例外，靠的是 FRCP 65(b)。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A homeowner brought a diversity action against a mining company in federal court for negligence, claiming that the company's negligent mining practices caused extensive damage to her property. Forty-five days before trial, the homeowner sent the company the evidence that she plans to use at trial, including a witness whose testimony she intends to present by deposition. The homeowner also attached a transcript of the pertinent depositions. Twenty-one days later, the company objected to the use of the deposition testimony on the ground that it is inadmissible hearsay.
Should the court hear the merits of the company's objection?

choices.A: No, because the company failed to object at least 30 days before trial.
choices.B: No, because the company failed to object within 14 days after the homeowner disclosed the deposition testimony she intended to use at trial.
choices.C: Yes, because the company objected within 30 days after the homeowner disclosed the deposition testimony she intended to use at trial.
choices.D: Yes, because the homeowner failed to disclose the deposition testimony at least 90 days before trial.

questions.explanation:
Required disclosures timeline

≤ 14 days after
≥ 90 days before
≥ 30 days before
≤ 14 days after
Initial planning conference
Initial disclosures
Expert testimony
Pretrial disclosures
Objections to pretrial disclosures
Trial begins

During discovery, parties must automatically disclose certain information through required disclosures.

This includes pretrial disclosures, which must contain the following:

  • The name, address, and phone number of each witness, separately identifying witnesses expected to testify at trial and those who may be called if the need arises
  • The designation of witnesses whose testimony will be presented by deposition, including a transcript of the pertinent parts of a deposition that was not taken stenographically (ie, by shorthand)
  • All documents and exhibits, separately identifying items expected to be offered as evidence and those that may be offered if the need arises

These must be disclosed at least 30 days before trial. Any objections to the use at trial of deposition testimony, documents, or exhibits must be made within 14 days after the disclosures.* An objection not made within this time is waived unless (1) excused by the court for good cause or (2) the objection is based on relevance.

Here, the homeowner timely disclosed 45 days before trial the witness whose deposition testimony she intends to present at trial and attached the deposition transcript. The company untimely objected 21 days later to the use of the deposition testimony at trial. There is no indication that the company's untimely objection is excused by good cause, and the objection is based on hearsay—not relevance. Therefore, the company waived its objection, and the court should not hear the merits of the objection (Choice C).

*A court may also set different deadlines for the parties to make pretrial disclosures and object to such disclosures.

(Choice C) The company waived its objection, and the court should not hear the merits of the objection.

(Choice A) Pretrial disclosures, not objections to such disclosures, must be made at least 30 days before trial. Objections to pretrial disclosures must instead be made within 14 days after the disclosures.

(Choice D) Expert witness testimony, not pretrial disclosures, must be disclosed at least 90 days before trial.

📌 Educational Objective

Pretrial disclosures must be made at least 30 days before trial. Objections to the use at trial of disclosed deposition testimony, documents, or exhibits must be made within 14 days after the disclosures or such objections are generally waived.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(3) (pretrial disclosures).
  • 8A Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2054 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining when pretrial disclosures and objections to such disclosures must be made).
questions.zh-question:
一位房主因疏忽向联邦法院对一家矿业公司提起了多元管辖权诉讼，声称该公司的疏忽采矿行为对她的财产造成了重大损害。在审判前四十五天，房主向该公司发送了她计划在审判中使用的证据，包括一名她打算通过书面证词（deposition）方式呈现其证言的证人。房主还附上了相关书面证词的誊本。二十一天后，该公司以该书面证词证言是不可采纳的传闻为由，反对使用该证言。

法院是否应审理该公司反对意见的实体内容？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为该公司未能在审判前至少30天内提出反对。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为在该房主披露她打算在审判中使用的书面证词证言后，该公司未能在14天内提出反对。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为在该房主披露她打算在审判中使用的书面证词证言后，该公司在30天内提出了反对。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为房主未能在审判前至少90天披露该书面证词证言。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Mandatory disclosures

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：预审披露（pretrial disclosures）后的14天异议期限，过了就通常弃权，法院不再听实体理由。

三秒认题路径：

预审披露 → 14天异议 → 超时了 → 弃权 → 不听实体

核心法律规则

在联邦民诉里，预审披露（pretrial disclosures）必须在开庭前至少30天（at least 30 days before trial）完成。对已披露的证言笔录（deposition testimony）、文件或展品提出异议，必须在披露后14天内（within 14 days after the disclosures）提出。

如果你没在这个窗口内提出，除非有good cause或异议本来就是relevance问题，否则异议通常waived。这题里，真正决定能不能听的是“异议有没有按时提”，不是“证言是不是传闻”。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(3) — 直接锁定：披露30天前，异议14天内；超期就一般弃权。

思维导图

T-45天
原告先做了预审披露（pretrial disclosures），把要用的证人和deposition transcript交出来。
T-14天内
被告要在披露后14天内提异议；这一步才是“能不能保住反对权”的关口。
T+21天
超时异议：已经晚了，除非有 good cause 或是 relevance。
结论
传闻抗辩被弃权 → 法院不该听实体异议。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然对方说的是 hearsay，那法院当然应该先看证据能不能进。

但考试真正问的是：异议有没有在披露后14天内提出。程序期限先卡死，法院才不会再进到实体证据问题。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干显示原告已在开庭前45天做pretrial disclosures，被告却21天后才反对；14天窗口已过，所以异议通常弃权。

❌ 法律适用 | 期限对象搞反

✕ A: 把30 days误当成异议期限了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 先后顺序错置

✕ C: 看到“30天内”就以为还能反对，披露后14天才是关键。

❌ 事实误判 | 90天规则偷换

✕ D: 把expert testimony那套90天期限硬搬到普通预审披露。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定程序窗口，再看是否超期；别被“传闻”带去证据法。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“披露30天前，异议14天内；过期就弃权，先看时间再看理由。”

遇到这类题先记住：程序期限优先，实体争点后看；别把“能不能反对”与“反对有没有道理”混为一谈。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A consumer, from State A, properly brought a federal diversity action against a retailer, from State B, based on strict products liability. The consumer was injured when the lock switch on a ladder purchased from the retailer malfunctioned, causing the consumer to fall and seriously injure himself. After being served with the consumer's complaint and filing an answer, the retailer filed a third-party claim under Rule 14 against the manufacturer of the ladder, incorporated and with its principal place of business in State A. The retailer claimed that the manufacturer would be liable to the retailer for the retailer's liability, if any, on the consumer's claim. The consumer then filed an additional claim against the manufacturer based on the defective ladder. In response to the consumer's claim, the manufacturer asserted a defense based on federal law.
Can the court exercise jurisdiction over the consumer's claim against the manufacturer?

choices.A: Yes, based on diversity jurisdiction.
choices.B: Yes, based on federal-question jurisdiction.
choices.C: Yes, based on supplemental jurisdiction.
choices.D: No.

questions.explanation:
Barred supplemental claims in diversity-jurisdiction cases
(28 U.S.C. § 1367(b))
When original subject-matter jurisdiction is based on diversity jurisdiction, these supplemental claims are barred:
  • Claims by existing plaintiffs against parties added through:
    • impleader (FRCP 14)
    • compulsory joinder (FRCP 19)
    • permissive joinder (FRCP 20)
    • intervention (FRCP 24)
  • Claims by persons seeking to join as plaintiffs through compulsory joinder or intervention
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A federal court can consider the merits of a claim only if the court has subject-matter jurisdiction, which can arise under:

  • federal-question jurisdiction – when a claim—but not a defense—arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or federal law
  • diversity jurisdiction – when the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 and the opposing parties are citizens of different states or
  • supplemental jurisdiction – when a claim that does not independently satisfy federal-question or diversity jurisdiction arises from the same transaction or occurrence as another claim over which the court has federal-question or diversity jurisdiction.

However, if the plaintiff's original claim arises under diversity jurisdiction, a court is statutorily barred from exercising supplemental jurisdiction over a claim made by the plaintiff against a party added though compulsory joinder (FRCP 19), permissive joinder (FRCP 20), intervention (FRCP 24), or impleader (FRCP 14).

Here, the consumer's original strict products liability claim against the retailer is based on diversity jurisdiction. The retailer then filed a third-party claim against the manufacturer through FRCP 14 impleader, and the consumer filed an additional claim against the manufacturer. However, the federal court does not have subject-matter jurisdiction over the consumer's claim against the impleaded manufacturer because:

  • even though the manufacturer asserted a defense based on federal law, the consumer's additional claim based on the defective ladder arises under state law (i.e., no federal-question jurisdiction) (Choice B)
  • the consumer and the manufacturer are both citizens of State A since the consumer is from State A and the manufacturer is incorporated and has its principal place of business there (i.e., no diversity jurisdiction) (Choice A) and
  • the court cannot exercise supplemental jurisdiction over the impleader claim asserted by the consumer (plaintiff) (i.e., no supplemental jurisdiction) (Choice C).

Therefore, the court cannot exercise jurisdiction over the consumer's claim against the manufacturer.

📌 Educational Objective

Subject-matter jurisdiction can arise under federal-question jurisdiction, diversity jurisdiction, or supplemental jurisdiction. However, if the original claim is based on diversity jurisdiction, a court is statutorily barred from exercising supplemental jurisdiction over a claim made by a plaintiff against a party added through impleader.

📚 References
  • 28 U.S.C. §1367 (supplemental jurisdiction).
questions.zh-question: 一位来自A州的消费者，基于严格产品责任（strict products liability），对一位来自B州的零售商提起了适当的联邦多元化管辖权诉讼（federal diversity action）。该消费者从零售商处购买的梯子锁扣开关失灵，导致其摔倒并受重伤。在被送达消费者起诉状并提交答辩状后，零售商根据《联邦民事诉讼规则》第14条（Rule 14）对梯子制造商提起了第三方索赔（third-party claim），该制造商在A州注册成立并拥有主要营业地。零售商主张，如果零售商对消费者的索赔负有责任，制造商应对零售商承担责任。随后，消费者基于有缺陷的梯子向制造商提起了额外的索赔。作为对消费者索赔的回应，制造商提出了基于联邦法律的抗辩。法院能否对消费者针对制造商的索赔行使管辖权？

zh-choices.A: 是，基于多元化管辖权（diversity jurisdiction）。
zh-choices.B: 是，基于联邦问题管辖权（federal-question jurisdiction）。
zh-choices.C: 是，基于补充管辖权（supplemental jurisdiction）。
zh-choices.D: 否。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：原告在多元管辖起诉后，能不能借 补充管辖（supplemental jurisdiction） 再去告一个被 Rule 14 介入（impleader） 拉进来的第三方。

三秒认题路径：

多元起诉 → 原告再告新被告 → 该人是介入进来 → §1367(b) 卡死 → 不能管

核心法律规则

联邦法院只有在有 标的管辖权（subject-matter jurisdiction） 时，才可以审理实体争议。这里原告最初靠的是 多元管辖（diversity jurisdiction），所以要先看 28 U.S.C. § 1367(b)。

考试意思：如果原告想对通过 Rule 14 介入（impleader） 进来的新当事人再加一条主张，法院通常不能用补充管辖帮忙，因为国会在多元案件里故意把这类原告主张堵住了。

本题里，消费者对制造商的索赔既没有单独的多元管辖，也不是原告起诉时自带的联邦问题；制造商自己提了 federal law 抗辩，也不能把原告的州法产品责任请求变成联邦问题。

核心判例： § 1367(b) 的法条规则直接锁定本题：原告对通过 impleader 加进来的第三方，不能借补充管辖绕过多元管辖门槛。

思维导图

先问：原告最初案件有 多元管辖（diversity） 吗？
YES 继续看 § 1367(b) 的限制名单。
原告要告的是谁？
通过 Rule 14 impleader 拉进来的制造商
结论：原告对该第三方的追加请求被法条挡住，不能用补充管辖补票。
NO 那就回去找别的独立管辖基础。
再问：有没有独立的 联邦问题管辖（federal-question jurisdiction） 或新的多元管辖？
本题 都没有：原告主张是州法，双方还是同州公民。
终点：不能行使管辖 → 选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：制造商都拿出 federal law 抗辩了，是不是就有联邦问题管辖。

但考试真正问的是：原告这条追加请求本身有没有独立管辖基础；抗辩是防守，不会把州法索赔变成联邦问题。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

消费者对制造商的追加请求没有独立 多元管辖，又被 § 1367(b) 对原告针对 impleader 当事人的补充管辖限制挡住，所以法院不能管。

❌ 概念混淆 | 联邦问题误套

✕ A: 把制造商的州民身份忽略了，还想硬凑多元管辖。

❌ 法律适用 | 抗辩变管辖

✕ B: 看到 federal law 就当成起诉依据了，抗辩不等于联邦问题。

❌ 事实误判 | 补充管辖偷放

✕ C: 把 § 1367 当成原告对第三方的通行证，但多元案件里原告这一步被法条专门排除。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁原告最初的管辖基础，再看追加对象是不是 § 1367(b) 明禁的那一类。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”是中间上诉的记忆法；但这题不是上诉题，真正要记的是：多元案件里，原告不能靠补充管辖去告被 Rule 14 拉进来的第三方。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A designer sued a clothing store in a federal district court for selling clothes that featured the designer's trademarked designs without the designer's permission. As the trial approached, the judge ordered the parties' attorneys to attend a final pretrial conference.
Which of the following can the judge NOT do at the conference?

choices.A: Decide which party has the burden of proof.
choices.B: Establish a time limit for each party's presentation of evidence.
choices.C: Limit each party's use of expert testimony.
choices.D: Rule on the admissibility of evidence.

questions.explanation:
Pretrial conferences
(FRCP 16(c))
Purpose Matters for consideration
Expedite litigation
  • Eliminate frivolous claims & defenses
  • Obtain admissions & stipulations
  • Set timeline for summary judgment & dispose of pending motions
  • Schedule discovery, pretrial briefs & future conferences
Improve quality of trial
  • Amend pleadings
  • Refer matters to magistrate or master
  • Require separate trial for different claims
  • Adopt special procedures for complex/unusual legal issues
  • Rule on admissibility of evidence
  • Avoid cumulative evidence & limit expert testimony
  • Establish order & time limit for presentation of evidence
Facilitate settlement Facilitate just, speedy & inexpensive resolution
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16 permits a judge to order the attorneys and any unrepresented parties to attend one or more pretrial conferences. These conferences are designed to expedite litigation, improve the trial's quality, and facilitate settlement. During these conferences, the judge has broad discretion to consider and act on a wide range of issues, including:

• establishing a time limit for each party's presentation of evidence (Choice B)

• limiting each party's use of expert testimony (Choice C) and

• ruling on the admissibility of evidence (Choice D).

However, the judge may not decide which party has the burden of proof. That is because a plaintiff (here, the designer) always has the burden to prove each element of the claim, often by a preponderance of the evidence.

📌 Educational Objective

During pretrial conferences, the judge has broad discretion to act on a wide range of issues—eg, (1) establish a time limit for each party's presentation of evidence, (2) limit each party's use of expert testimony, and (3) rule on the admissibility of evidence. However, the judge may not decide which party has the burden of proof.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 16 (pretrial conferences).

一名设计师向联邦地区法院起诉一家服装店，因其未经设计师许可，销售带有该设计师商标设计的服装。随着审判的临近，法官命令双方律师参加最终的审前会议。

在该会议上，法官不能做下列哪项？

zh-choices.A: 决定哪一方承担举证责任。
zh-choices.B: 为各方出示证据设定时间限制。
zh-choices.C: 限制各方使用专家证言。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Case management

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：预审会议（pretrial conference）里，法官能管诉讼推进和证据安排，但不能改掉本来就由原告承担的举证责任（burden of proof）。

三秒认题路径：

预审会议 → 法官权限 → 能管程序 → 不能改举证责任 → 选 A

核心法律规则

《联邦民事诉讼规则》16(c)（FRCP 16(c)）允许法官在pretrial conference上处理很多“管案件怎么打”的事，考场意思：先把诉讼推进、证据顺序、专家证人、证据可采性这些细节定下来。

法官可以决定time limit for presentation of evidence、限制expert testimony，也可以直接裁定admissibility of evidence；但法官不能把burden of proof从本来该承担的一方身上挪走。

考场意思：谁来证明案子的要件，是实体法和起诉结构决定的，不是预审会议上法官临时“分配”的。

核心判例： 本题不需要背额外判例；直接按 FRCP 16(c) 的会议权限表判断即可。

思维导图

起点
进入 final pretrial conference
先看法官“能管什么”
可管
证据时间限制
专家证言限制
证据可采性裁定
卡死点
不能改 burden of proof
这不是会议权限
结论
选项 A 错
B / C / D 都是法官可做

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是最后一次庭前会议，法官是不是能把整个案件的胜负规则都顺手定了，包括谁负举证责任。

但考试真正问的是：pretrial conference 只能管诉讼管理和证据安排，不能替实体法重分“谁来证明”。

司法考试看的是「法官程序上能不能管」，而不是「案件到底谁更像会赢」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干点出 final pretrial conference，法官可管证据和进度，但不能改原告本来就要承担的举证责任。

❌ 事实误判 | 会议权限看漏

✕ B: 看到 time limit 就以为超权，其实这正是会议常规权限。

❌ 法律适用 | 专家规则错位

✕ C: 把 expert testimony 当成禁区，但规则明示可以限制。

❌ 概念混淆 | 证据裁定误解

✕ D: 以为 admissibility 只能开庭再说，其实预审会上也能先裁。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓会议权限清单，再排除“改实体负担”这种越界选项。

考场速记

记住一句：pretrial conference 里，法官能管“怎么审”，不能改“谁证明”。

顺手背：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉例外口诀，但这题不是上诉题，别跑偏。
