questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
Two women filed a joint complaint in federal court against their employer for allegedly violating a federal law that prohibits workplace discrimination against pregnant women.
The complaint alleged that the women applied for promotion to two, newly opened supervisor positions when they were six and seven months pregnant, respectively. The women claimed that their employer told each of them separately that he was denying them the promotion because they would miss work as a result of their pregnancies. The complaint also alleged that the women were fired from their positions shortly after these meetings. One woman seeks to be reinstated to her former position, while the other woman requests $100,000 in damages.
The employer denied these allegations and filed a motion asking the court to sever the women's claims.
How will the court likely rule on the employer's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the women are required parties to the lawsuit.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the women's claims arise out of the same series of occurrences and share common questions of law and fact.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the women requested different relief.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because trying both women's claims together would prejudice the employer.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Joinder of parties
Compulsory
joinder
(FRCP 19) 		Person must be joined in lawsuit—provided subject matter jurisdiction is preserved—
if absence will:
  • prevent court from granting complete relief to existing parties
  • prejudice absent person's interest or
  • subject existing party to multiple or inconsistent obligations
Permissive
joinder
(FRCP 20) 		Person may be joined in lawsuit if:
  • claims by or against person arise out of same transaction/occurrence and
  • common question of fact or law will arise
FRCP = Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

The employer's motion to sever the women's complaint should be granted if their claims regarding workplace discrimination were improperly joined. Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 20—the permissive joinder rule—multiple persons may be joined as plaintiffs or defendants in the same suit if:

• the claims asserted by or against the joined parties arise out of the same transaction, occurrence, or series of transactions or occurrences and

• the action will involve a common question of law or fact among all joined parties.

Here, the claims asserted by both women stem from their mutual employer's alleged discrimination (same series of occurrences). Their claims are based on the same federal statute (common question of law) and the same allegation that they were denied a promotion and fired because they were pregnant (common question of fact). Therefore, the women were properly joined as plaintiffs, and the employer's motion to sever will likely be denied.

(Choice A) The women are not required parties to the lawsuit under FRCP 19. This is because the women could separately sue the employer without (1) preventing the court from granting them complete relief, (2) prejudicing the absent woman's interest, or (3) subjecting the parties to multiple or inconsistent obligations.
(Choice B) The women's claims arise out of the same series of occurrences and share common questions of law and fact.
(Choice C) Parties need not seek (or defend against) the same relief to be joined. Therefore, the fact that the women requested different relief is not a basis for severing their joint complaint.
(Choice D) FRCP 20(b) allows a judge to take protective measures (eg, ordering separate trials) when the joinder of parties would cause an opposing party embarrassment, delay, expense, or other prejudice. But this can only be done when the claims by or against the joined parties do not concern the opposing party (not seen here).
📌 Educational Objective

Permissive joinder of parties is appropriate when (1) the claims asserted by or against the joined parties arise from the same transaction, occurrence, or series thereof and (2) a common question of law or fact will arise among them.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 20 (permissive joinder of parties).
questions.zh-question:
两名女性向联邦法院提起联合诉讼，指控其雇主违反了禁止工作场所歧视孕妇的联邦法律。

诉状称，这两名女性在分别怀孕六个月和七个月时，申请了两个新设立的主管职位。这两名女性声称，其雇主分别告知她们，拒绝她们的晋升是因为她们会因怀孕而缺勤。诉状还称，在这些会面后不久，这两名女性即被解雇。其中一名女性寻求恢复原职，而另一名女性则要求10万美元的损害赔偿。

雇主否认了这些指控，并提交了一项动议，请求法院分案审理这两名女性的诉讼请求。

法院可能会如何裁定雇主的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议，因为这两名女性是诉讼的必要共同诉讼人。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该动议，因为这两名女性的诉讼请求源于同一系列的事件，并且存在共同的法律和事实问题。
zh-choices.C: 批准该动议，因为这两名女性请求了不同的救济。
zh-choices.D: 批准该动议，因为将两名女性的诉讼请求合并审理会对雇主造成偏见。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：两名原告能不能依照 可允许联诉（permissive joinder） 一起起诉，而不是要不要强制联诉。

三秒认题路径：

同一雇主 → 同类歧视 → 同法同事实 → FRCP 20 → 不用拆

核心法律规则

可允许联诉（permissive joinder） 看的是 FRCP 20：两个条件都要过，第一，主张必须来自同一 交易、事件或一系列交易事件（same transaction, occurrence, or series thereof）；第二，案件里要有共同的 法律问题或事实问题（common question of law or fact）。考场意思：不是看两个人要不要拿同样救济，而是看他们能不能在同一个案子里一起打。

强制联诉（compulsory joinder） 是 FRCP 19，问的是“这个人不进来会不会让法院没法完整解决、损害缺席者利益，或让现有当事人面临重复/矛盾义务”。这题里问的是把两位女性一起起诉是否合并得当，核心还是 FRCP 20，不是 FRCP 19。

只要两人的遭遇来自同一雇主、同一轮拒绝晋升和解雇、同一部反怀孕歧视联邦法，联诉就成立。

思维导图

先问：这题是“必须加人”还是“可以一起告”?
看FRCP 19：缺席会不会让法院没法完整救济、损害缺席者、或造成重复/矛盾义务？
本题不是在考这个：两名女性都可以单独起诉雇主，不是“必须加入”的人。
转FRCP 20：同一交易/事件或一系列事件？
是：同一雇主、同一轮拒绝晋升、同一轮解雇，事实线是连着的。
再问：有没有共同法律或事实问题？
有：都主张怀孕歧视，套同一联邦法，也都围绕“被拒升职并被解雇”的同类事实。
结论：两位原告可一起起诉 → 法院应否决 sever → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：两个人请求的救济不一样，一个要复职，一个要钱，所以不能放一起审。
但考试真正问的是：她们的诉求是不是来自同一组事实、会不会碰到共同法律问题。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

不同救济不妨碍联诉；真正会卡住的是事实线不连、法律问题不共用，或者只是在硬凑同案。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 同一雇主、同一轮拒绝晋升和解雇，说明来自同一系列事件；再加上同一怀孕歧视法和同类事实争点，FRCP 20 允许一起起诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 required parties 当成这题主轴了。

❌ 事实误判 | 救济差异误读

✕ C: 看到 different relief 就误判会拆案，但救济不同不影响联诉。

❌ 法律适用 | 预防性拆分误套

✕ D: 把 prejudice 直接推成必须分案，忽略了这里本来就符合 FRCP 20。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判 FRCP 20 两件事，再看 FRCP 19 不是主考点，别被“救济不同”带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：同一串事实 + 共同法/事实问题 = 可一起告。看到联诉题先问 FRCP 20，不要先想 FRCP 19。

小口诀：same transaction + common question = join。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A plastic surgeon left her business partner to open her own plastic surgery clinic in a neighboring state. The business partner brought a diversity action against the plastic surgeon in federal court for violating a noncompete clause in the partnership agreement. The business partner properly filed an ex parte application for a temporary restraining order (TRO) that would prohibit the plastic surgeon from operating her new clinic. After a hearing at which only the business partner was present, the court properly issued the ex parte TRO, finding that the partner would be immediately and irreparably harmed by the loss of goodwill caused by the plastic surgeon's violation of the noncompete clause. The TRO was served on the plastic surgeon the next day.
One week later, the business partner moved to convert the TRO into a preliminary injunction. He requested that the court grant the motion immediately without providing notice to the plastic surgeon.
Will the court grant the business partner's request?

choices.A: No, because notice must be given to an opposing party before a court may issue a preliminary injunction.
choices.B: No, because the partner's attorney failed to certify in writing why the plastic surgeon need not be notified.
choices.C: Yes, because the ex parte TRO had expired and was no longer in effect.
choices.D: Yes, because the partner will suffer immediate and irreparable harm if the request is not granted.

questions.explanation:
Preliminary relief
(FRCP 65)
Type Required contents Effect
Preliminary
injunction		 Notice of
hearing		 • State reasons issued

  restrained or required
• Specify terms 		Persons bound upon receiving
actual notice of order:
• parties to the case

  employees & attorneys

Temporary
restraining
order		 Ex parte
(no notice)		 Above requirements plus:
• date & hour issued
• why injury is irreparable
• why issued without notice
• promptly filed with clerk & entered
  into record
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A temporary restraining order (TRO) is a court order that commands a party to do or stop doing a specified action for 14 days or until a preliminary-injunction hearing can take place—whichever occurs first.

A court may issue a TRO without notice to the adverse party (ie, ex parte). But when a party attempts to convert a TRO into a preliminary injunction, the adverse party must receive notice. Therefore, the court will deny the business partner's request because the plastic surgeon did not receive notice of the preliminary-injunction hearing.

(Choice B) The business partner's attorney must certify in writing why the plastic surgeon need not be notified when applying for an ex parte TRO—not a preliminary injunction. That is because, unlike an ex parte TRO, a preliminary injunction may be issued only after the adverse party has received notice of the preliminary-injunction hearing.

(Choice C) An ex parte TRO automatically remains in effect for 14 days unless that time period is (1) shortened by the court or (2) extended by the court for good cause or the adverse party's consent. Here, the TRO was seven days old when the business partner moved to convert it into a preliminary injunction. Since there is no indication that the TRO was to last fewer than 14 days, it had not expired and was still in effect.

(Choice D) Although the business partner will suffer immediate and irreparable harm if his motion to convert the TRO into a preliminary injunction is denied, the court cannot grant a preliminary injunction on that basis alone. Even if it could, the motion cannot be granted because the plastic surgeon did not receive notice of the hearing.

📌 Educational Objective

A court may issue a temporary restraining order without providing notice to the adverse party (ie, ex parte). However, the adverse party must receive notice before the court can convert a TRO into a preliminary injunction.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(a) (preliminary injunction).

一周后，该商业伙伴动议将临时限制令转换为初步禁令。他请求法院在不通知整形外科医生的情况下立即批准该动议。

法院会批准该商业伙伴的请求吗？

zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该伙伴的律师未能以书面形式证明为何无需通知整形外科医生。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Preliminary injunctions & TROs

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：临时限制令（temporary restraining order, TRO）能不能在没有通知对方的情况下，直接变成初步禁令（preliminary injunction）。

三秒认题路径：

TRO 已下 → 想转 PI → 对方未通知 → 不能批

核心法律规则

初步禁令（preliminary injunction）和其听证，必须通知（notice）对方；没有通知，就不能直接发这个命令。临时限制令（TRO）可以在紧急时ex parte发出，但这是给“先撑住局面”的，不是给“直接升格”用的。

所以这题里，法院要看的不是业务纠纷多严重，而是塑料外科医生有没有收到初步禁令听证（preliminary-injunction hearing）通知；没有通知，申请就卡住。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(a) — 初步禁令要先给对方通知；TRO的无通知规则不能直接搬到这里。

思维导图

先看法院现在要发的是什么？
是 TRO： 可在紧急时 ex parte，先挡住损害。
不是 TRO，而是 PI： 进入 notice 关卡。
关键门槛： 对方有没有收到 初步禁令听证（preliminary-injunction hearing） 通知？
没有通知 → 第三步直接卡死 → 不能发 preliminary injunction
题干结果： 7 天内 TRO 还没过期，但这不等于可以无通知转成 PI。
结论： 选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：已经有 ex parte TRO 了，而且对方伤害看起来很急，法院就该顺手批一个 preliminary injunction。

但考试真正问的是：初步禁令这一步有没有给对方通知和听证机会。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的损害有没有继续扩大」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干要把 TRO 转成 preliminary injunction，但对方没收到听证通知；FRCP 65(a) 要先通知，法院不能直接批。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ B: 把 ex parte TRO 的书面说明要求错搬到初步禁令。

❌ 事实误判 | 过期时间偷换

✕ C: 7 天不等于到期，题干没说 expired。

❌ 法律适用 | 紧急损害误判

✕ D: 只盯着 irreparable harm，忘了先有 notice。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是 TRO 还是 PI，再看是否已给对方 notice；程序门槛优先于损害叙事。

考场速记

记住：TRO 可以 ex parte，但 preliminary injunction 要先 notice。

口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely” 是别的中间上诉记忆法；本题更直接记成：先通知，后禁令。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A software developer left her company to open her own software firm. The developer and her new employees immediately began contacting the company's clients in violation of her noncompete agreement with the company.
The company filed a diversity action in federal court against the developer. The complaint requested damages and preliminary and permanent injunctions. After a hearing at which both parties were present, the court granted a preliminary injunction that prohibited "[the developer] and her employees from contacting any of [the company's] clients pending the outcome of the case." The court also explained why the injunction was issued. The developer and her employees received copies of the preliminary injunction the following day.
Are the employees bound by the preliminary injunction?

choices.A: No, because the employees are not parties to the lawsuit.
choices.B: No, because the preliminary injunction violates due process.
choices.C: Yes, because the employees received actual notice of the preliminary injunction.
choices.D: Yes, because the preliminary injunction specifically mentioned the employees.

questions.explanation:
Preliminary injunction
Grounds* Movant establishes that:
  • movant is likely to succeed on merits
  • movant is likely to suffer irreparable harm in absence of relief
  • balance of equities favors movant and
  • injunction is in public's best interests
Contents Order granting injunction must:
  • state reasons for issuance
  • reasonably describe prohibited or commanded acts and
  • state terms specifically
Effect Binds the following persons who receive actual notice of order:
  • parties
  • parties' officers, agents, employees & attorneys and
  • anyone in active concert or participation with above-listed persons
*Movant also must provide bond to pay costs & damages if nonmovant was wrongfully enjoined.

A preliminary injunction is a temporary court order that commands or prohibits certain actions while the case is pending before the court. It binds any of the following persons who receive actual notice of it:

  • The parties to the case
  • Those parties' officers, agents, employees, and attorneys
  • Any person who is in active concert or participation with the aforementioned persons

Since the developer's employees received copies of the preliminary injunction, they are bound by it (Choice A).

(Choice B) Due process protects persons against unfair deprivation of life, liberty, or property. Only public employees who are terminable for cause (as opposed to at-will employees) have a property interest in their jobs. And even if the employees here had such a property interest, the injunction's prohibition against contacting the company's clients would not deprive them of that interest.

(Choice D) The employees are not bound merely because they are mentioned in the preliminary injunction. Instead, they are bound because they received actual notice of it.

📌 Educational Objective

A preliminary injunction binds the following persons who receive actual notice of it: (1) the parties, (2) their officers, agents, employees, and attorneys, and (3) any person in active concert or participation with the aforementioned persons.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(d) (persons bound by preliminary injunction).

原公司向联邦法院对该开发人员提起了多元管辖诉讼(diversity action)。诉状请求损害赔偿、初步禁令(preliminary injunction)以及永久禁令(permanent injunction)。在双方当事人均出席的听证会后，法院发出了一项初步禁令，禁止“[该开发人员]及其员工在案件判决前联系[原公司]的任何客户”。法院还解释了发出该禁令的理由。第二天，该开发人员及其员工收到了初步禁令的副本。

这些员工是否受该初步禁令的约束？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为这些员工不是诉讼的当事人。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该初步禁令违反了正当程序(due process)。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为这些员工收到了该初步禁令的实际通知(actual notice)。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该初步禁令明确提到了这些员工。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Injunctions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：临时禁令（preliminary injunction）能不能约束非当事人；答案看的是实际通知（actual notice），不是看对方有没有正式列在诉讼名单里。

三秒认题路径：

临时禁令 → 非当事人 → 实际通知 → 受约束 → 选 C

核心法律规则

临时禁令（preliminary injunction）是案件审理期间先行约束行为的法院命令。按照联邦民事诉讼规则 65(d)（Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(d)），它不仅约束当事人，还约束当事人的雇员（employees）、代理人、律师，以及和这些人共同参与（active concert or participation）的人。考场意思：只要收到了实际通知，就可能被绑住。

这里关键不是“他是不是被告”，而是“他有没有收到命令的副本或其他实际通知（actual notice）”。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(d) — 这条规则直接锁定：收到实际通知的当事人雇员会被临时禁令约束。

思维导图

先看对象：员工是不是“被禁令绑定的人”
第一步：是不是当事人？
不是也没关系，继续看 65(d)
第二步：是不是当事人的员工、代理、律师，或与其共同参与的人？
员工收到副本
→
实际通知（actual notice）
→
被临时禁令约束
第三步：是否只因为“禁令里点名了他”？
不够；真正的钩子是 actual notice + 身份关系
结论：员工收到了禁令副本 → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：员工不是诉讼当事人，所以当然不受影响。

但考试真正问的是：65(d)会不会把收到actual notice的员工也绑进去。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题真正的坑是把“非当事人”误当成“当然不受禁令约束”，其实规则明确把当事人的员工也算进去。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干写明员工收到了preliminary injunction副本；65(d)说收到actual notice的当事人员工会被绑定，所以能选 C。

❌ 概念混淆 | 非当事人误判

✕ A: 只盯着“不是当事人”，漏了employees也在规则里。

❌ 法律适用 | 正当程序误套

✕ B: 把正当程序问题硬塞进来，但这里争的是禁令拘束范围，不是解雇权利。

❌ 事实误判 | 点名即生效

✕ D: 以为被写进命令就自动受限，忽略还要看actual notice。

这题建议用什么方法？

先问“谁被 65(d) 绑住”，再看有没有实际通知，别先被“非当事人”四个字带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：临时禁令（preliminary injunction）不只管当事人，也管收到actual notice的员工、代理人和共同参与者。

口诀：actual notice + party-side people = bound。先找“谁收到了”，再找“他和当事人是什么关系”。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A company incorporated in State A and with its principal place of business in State B sued its former employee from State C in a federal district court in State A for allegedly embezzling $80,000. During a deposition of the employee in State B, the company's attorney asked the employee whether he stole the money. The employee's attorney objected and directed the employee not to answer to preserve his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. The company's attorney thinks this privilege does not apply because she believes that the statute of limitations has run on any criminal proceedings that could be brought against the employee for his conduct.
How should the company's attorney proceed?

choices.A: Adjourn the deposition and file a motion with the federal court in State B to compel the employee to answer.
choices.B: Adjourn the deposition and file a motion with the federal court in State C to compel the employee to answer.
choices.C: Proceed with the deposition and then file a motion with the federal court in State A to compel the employee to answer.
choices.D: Proceed with the deposition and then file a motion with the federal court in State B to compel the employee to answer.

questions.explanation:
Depositions
Type Procedure Objections Answers
Oral
(most common)
  • Questions asked by attorneys
  • No notice of questions
  • Responses recorded by officer
 Concisely stated
on record		 Answer required unless:
  • enforcing court-ordered limitation
  • presenting motion to terminate or limit or
  • preserving privilege
Written
  • Questions asked by officer
  • Notice of questions required
  • Responses recorded by officer
 Served in writing

A deposition is a method of discovery in which a party conducts a written or oral examination of another (ie, the deponent) under oath and outside of court. In an oral deposition, the parties' attorneys question the deponent. Like at a trial, any objections to these questions must be stated on the record or they may be waived. But unlike a trial, a judge is not present to rule on any objections. As a result, the objection is noted, the examination proceeds, and the deponent must answer the questions unless refusing to answer is necessary to:

• enforce a court-ordered limitation (eg, an order limiting the deposition's scope)

• present a motion to terminate or limit the deposition (eg, to prevent unreasonable annoyance or embarrassment of the deponent) or

• preserve a privilege (eg, privilege against self-incrimination)—as seen here.

The questioning party may adjourn or complete the deposition before filing a motion to compel a response. If the deponent is a nonparty, the motion must be filed where the deposition occurred. But if the deponent is a party (as seen here), it must be filed where the lawsuit is pending. Therefore, the company's attorney should proceed with the deposition and file a motion in State A federal court to compel the employee's answer (Choices A, B & D). The judge will then assess the merits of the employee's privilege claim and decide if a response is required.

📌 Educational Objective

When a deponent refuses to answer a question at a deposition, the questioning party may file a motion to compel a response. When the deponent is a nonparty, that motion must be filed in the district where the deposition occurred. But when the deponent is a party, the motion must be filed where the lawsuit is pending.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 30(c)(2) (objections at depositions).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(a)(2)–(3) (motion to compel deposition answer).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Depositions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：口头证言取证时，party deponent（当事人证人）拒答后，动议强制回答要去哪里提、要不要先停下庭外问话。

三秒认题路径：

口头证言 → 拒答 → 保留特权 → 先继续问 → 去法院催答

核心法律规则

在 oral deposition（口头证言取证） 里，律师对问题的 objection（异议） 要当场说在记录上，但通常不能让法官立刻裁决，所以证言一般继续进行。若拒答是为了保留 privilege（特权），对方可以之后提 motion to compel（强制答复动议）。

这里最关键的不是“有没有特权”，而是“动议要向哪个法院提”。如果拒答的人是 party（当事人），动议要向 lawsuit is pending（诉讼正在进行的法院） 提；如果是 nonparty（非当事人），才去证言发生地提。

核心判例： 这题不靠专门判例，直接用 Fed. R. Civ. P. 30(c)(2) 和 37(a)(2)–(3) 锁定：先继续取证，事后去有管辖的法院催答。

思维导图

先看：这是口头证言（oral deposition）中的拒答吗？
是 异议记在记录上，证言先继续，不是法官现场裁定。
再看 拒答是不是为了保留特权（preserve a privilege）？
是：可以拒答，但之后可提 motion to compel。不是“当场停止”。
最后 deponent 是 party 还是 nonparty？
party 去 诉讼进行地 申请强制答复 → 本题去 State A。
nonparty 才去 证言发生地 申请。
结论：先继续 depo，后到 State A 联邦法院催答 → 选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然对方说的是 Fifth Amendment privilege（第五修正案特权），那就先停下取证、去别的地方立刻告他拒答。

但考试真正问的是：先把 deposition 做完，再按“当事人/非当事人”规则决定 motion to compel 去哪个法院。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干已明确是 deposition of the employee in State B，而 employee 是 party，所以公司应先继续取证，再去 State A 这个诉讼进行地提强制答复动议。

❌ 事实误判 | 证言地点偷换

✕ A: 把 party 当成 nonparty，才会去 State B 提动议。

❌ 法律适用 | 错把住所当场所

✕ B: 以为去被告州就行，其实动议看的是诉讼进行地，不看员工原籍州。

❌ 概念混淆 | 先后顺序颠倒

✕ D: 先 proceed with 取证后再动议是对的，但 State B 选错了。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先分清 party/nonparty，再按诉讼进行地锁定 motion to compel。

考场速记

记住一句：口头证言先继续，拒答后再催答；当事人去诉讼地，非当事人去证言地。

如果题目在考中间上诉，记忆口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”，分别联想到 injunction、certification、class action 等法定例外；但本题不是立刻上诉题，是 motion to compel（强制答复动议） 的地点题。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A doctor from State B performed surgery on a man from State A and implanted a device in the man's lower spine. The device was manufactured by a corporation incorporated and with its principal place of business in State C. Following the surgery, the device fell apart inside the man's back and caused him to suffer severe injuries.
The man sued the corporation in a federal district court in State B for $250,000. The corporation filed a pre-answer motion to dismiss the man's suit for failing to join the doctor as a required party. The corporation claimed that the doctor improperly installed the device and, therefore, is jointly and severally liable for the man's injuries.
Will the court likely grant the corporation's motion to dismiss?

choices.A: No, because the corporation must file an answer before it can make this motion.
choices.B: No, because the doctor is not a required party to the suit.
choices.C: Yes, because it is inequitable to proceed without the doctor.
choices.D: Yes, because joining the doctor to the suit is not feasible.

questions.explanation:
Required joinder of parties
(FRCP 19)
Is absent person a required party?
Person's absence will:
• prevent complete relief to existing parties
• prejudice absent person's interest OR
• result in multiple or inconsistent obligations
Proceed
with suit
Yes
↓
Is joinder feasible?
• Personal jurisdiction over required party
• subject-matter jurisdiction preserved AND
• proper venue remains
Join
required
party
Yes
↓
Is it equitable to proceed without required party?
• Judgment would impose slight prejudice
• court can avoid or lessen prejudice
• judgment would be adequate AND
• plaintiff has no other adequate remedy
Proceed without
required party
Yes
↓
Dismiss suit

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure

Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 19, an absent party must be joined (ie, added) to a suit in certain circumstances. This required-joinder rule provides a three-step process for determining whether joinder is necessary. The first step requires the court to determine whether the absent party is a required (ie, indispensable) party because:

• complete relief cannot be granted to the existing parties without that party's presence
• the party's absence will subject existing parties to a substantial risk of multiple or inconsistent obligations or
• the party's absence will prejudice his/her ability to protect an interest related to the suit.

Potential tortfeasors facing joint and several liability are not required parties. Joint and several liability allows a plaintiff to obtain complete relief from any one of the tortfeasors. That tortfeasor is not subject to multiple or inconsistent obligations because the tortfeasor may sue any absent tortfeasor for contribution. The absent tortfeasor can then protect its interests in the contribution suit. As a result, the doctor is not a required party in the man's suit, and the court will likely deny the corporation's motion to dismiss.*

*If the corporation seeks to add the doctor because he is allegedly liable to the corporation for all or part of the man's claim, it should add the doctor to the suit through third-party practice (ie, impleader).

(Choice A) FRCP 12 allows a defendant to make several motions before filing its answer—including a motion to dismiss for failing to join a required party (as seen here).

(Choice B) No, because the doctor is not a required party to the suit.

(Choices C & D) The second step in the required-joinder rule considers whether it is feasible to join the required party, and the third step considers whether it is equitable to proceed without the required party. However, these steps need only be considered if the absent party is a required party (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Alleged tortfeasors facing joint and several liability are not required parties because (1) complete relief can be granted in their absence, (2) the tortfeasors in the suit will not be subjected to multiple or inconsistent obligations, and (3) the absent tortfeasors can adequately protect their interests in a future action.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 19 (required joinder of parties).
  • Temple v. Synthes Corp., Ltd., 498 U.S. 5, 7–8 (1990) (explaining that joint tortfeasors are not required parties).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：FRCP 19 required joinder 里，潜在共同侵权人是不是“必须拉进来”的当事人；答案是通常不是，所以不能因为没把医生加进来就直接驳回。

三秒认题路径：

先看缺谁 → 再看必加吗 → 联想 joint tortfeasor → 不是必加 → 不能驳回

核心法律规则

规则先看 required party（必要当事人）：只有缺席会让现有当事人拿不到完整救济、让缺席者利益受损，或让现有当事人面临重复/不一致义务时，才要继续往下看。共同侵权人（joint tortfeasor） 考场意思：通常不是必要当事人，因为原告可以先单独告其中一个人拿到完整赔偿。

如果某一方只是可能要承担分担或追偿责任，这更像 第三方诉讼（impleader） 的问题，不是原告这案子里必须先把他加进来。FRCP 12 允许被告在答辩前提 motion to dismiss for failure to join a required party，但前提仍然是这个人真的是必要当事人。

核心判例： Temple v. Synthes Corp., Ltd. — 联合侵权人通常不是 FRCP 19 的必要当事人，所以本题医生不必被强制加入。

思维导图

先问：医生缺席，会不会让现有当事人拿不到完整救济，或造成重复 / 不一致义务？
不会
卡死结论：医生不是 required party，不用继续问能否加入，法院继续审。
会
才往下看：能不能把医生加进来？
能加
加进来，继续审
不能加
再问：缺了他继续审，是否仍然公平？
公平
继续审
不公平
这才可能 dismiss suit
原告：受伤患者可先单独告制造商
→
被告：公司想借 FRCP 19 拉医生进来
→
医生可能另案分担 / 追偿

考点陷阱

你可能会想：医生好像真有责任，没把他加进来会不会不公平，所以应该让案件直接被驳回。

但考试真正问的是：这个人是不是 required party，不是他“有没有错”。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。本题里联合侵权人一般能分案追责，现案照样可以把赔偿问题审完。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键是 joint and several liability：公司就算单独被告，也能面对完整赔偿，因此医生不是必须加入的必要当事人。

❌ 法律适用 | 先后顺序误判

✕ A: 把 before it can make 当成程序障碍；其实 FRCP 12 允许先提这个动议。

❌ 概念混淆 | 义务关系误判

✕ C: 看到医生可能有错，就误以为“有责任的人都要拉进来”。

❌ 事实误判 | 必加前提偷换

✕ D: 把 not feasible 直接拿来用，但前提是医生先得是必要当事人。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判“是不是必要当事人”，别急着往“能否加入”“是否公平”那两步走。

考场速记

记住一句：joint tortfeasor ≠ required party。先抓“能否完整救济”和“是否重复义务”，只要这两项都没卡死，通常就不用因为少一个潜在侵权人而驳回。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 不是本题主轴；本题更该记的是“共同侵权人通常不必 joinder，先告一个也行”。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A mail clerk domiciled in State A slipped and fell on ice that had formed near the loading dock of the building in State B where the clerk's State B employer leased space for its headquarters. The building was owned and operated by a State C corporation. As a result of the fall, the clerk was injured and the employer's expensive computer he was carrying was badly damaged.
The clerk sued the building owner for negligence in a federal district court in State B, seeking $100,000 in personal-injury damages. The employer has filed a timely motion to intervene, asserting an $80,000 negligence claim against the building owner for the damage to its computer.
Is the court likely to grant the employer's motion to intervene?

choices.A: No, because although the employer has an interest in the clerk's action, that interest is not likely to be impaired in the employer's absence.
choices.B: No, because the clerk chose not to join the employer as a co-plaintiff in his action.
choices.C: Yes, because the employer is an indispensable party.
choices.D: Yes, because the employer's claim shares common questions of law and fact with the clerk's action.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Intervention
(FRCP 24)
Intervention of
right		 • On timely motion, court must permit intervention when either:
  • nonparty's interest in case not adequately represented by existing parties & deciding case may impair nonparty's ability to protect that interest
  • federal statute gives unconditional right to intervene
Permissive
intervention		 • On timely motion, court may permit intervention when either:
  • nonparty's claim or defense shares common question of law or fact with main action
  • federal statute gives conditional right to intervene
• Court must consider whether intervention will unduly delay or prejudice adjudication of original parties' rights

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A nonparty can join a case to protect his/her interest by timely filing a motion to intervene under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 24.* There are two types of intervention:

• Intervention of right – the court must permit an intervention when (1) the nonparty's interest is inadequately represented by the existing parties and (2) deciding the case may impair the nonparty's ability to protect that interest.

• Permissive intervention – the court may permit an intervention when the nonparty's claim or defense shares a common question of law or fact with the main action. But a court may deny permissive intervention if it would unduly delay or prejudice the adjudication of the original parties' rights.

Here, the employer timely moved to intervene in the clerk's action against the building owner. Although the employer's interest (property-damage claim) is inadequately represented by the existing parties, deciding the clerk's personal-injury action is not likely to impair the employer's ability to protect its interest (no intervention of right). But since both actions are based on the owner's alleged negligence (common questions of law and fact), the court will likely allow the employer to permissively intervene (Choice A).

*To determine if a motion to intervene is timely filed, the court considers (1) the length of time the movant knew or should have known about its threatened interest, (2) the prejudice to the parties if intervention is permitted, and (3) the prejudice to the movant if intervention is denied.

(Choice B) The clerk's decision to exclude the employer as a co-plaintiff does not affect the employer's ability to intervene.

(Choice C) Under FRCP 19, an indispensable party must be joined in a lawsuit. But the employer is not an indispensable party because the employer's absence would not affect the court's ability to provide relief to the clerk or the employer's ability to protect its related property interest.

📌 Educational Objective

Intervention must be permitted when the nonparty's interest is inadequately represented and deciding the case may impair his/her ability to protect that interest (ie, intervention of right). And intervention may be permitted when the nonparty's claim or defense shares a common question with the main action (ie, permissive intervention).

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 24 (intervention).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：非当事人想加入诉讼时，是走 介入（intervention），而不是硬说自己是必须并入的当事人。

三秒认题路径：

非当事人 → 及时动议 → 共享争点 → 许可介入 → 选 D

核心法律规则

先看 联邦民事诉讼规则 24（FRCP 24）：非当事人可以通过及时提交 介入动议（motion to intervene） 申请加入案件。

如果只是想和主案共享同一组 法律或事实问题（common question of law or fact），法院 可以 允许，叫 许可介入（permissive intervention）。

如果是 当事人权益未被充分代表，而且判决会妨碍他保护该权益，法院 必须 允许，那才是 当然介入（intervention of right）。

规则落点： 本题里雇主的财产损害索赔和雇员的滑倒索赔都围绕楼主的过失，所以是共享争点，法院很可能允许 许可介入（permissive intervention）。

思维导图

先问：这是 介入（intervention），还是必须并入的 必要当事人（indispensable party）？
事实钩子 雇主不是原告，但想带着自己的 80,000 美元 财产损害请求进来。
规则门槛 FRCP 24 先看是否及时；再看是 当然介入 还是 许可介入。
当然介入卡死点：虽然雇主利益没被充分代表，但雇员输赢不会真正妨碍雇主另行保护财产损害请求。
真正能过关的点 雇主与雇员都在打楼主的 过失（negligence），共享同一组法律与事实问题。
结论 这是 许可介入（permissive intervention），所以选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：雇主有自己的损失，而且看起来和雇员案子很像，所以是不是一定能“加入”或者必须作为 必要当事人（indispensable party）？

但考试真正问的是：它能不能按 FRCP 24 以 许可介入（permissive intervention） 进来，不是看它能不能被硬塞进 FRCP 19。

本题不是在比谁更惨，而是在看有没有共享争点、能不能让同一场诉讼一起处理。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里雇主的 negligence claim 和雇员的滑倒案都要证明楼主过失，属于共同法律与事实问题，所以法院很可能允许介入。

❌ 概念混淆 | 当然介入误判

✕ A: 把 interest 有无代表好，当成一定能进来；其实这里卡在“能否 permissively 介入”。

❌ 事实误判 | 共有人选偷换

✕ B: 命题人骗你去想“没被列为共同原告就不能进”，但介入和是否先被选作原告不是一回事。

❌ 法律适用 | FRCP 19误搬

✕ C: 直接套 indispensable party，但雇主不是必须并入才能给雇员救济的那种人。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认是介入题，再分 当然介入 和 许可介入，最后盯住“是否共享争点”。

考场速记

记住一句：及时动议（timely motion） + 共享共同问题（common question） = 先想到 许可介入（permissive intervention）。

口诀：“先看及时，再看争点；没到当然介入，也可能许可介入。”

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
Hundreds of same-sex couples domiciled across the country initiated a class action in a federal district court against a health insurance company. The suit alleged that the insurance company violated a federal statute by charging the couples higher insurance premiums solely because they were in a same-sex relationship. The suit sought an injunction to stop the insurance company's discriminatory premiums as well as individualized monetary damages of $5,000 to $20,000 for each couple.
The district court entered an order certifying the suit as a "final equitable relief" class action after it determined that injunctive relief was appropriate because the insurance company's actions applied generally to the whole class. The insurance company immediately appealed the certification order.
Is the federal appellate court likely to overturn the certification order?

choices.A: No, because subject-matter jurisdiction exists over the class action.
choices.B: No, because the district court has not entered a final judgment.
choices.C: Yes, because the amount-in-controversy requirement was not satisfied.
choices.D: Yes, because the class action seeks individualized monetary damages.

questions.explanation:
Class action certification requirements
Case satisfies prerequisites
  • Numerosity – joinder of all members is impracticable
  • Commonality – class shares common questions of law or fact
  • Typicality – named parties' claims or defenses are typical of class AND
  • Adequacy – named parties will protect class’s interests
+
Case is suitable type of class action
  • Prejudicial risk to parties or absent class members if separate actions
  • Final equitable relief is appropriate because opposing party's actions
    apply to whole class OR
  • Common questions of law or fact predominate & class action is best
    method to resolve dispute
=
Certification permitted

A federal appellate court applies the abuse of discretion standard when reviewing a district court's discretionary certification order authorizing a class action to proceed. Class action certification is proper if the case satisfies four prerequisites (shown above) and is one of the following types of class actions:

• Prejudicial risk – when separate actions would create a risk of (1) inconsistent decisions regarding the parties or (2) impairing absent class members' interests

• Common question – when common questions of law or fact predominate over individual questions and a class action is the best method to resolve the dispute

• Final equitable relief – when injunctive or declaratory relief is appropriate because the opposing party's actions generally apply to the whole class

A certified "final equitable relief" class action is valid if the suit also seeks incidental monetary damages. Such damages flow from liability to the class and do not require individualized determinations (eg, statutorily mandated damages). In contrast, a certified "final equitable relief" class action is invalid if the suit also seeks individualized monetary relief (as seen here).* Therefore, the district court abused its discretion in certifying the couples' suit as a "final equitable relief" class action, and the certification order will likely be overturned.

*A certified "final equitable relief" class action that seeks individualized monetary relief may violate due process because, unlike in "common question" class actions, class members are not entitled to notice or an opportunity to opt out and pursue individual suits.

(Choices A & C) Subject-matter jurisdiction exists through federal-question jurisdiction, which has no amount-in-controversy requirement, because this class action arises under a federal statute. However, this action was improperly certified since it contains individualized monetary claims.

(Choice B) The final-judgment rule bars a federal appellate court from hearing an appeal until the district court has entered a final judgment—absent limited exceptions. One such exception is an appeal of a district court's order granting or denying class action certification (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A suit may be certified as a "final equitable relief" class action when injunctive or declaratory relief is appropriate because the opposing party's actions generally apply to the whole class. Certification of such a class action is appropriate even if it also seeks incidental monetary damages—but not individualized monetary relief.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(a)–(b) (class action certification requirements).
  • Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. v. Dukes, 564 U.S. 338, 360–62 (2011) (explaining that certification of a "final equitable relief" class action is invalid when the class members seek individualized monetary relief).

数百对居住在全国各地的同性伴侣在一家联邦地区法院对一家健康保险公司提起了集体诉讼。诉讼声称，该保险公司仅仅因为这些伴侣是同性关系就向他们收取更高的保险费，从而违反了一项联邦法规。该诉讼旨在寻求一项禁令以制止该保险公司的歧视性保费，并为每对伴侣寻求5,000至20,000美元的个体化金钱损害赔偿。

地区法院认定禁令救济是适当的，因为该保险公司的行为普遍适用于整个集体，因此下达了一项命令，将该诉讼认证为一项“最终衡平法救济”集体诉讼。该保险公司立即对该认证令提起了上诉。

联邦上诉法院是否可能推翻该认证令？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为对该集体诉讼存在标的物管辖权。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为地区法院尚未作出最终判决。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为未满足争议金额的要求。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该集体诉讼寻求个体化金钱损害赔偿。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Class Actions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：“最终衡平救济” class action（final equitable relief class action） 不能夹带 个别化金钱救济（individualized monetary relief）。

三秒认题路径：

禁令类 → 赔偿金 → 个别化 → 不能证成 → 可撤销

核心法律规则

先看 class action certification（集体诉讼认证）：要先满足 numerosity、commonality、typicality、adequacy 四个前提，考场意思：人够多、问题共通、代表典型、代表能护住全体利益。

再看类型：final equitable relief 的意思是对方行为基本是冲着全体成员来的，所以可以做禁令或宣告性救济；但它只容纳 incidental monetary damages（附带金钱损害），不能塞进需要逐个算的赔偿。

所以这题里，救济请求如果包含每对夫妻各自 individualized monetary relief，就会把这种 class action 的骨架撑坏，认证会被推翻。

核心判例： Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. v. Dukes — 说明 final equitable relief 不能和需要个别化判断的金钱赔偿混在一起。

思维导图

先问：这是哪种 class action？
YES：全班共同受影响
可走 final equitable relief
再查救济类型
只有 incidental monetary damages
卡死点：题目给的是 individualized monetary relief
结论：认证会被撤销
NO：需要逐个算钱
不适合 final equitable relief
结果：district court 滥用裁量，会上诉被改判

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然联邦问题诉讼能立案，而且法院也说可以给整个 class 发禁令，那就顺手一起要钱吧。

但考试真正问的是：这种 class action 的 type 能不能装下 individualized monetary relief，不是这个公司坏不坏、也不是总金额够不够大。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 individualized monetary damages 让 final equitable relief 失去资格，所以认证令大概率会被撤销。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 subject-matter jurisdiction 当成认证标准了。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ B: 盯着 final judgment 却忘了 class certification 本来就能立刻上诉。

❌ 事实误判 | 题干条件偷换

✕ C: 题目没考 amount-in-controversy，也没有金额管辖门槛问题。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认救济类型，再看能否混入个别化赔偿；一旦是，就直接判认证失败。

考场速记

记住：final equitable relief 可以带 incidental monetary damages，但不能带 individualized monetary relief。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely —— 遇到法定中间上诉例外再谈立刻上诉，别把“能上诉”误当成“能认证”。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
The attorney for a plaintiff in an action filed in federal district court served the defendant with the summons, the complaint, and 25 interrogatories asking questions about the defendant's contentions in the case. The interrogatories stated that they were to be answered within 30 days after service.
The defendant is likely to succeed in obtaining a protective order on which of the following grounds?

choices.A: Interrogatories are only proper to discover facts, not contentions.
choices.B: Interrogatories may not be served until an answer to the complaint is filed.
choices.C: Interrogatories may not be served until the parties have conferred to arrange for initial disclosures and prepare a discovery plan.
choices.D: The interrogatories exceed the number permitted without permission from the court or an agreement between the parties.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Methods of discovery
Depositions
  • Written or oral examination of party or witness under oath
  • 10 per side
Interrogatories
  • Written questions served on party
  • Serve up to 25
  • Written responses due within 30 days of service
Request for
production
  • Request served on party (or subpoena served on nonparty) to produce & allow inspection of documents, electronic information, tangible items, or land
  • No limit
  • Written response due within 30 days of service
Requests for
admission
  • Requests served on other party to admit truth of facts within scope of discovery
  • No limit
  • Written response due within 30 days of service
Physical/mental
exams
  • Order by court or parties' agreement for physical or mental examination of party if those conditions are in controversy

Except in limited circumstances,* a party may not seek discovery (including interrogatories) until the parties have held an initial planning conference—ie, a meeting where the parties arrange for initial disclosures and prepare a plan for discovery. If a discovery request is submitted before this conference is held (as seen here), the court would likely grant a protective order. This shields the served party from the undue burden of responding to that request, especially since the disclosure of the requested information will likely be arranged at the initial planning conference.

*Discovery may be sought before an initial planning conference (1) in a proceeding exempt from initial disclosures or (2) if permitted by a court order, the parties' stipulation, or a procedural rule.

(Choice A) Interrogatories are written questions (served by one party on another party) that may inquire about any matter within the scope of discovery—including facts, opinions, and contentions that pertain to the case.

(Choice B) Interrogatories may be served after an initial planning conference has been held—not when an answer to the complaint has been filed.

(Choice D) A party may serve up to 25 interrogatories on any other party without the court's permission or an agreement between the parties (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Discovery requests generally cannot be served until the parties have held an initial planning conference to arrange for initial disclosures and prepare a discovery plan.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(d) (timing of discovery).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 33 (interrogatories).

被告很可能基于以下哪一项理由成功获得保护令？

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery, disclosures, sanctions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：在初次规划会议前，能不能提前送达 询问书（interrogatories）。

三秒认题路径：

先送达 → 还没会商 → 触发26(d) → 先禁取证 → 选C

核心法律规则

询问书（interrogatories）是写给对方当事人的书面问题，能问事实、观点和立场，数量一般最多25个。可是 取证开始时间（timing of discovery） 不是看你已经没收到起诉状答复，而是先看双方有没有完成 初次规划会议（initial planning conference），用来安排初始披露和取证计划。

所以，这题里原告虽然已经送达了 summons、complaint 和询问书，但在会议前就发起取证，法院通常会发 protective order，把这次请求挡回去。

核心判例： 本题对应 Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(d) 和 Rule 33：先会商、后取证；没开初次规划会议，就先别急着问。

思维导图

Step 1
先看原告已送达 interrogatories
Step 2
但双方还没开 initial planning conference
Step 3
26(d) 先卡住：通常不能提前寻求 discovery
Step 4
法院给 protective order
结论
选 C：先会商，再发问

考点陷阱

你可能会想：对方都已经被起诉了，当然可以马上答 interrogatories，而且题目还写了 30 天答复，看起来很正常。

但考试真正问的是：取证时点对不对，不是问题内容像不像标准格式，也不是对方有没有时间回。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 初次规划会议前就送达询问书 直接撞上 Rule 26(d)；这时法院通常会准 protective order，因为取证还没到开放窗口。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则范围误判

✕ A: 把 contentions 当成禁区了，但询问书本来就能问立场和观点。

❌ 事实误判 | 起点条件偷换

✕ B: 以为要等 answer to the complaint，其实等的是初次规划会议。

❌ 法律适用 | 数量规则错位

✕ D: 这题没超 25，真正的问题是时点太早，不是数量太多。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看程序姿态：先问能不能开始取证，再看询问书的内容和数量。

考场速记

记忆顺口溜：先会商，再取证；没开会，先暂停。 看到 interrogatories，先问自己一句：initial planning conference 开了没有。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A plaintiff filed an action in federal district court and served the defendant with the summons and complaint. The defendant moved to dismiss the complaint for failure to state a claim.
Instead of opposing the motion to dismiss, the plaintiff voluntarily dismissed the action and filed a new action alleging the same claims and addressing the pleading defects outlined in the defendant's motion to dismiss. The defendant moved to dismiss the second action, and the plaintiff voluntarily dismissed the second action instead of filing opposition papers.
The plaintiff has filed a third action asserting the same claims and new allegations that are responsive to the defendant's second motion. The defendant has moved to dismiss the third action; the plaintiff opposes the motion.
Is the court likely to grant the defendant's motion?

choices.A: No, because the plaintiff has promptly and diligently attempted to address the pleading defects.
choices.B: No, because the plaintiff voluntarily dismissed each previous action before the defendant filed an answer or moved for summary judgment.
choices.C: Yes, because the plaintiff failed to seek a court order dismissing the second action.
choices.D: Yes, because the plaintiff's previously dismissed actions asserting the same claims operate as an adjudication on the merits.

questions.explanation:
Two-dismissal rule on voluntary dismissals
First action
Voluntary dismissal
without court order
Second action
on same claim
Voluntary dismissal by
court order or stipulation
Rule does NOT apply
(π can refile)
Notice of voluntary
dismissal
Rule applies
(π cannot refile)
Voluntary dismissal
with court order
Second action
on same claim
Rule does NOT apply
(π can refile)

Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 41(a), a plaintiff may voluntarily dismiss a suit without a court order by filing (1) a stipulation of dismissal signed by all the parties or (2) a notice of dismissal before the defendant serves an answer or a summary judgment motion. Here, no court order was required since the plaintiff voluntarily dismissed the first and second actions before an answer or summary judgment motion was filed (Choice C).

A voluntary dismissal is generally entered without prejudice. This means that the plaintiff can sue the defendant on the same claim in the future. However, a voluntary dismissal is with prejudice and operates as an adjudication on the merits when stated in an order, notice, or stipulation of dismissal OR the two-dismissal rule applies. This rule applies when the plaintiff:

  • voluntarily dismissed the first action in federal or state court without a court order and
  • voluntarily dismissed the second action based on the same claim in federal court by filing a notice of dismissal.

Here, the plaintiff likely dismissed both actions by a notice of dismissal since there is no indication that the court issued an order or the parties signed a stipulation. Since these actions asserted the same claims, the second dismissal operated as an adjudication on the merits. Therefore, the court will likely grant the defendant's motion to dismiss the third action.

(Choice A) The fact that the plaintiff has promptly and diligently attempted to address the pleading defects raised by the defendant does not affect the application of the two-dismissal rule.

(Choice B) Although the plaintiff voluntarily dismissed each previous action before the defendant filed an answer or moved for summary judgment, the two-dismissal rule still bars the third action.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the two-dismissal rule, a voluntary dismissal of a second action operates as an adjudication on the merits when the plaintiff voluntarily dismissed (1) the first action in federal or state court without a court order and (2) the second action based on the same claim in federal court by filing a notice of dismissal.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 41(a) (voluntary dismissals).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Adjudication without trial

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：两次自愿撤诉规则（two-dismissal rule）会不会让第二次撤诉变成对实体的裁判（adjudication on the merits），从而堵住第三次再起诉。

三秒认题路径：

先看撤诉几次 → 再看同一请求 → 再看是否无法院命令 → 再看第二次是否为 notice → 结论：能否再告

核心法律规则

联邦民事诉讼规则 41(a)下，原告可以在某些情况下不经法院命令撤诉；但如果原告先后两次对同一请求（same claim）作出自愿撤诉，而且第一次是无法院命令（without a court order）的撤诉，第二次又是用 notice of dismissal 完成，第二次撤诉就会按对实体的裁判处理。

考场意思：前两次都算“自己主动退场”，法律就不再允许你第三次换个版本重来。没有法院命令不等于你可以无限次重提；关键是第二次同样针对同一请求的 notice 撤诉。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 41(a) — 两次对同一请求的自愿撤诉，第二次会变成有偏见撤诉，第三次可被直接挡掉。

思维导图

先抓动作：原告是不是已经对“同一请求”撤过两次？
第 1 次 无法院命令的自愿撤诉
第 2 次 同一请求 + notice 撤诉
卡死点：第二次撤诉 = adjudication on the merits，第三次不能再起诉
本题结果 法院应准许被告驳回第三案
不会触发 若第二次是法院命令/双方协议撤诉
这时两次撤诉规则通常不适用，原告还能再告
题干噪音 是否及时补正、是否先答辩，都不是关键

考点陷阱

你可能会想：原告每次都在被告答辩前撤诉，还积极修正起诉状，所以第三次应该可以继续。

但考试真正问的是：前两次是否已经把two-dismissal rule触发了；一旦触发，法律直接把第二次算成对实体的裁判。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「原告是不是努力补正了」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干显示两次都对同一请求作出自愿撤诉，前两次后再起第三案时，第二次撤诉已按adjudication on the merits处理，所以被告的驳回动议应获准。

❌ 概念混淆 | 补正努力误判

✕ A: 把“努力改错”当成能绕开两次撤诉规则的理由。

❌ 事实误判 | 只看撤诉时点

✕ B: 只盯着 before answer，却漏掉第二次已经触发限制。

❌ 法律适用 | 无命令即无事

✕ C: 误以为没有法院命令就永远能再撤一次。

这题建议用什么方法？

先数撤诉次数，再核对是不是“同一请求 + 第二次 notice 撤诉”，最后直接套 two-dismissal rule。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“两次无命令，同一请求，再用 notice，第三次就堵死。” 看到 Rule 41(a) 先数次数，不要先盯着原告有没有认真补材料。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
The owner of a food processing plant sued a food preservative company in federal court for federal antitrust violations. During discovery, the owner's lawyer served the company with notice of a written deposition of the company. The notice stated the company's name and address and provided the name and address of the officer before whom the deposition would be taken.
The company refused to attend the written deposition. The owner moved for sanctions.
The company is likely to succeed in defeating the owner's motion on which of the following grounds?

choices.A: The owner failed to designate an individual from the company to answer the questions.
choices.B: The owner failed to include a subpoena with the notice.
choices.C: The owner failed to obtain the court's leave before serving the company with the notice.
choices.D: The owner failed to reasonably describe the matters to be examined.

questions.explanation:
Contents for written notice of deposition*
Type Similar contents Unique contents
Oral
  • Deponent's name & address (if known) OR general description to identify deponent or group to which deponent belongs (if name unknown)
  • If deponent is organization, matters for examination described with reasonable particularity
  • Time & place of deposition
  • Method of recording
Written
  • Deponent's name & address (if known) OR general description to identify deponent or group to which deponent belongs (if name unknown)
  • If deponent is organization, matters for examination described with reasonable particularity
  • Officer's name / descriptive title & address
  • Copy of deposition questions
*Must be served on party deponent to compel his/her attendance.

A deposition is a method of discovery in which a deponent (party or nonparty) is examined under oath and outside court. There are two types of depositions:

• Oral depositions (most common) – in which the parties' attorneys question and cross-examine the deponent as they would at trial and an officer records that testimony

• Written depositions – in which an officer asks the deponent questions submitted by the parties and then records the deponent's responses

To compel a party deponent's attendance at either deposition, the deposing party must serve the party deponent with written notice.* If the party deponent is an organization, the notice must describe the matters for examination with reasonable particularity and satisfy all other notice requirements. Based on the matters identified for examination, the organization must then designate one or more individuals to testify on its behalf. If the deponent fails to attend the deposition, the court may impose sanctions.

Here, the owner served the company with notice of a written deposition, but the company did not attend. However, the notice was deficient because it failed to reasonably describe the matters for examination. As a result, the company is likely to defeat the owner's motion for sanctions on this ground.

*The deposing party must also serve a copy of the written notice on the other parties and, for written depositions, on the officer before whom the deposition will be taken.

(Choice A) The company, not the owner, must designate an individual(s) to answer the deposition questions.

(Choice B) A subpoena is required to compel a nonparty deponent's attendance, but a party deponent (eg, the company) can be compelled to attend through written notice.

(Choice C) A party may conduct a deposition without the court's leave or the parties' stipulation unless (1) the deposition exceeds the 10-deposition maximum, (2) the deposition is sought before the initial planning conference, or (3) the deponent was already deposed in the case. None of these exceptions apply here.

📌 Educational Objective

To compel a party deponent's attendance at a deposition, the deposing party must serve the deponent with written notice. When the deponent is an organization, the notice must describe the matters for examination with reasonable particularity. The organization must then designate one or more individuals to testify on its behalf.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 31 (depositions by written questions).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 30(b)(6) (notice requirements for deposing an organization).

该公司拒绝出席书面证言质询。所有者请求法院施加制裁（sanctions）。

该公司很可能基于以下哪一项理由成功驳回所有者的动议（motion）？

zh-choices.A: 所有者未能从公司中指定一名个人来回答问题。
zh-choices.B: 所有者未能在通知中附上传票（subpoena）。
zh-choices.C: 所有者在向公司送达通知前，未能获得法院的许可（leave）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery, disclosures, sanctions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：写明组织被通知的取证事项是否足够具体，也就是 written notice of deposition（书面证言通知） 对公司这种组织是否写对了。

三秒认题路径：

组织作证 → 书面通知 → 事项要具体 → 没写清 → 可抗辩

核心法律规则

先抓住规则再看事实

要强制 party deponent（当事人证言对象） 出席，送达 written notice（书面通知） 就够了；对 organization（组织），通知还必须把要问的事项写得 with reasonable particularity（合理具体），这样公司才知道要派谁来答。

公司收到后，应该自己指定一个或多个 individuals（个人） 代表作答，不是由原告替它挑人。

本题里，公司拒不到场不是关键，关键是通知把 matters for examination（待询问事项） 写得不够具体，所以公司有理由对制裁动议说“不”。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 30(b)(6) / 31 — 组织证言通知必须具体描述询问事项，组织再指定代表出面作答。

思维导图

题干起点
食品公司是 party deponent（当事人证言对象），所以可以用 written notice（书面通知） 逼它出席。
必查通知内容
对组织必须写清 matters for examination（询问事项），而不是只写公司名和地址。
组织的动作
公司收到后要自己 designate（指定） 一名或多名代表回答。
卡死点
这里通知没把事项写得 with reasonable particularity，所以公司能拿这个挡住制裁。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：公司没来开证言，原告当然能要制裁，问题只是它有没有被 subpoena 或者要不要法院许可。

但考试真正问的是：对 organization 的 written deposition，通知有没有把要问的事项写到位。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干只写了公司名称、地址和 officer 信息，没有把 matters for examination 写得足够具体；对组织的书面通知缺这一项，公司就能拿它抗辩制裁。

❌ 概念混淆 | 代表指定误判

✕ A: 把 designate 的责任放反了，应该是公司自己指定人。

❌ 事实误判 | 传票对象偷换

✕ B: 看到 subpoena 就套非当事人规则，但公司是当事方，不用传票。

❌ 法律适用 | 许可条件错用

✕ C: 把 leave 当成必经门槛，其实这题根本不是超额或时机过早问题。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是 party 还是非当事人，再查组织通知是否写明询问事项。

考场速记

记住一句：party deponent 用书面通知就能叫来；organization 还得写清问什么。看到公司没到场，先查通知里有没有 reasonable particularity。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A construction company bought lumber from an out-of-state supplier. The lumber was supposed to be pressure-treated, which renders the lumber resistant to rot and termites. The construction company used the lumber to build its headquarters, and after one year, the lumber began to show signs of rot and termites.
The construction company sued the supplier for breach of contract in a federal district court.
Which method of discovery should the construction company use to most efficiently identify the supplier's employees who might have information about how the lumber was treated?

choices.A: Interrogatories.
choices.B: Oral deposition.
choices.C: Request for production of documents.
choices.D: Subpoena.

questions.explanation:
Methods of discovery
Depositions
  • Written or oral examination of party or witness under oath
  • 10 per side
Interrogatories
  • Written questions served on party
  • Serve up to 25
  • Written responses due within 30 days of service
Request for
production
  • Request served on party (or subpoena served on nonparty) to produce & allow inspection of documents, electronic information, tangible items, or land
  • No limit
  • Written response due within 30 days of service
Requests for
admission
  • Requests served on other party to admit truth of facts within scope of discovery
  • No limit
  • Written response due within 30 days of service
Physical/mental
exams		 Order by court or parties' agreement for physical or mental examination of party if those conditions are in controversy

Interrogatories are written questions served by one party on another party that may inquire about any facts, opinions, and contentions within the scope of discovery. One of the primary purposes of interrogatories is to ascertain facts and information that might lead to other evidence, and the main benefit of interrogatories is that they are simple and inexpensive. Therefore, interrogatories are the most efficient way for the construction company to identify the supplier's employees who might have information about the lumber's treatment.

(Choice B) A deposition is a written or oral examination of a party or nonparty under oath and outside of court. Oral depositions are useful to question potential witnesses because their answers can be used at trial if they are inconsistent with the witnesses' trial testimony or the witnesses are unavailable to testify. But an oral deposition is time-consuming and expensive, so it is not the most efficient method to identify potential witnesses.

(Choice C) A request for production is used to make another party produce and allow inspection of documents, electronically stored information, tangible things, or land in their control. Here, the supplier may have documents that show which employees treated the lumber. But the more efficient method to obtain this information is through interrogatories since they place the burden on the responding party (eg, the supplier) to find the answer.

(Choice D) A subpoena is a written court order that can be used in conjunction with other discovery methods to compel a person to appear in court, take part in a deposition, or produce documents in the person's possession. But it would not be useful here since the company is trying to identify potential witnesses.

📌 Educational Objective

Interrogatories are written questions served by one party on another party that may inquire about any matter within the scope of discovery. This simple and inexpensive method of discovery is primarily used to identify facts and information that might lead to other evidence—eg, the identity of potential witnesses.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 33 (interrogatories).

该建筑公司在联邦地区法院以违约为由起诉了该供应商。

该建筑公司应使用何种证据发现方法，才能最有效地确定可能了解木材处理方式相关信息的供应商员工？

zh-choices.A: 书面质询。
zh-choices.B: 口头取证。
zh-choices.C: 文件出示请求。
zh-choices.D: 传票。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery Devices

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：在取证工具里，哪一种最适合用来先找出知情员工是谁，而不是直接拿文件或逼人出庭。

三秒认题路径：

找知情人 → 要便宜快 → 先问当事人 → 选 Interrogatories

核心法律规则

询问书（interrogatories）是向对方当事人送达的书面问题，考场意思：让对方自己把事实、线索和相关人员名字写出来。

它简单、便宜，特别适合先摸清“谁知道什么”；证言录取（deposition）和文件生产请求（request for production）更像是后一步深挖，不是最省事的起手式。

核心判例： 本题不靠判例推翻规则，直接按 Rule 33：询问书就是用来找事实线索和潜在证人的。

思维导图

题干任务
先找出“哪些供应商员工知道木材怎么处理过”。目标是识别知情人，不是马上拿证词。
最省事工具
询问书（interrogatories）直接问对方当事人，成本低，能逼对方列出人名和线索。
为什么不是 deposition
口头询问要约人出庭、耗时耗钱，太重了，不是“最有效率”的第一步。
为什么不是 production / subpoena
文件请求和传票是拿材料或强制出席，不能直接帮你先锁定知情员工。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然要找“谁处理过木材”，那就直接要文件、叫人来作证更快。

但考试真正问的是：哪种方法最省钱、最省步骤，先把知情人名单挖出来。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干要先找出供应商哪些员工知道处理过程，询问书最便宜也最直接，正好逼对方把人名和线索写出来。

❌ 法律适用 | 口供前置误判

✕ B: 误把 oral deposition 当成先找人名单的最优工具。

❌ 概念混淆 | 文件人名单混用

✕ C: 以为 request for production 一定能最快锁定知情员工。

❌ 事实误判 | 传票对象偷换

✕ D: 把 subpoena 当成找潜在证人的首选，忽略它更偏向强制出席或交材料。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看题目要的是“找人”还是“拿材料”，再选最省钱、最少步骤的取证工具。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先找人，问对方；先要线索，用询问书。 这类题先想 interrogatories，因为它最适合把潜在线索和知情人名单逼出来。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A man from State A and a woman from State B started a fashion business together in State A. After a year of working together, the man and the woman began to have different opinions on how the business should operate. The woman was also concerned that the man used dress designs from his previous employer, thereby risking a lawsuit from the former employer. They tried to figure out a solution to wind down the business without involving lawyers but failed.
The woman sued the man in federal district court, seeking $2 million for breach of contract. During discovery, the woman served a subpoena on the man's former employer seeking copies of the employer's dress designs. The employer is worried that disclosing these designs will reveal his trade secrets.
What is the most efficient action the employer can take to prevent disclosure of his trade secrets?

choices.A: Claim privilege over the dress designs.
choices.B: File a motion to quash the subpoena.
choices.C: Intervene in the case.
choices.D: Request a temporary restraining order.

questions.explanation:
Quashing or modifying subpoenas
(FRCP 45(d)(3))
Required Court must quash or modify subpoena that:
  • fails to allow reasonable time to comply
  • requires person to comply beyond geographical limits
  • requires disclosure of privileged or protected matter or
  • subjects person to undue burden
Permitted Court may quash or modify subpoena that requires disclosing:
  • unretained expert's opinion or information that (1) does not describe occurrences in dispute & (2) results from expert's study not requested by party
  • trade secret or confidential research, development, or commercial information
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A subpoena is a written court order that compels a person (party or nonparty) to appear in court or at a deposition OR to produce documents or items in his/her possession.* Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 45(d), a person subjected to a subpoena may file a motion to modify or quash that subpoena.

A court may grant the motion if the subpoena requires disclosure of:

  • an unretained expert witness's opinion or information that (1) does not describe specific occurrences in dispute and (2) results from the expert's independent study instead of a party's request or
  • trade secrets or other confidential research, development, or commercial information.

Here, the woman served a subpoena on the man's former employer (nonparty) to produce copies of his dress designs. Since the employer is concerned that disclosure will reveal his trade secrets and a motion is relatively cost-effective, the most efficient action to prevent disclosure is to file a motion to quash the subpoena.

*A person commanded to produce documents or items need not appear in person at the place of production or inspection unless also commanded to appear for a deposition, hearing, or trial.

(Choice A) In general, trade secrets are not privileged. If they were, the court would be required to modify or quash a subpoena compelling the disclosure of that privileged information.

(Choice C) A nonparty may intervene (ie, join) and fully participate in a pending suit to protect his/her interests. But here, the employer does not have an interest in the pending suit other than the subpoena, and he can efficiently protect this interest by filing a motion to quash.

(Choice D) A temporary restraining order (TRO) is a court order that preserves the status quo of the parties until there is an opportunity to hold a full hearing on an application for a preliminary injunction. But since the employer is not a party to the suit and a TRO provides only a temporary solution, it is not the most efficient action.

📌 Educational Objective

A court may modify or quash a subpoena that requires disclosing (1) an unretained expert's opinion or information that does not describe specific occurrences in dispute and results from the expert's independent study instead of a party's request or (2) trade secrets or other confidential research, development, or commercial information.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 45(d)(3) (modifying or quashing a subpoena).

一名来自 A 州（State A）的男子和一名来自 B 州（State B）的女子在 A 州共同创办了一家时装企业。合作一年后，该男子和女子开始在企业运营方式上产生分歧。该女子还担心该男子使用了其前雇主的服装设计，从而有被前雇主起诉的风险。他们试图在不聘请律师的情况下找出解决办法来结束业务，但未能成功。

该女子在联邦地区法院起诉该男子，以违约为由索赔 200 万美元。在证据开示（discovery）期间，该女子向该男子的前雇主送达了一张传票（subpoena），要求其提供服装设计的副本。该前雇主担心披露这些设计会泄露其商业秘密。

该前雇主可以采取何种最有效的行动来防止其商业秘密被披露？

zh-choices.A: 主张服装设计享有特免权（privilege）。
zh-choices.B: 提交一份动议（motion）以撤销该传票。
zh-choices.C: 申请介入（intervene）此案。
zh-choices.D: 申请临时限制令（temporary restraining order）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery, disclosures, sanctions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：非当事人收到 传票（subpoena） 后，能不能用 撤销传票动议（motion to quash） 先挡住会暴露 商业秘密（trade secrets） 的披露。

三秒认题路径：

非当事人 → 传票索取 → 商业秘密 → 动议撤销 → 先止披露

核心法律规则

传票（subpoena） 是法院命令，能逼人交文件；收到的人可以在 FRCP 45(d)(3) 下提 撤销或修改传票动议（motion to quash or modify），考场意思：先让法院把这份命令拦下。商业秘密（trade secrets） 属于法院可以撤销或修改传票的对象，所以不是去硬扛披露，而是直接打传票本身。
这题里，雇主是 非当事人（nonparty），又被要求交出会暴露设计的材料；最省事、最直接、最符合规则的动作就是 motion to quash。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不管的是披露命令能否立刻上诉；本题不是上诉问题，而是 非当事人如何阻止传票披露，所以直接落到 FRCP 45(d)(3)。

思维导图

收到的是不是 传票（subpoena）？
是非当事人被要求交文件
要交的是不是会外泄的 商业秘密（trade secrets）？
是规则给的正门是 motion to quash
别绕去 intervene、TRO；先用传票规则直接卡住披露
结论：最有效动作 = 撤销传票动议（motion to quash）

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然 trade secrets 很敏感，那是不是要先告它“禁止披露”。

但考试真正问的是：非当事人 面对 传票 时，最有效的程序动作是不是先打掉这份命令本身。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以别被“怕泄密”带跑去想临时禁令；这里最稳的是先用 motion to quash 阻止披露。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 subpoena 直接要求非当事人交出可能暴露 trade secrets 的设计，FRCP 45(d)(3) 允许先用 motion to quash 挡掉披露。

❌ 概念混淆 | 特权张冠李戴

✕ A: 把 privilege 当成 trade secrets，命题人就等你混淆两者。

❌ 法律适用 | 介入条件误套

✕ C: 想靠 intervene 进主案，但这里只是挡传票，没必要绕远路。

❌ 事实误判 | 临时救济偷换

✕ D: 把 TRO 当成最省事工具，但题目要的是直接阻止披露，不是先做临时绕行。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看程序身份是不是 nonparty，再看能不能直接对 subpoena 用 quash 卡住披露。

考场速记

记住这组动作：传票 + 商业秘密 + 非当事人 = 先想 motion to quash。

口诀：“先打传票，不先打官司。” 需要联想中间上诉例外时，再记 In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，但那是另一类题。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A woman bought a piece of farmland in the state where she resides. Three years after this purchase, a man informed her that he held a mortgage against the farmland and that she must pay him.
The woman then filed a quiet title action in an appropriate federal court in the state where the farmland is located. The man was properly served with the complaint and summons.
The day after receiving the complaint and summons, the man called the woman and informed her that he co-owns the mortgage on the farmland with his brother. Both the man and his brother live in another state.
What is the easiest action the woman can take to join the man's brother in the suit?

choices.A: File a motion for compulsory joinder.
choices.B: Immediately file and serve an amended complaint listing both siblings as defendants.
choices.C: Move the court for permission to join the other sibling.
choices.D: Voluntarily dismiss the case and refile a complaint naming both siblings as defendants.

questions.explanation:
Amending pleadings
(FRCP 15)
Original
complaint filed
Answer or FRCP
12 motion served
21 days
after service
Start of
trial
Post-
trial
Amend once as matter of course
Amend to add issues tried by consent
Amend with opposing party's consent or court's permission

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure

Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 19, a person must be joined as a party to a lawsuit in certain situations. Here, for example, the brother is likely a required party in the woman's quiet title action since his absence could prejudice his mortgage interest. And though the woman failed to name him in her complaint, FRCP 15 allows a party to amend a pleading once as a matter of course—ie, without the court's permission or the opposing party's written consent. But this must be done within 21 days after:

  • serving that pleading if a responsive pleading is not required or
  • being served with a responsive pleading or FRCP 12 motion (whichever occurs first) if a responsive pleading is required.

A defendant is required to file and serve an answer in response to the plaintiff's complaint. And since the man has not yet filed an answer (or FRCP 12 motion), the woman can amend her complaint without the court's permission or the man's written consent (Choice C). Therefore, the easiest way the woman can join the brother in the suit is to immediately file and serve an amended complaint listing both siblings as defendants.

(Choice A) Compulsory (ie, required) joinder makes it mandatory to include all necessary parties in a lawsuit—eg, co-owners of property in a quiet title action. Therefore, a defendant would file a motion for compulsory joinder to add any necessary parties, while a plaintiff would simply amend the complaint (as seen here).

(Choice D) A plaintiff may voluntarily dismiss a suit if the plaintiff wants to file it in a different court or has reached a settlement with the defendant. But the plaintiff need not dismiss a complaint to add another party.

📌 Educational Objective

A party can amend a pleading once as a matter of course within 21 days (1) after serving that pleading or (2) if a responsive pleading is required, after being served with a responsive pleading or motion under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 12.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a) (amending complaint before trial).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 19 (required joinder of parties).
questions.zh-question:
一名女子在她居住的州购买了一块农田。购买三年后，一名男子通知她，他对该农田持有抵押权，她必须向他付款。

该女子随后向农田所在州的相应联邦法院提起了确认产权诉讼。该男子被依法送达了起诉状和传票。

在收到起诉状和传票的第二天，该男子致电该女子，告知她他与他的兄弟共同拥有该农田的抵押权。该男子和他的兄弟都居住在另一个州。

该女子可以采取何种最简便的措施将其兄弟追加为本案当事人？

zh-choices.A: 提出强制追加当事人的动议。
zh-choices.B: 立即提交并送达一份将兄弟二人均列为被告的修改后起诉状。
zh-choices.C: 请求法院许可追加另一名兄弟为当事人。
zh-choices.D: 自愿撤诉，并重新提交一份将兄弟二人均列为被告的起诉状。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Amendments and Supplemental Pleadings

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：原告在对方还没答辩前，能不能用 一次当然修改（amend once as a matter of course） 直接把漏掉的必要当事人加进来。

三秒认题路径：

原告补人 → 对方未答辩 → 21天窗口 → 直接改诉状 → 选 B

核心法律规则

FRCP 15(a) 的考场意思：一方在特定早期窗口内，可以不经法院许可、也不经对方书面同意，改诉状（amend a pleading） 一次。若对方还没提交 答辩（responsive pleading） 或 FRCP 12 动议（motion under Rule 12），这个窗口通常还开着。

本题里，男方只是被送达了 complaint 和 summons，还没 answer，也没 Rule 12 motion，所以女方最省事的做法就是马上交一份 修正后的起诉状（amended complaint），把兄弟一起列为被告。

核心判例： 本题不靠判例名取胜，直接锁定 FRCP 15(a) 的“21天/答辩前”窗口，就能推出可直接修改。

思维导图

起点
原告已起诉，但漏掉兄弟
送达后
对方只收到 complaint + summons
关键门槛
未见 answer，也未见 Rule 12 motion
Rule 15(a)
仍在 一次当然修改 窗口内
结论
直接交 amended complaint，把兄弟加为被告

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然兄弟是 required party，那是不是要先去申请 compulsory joinder 或找法院许可？

但考试真正问的是：原告现在能不能直接改诉状把人加进来。 这里男方还没答辩，FRCP 15(a) 的“当然修改”比“先申请许可”更快。

司法考试看的是「能不能按程序直接补进来」，不是「兄弟在实体上是不是必要人」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 对方还没答辩，所以原告仍在 一次当然修改 的窗口内，直接提交 amended complaint 就能把兄弟加进去。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 required party 误当成必须先由被告提动议。

❌ 法律适用 | 许可前置误判

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A plaintiff brought a diversity action against a defendant in federal court. During discovery, the plaintiff orally deposed the defendant. Upon completion of that deposition, the plaintiff sought to depose the defendant again, which would be the tenth deposition taken by the plaintiff in the case.
The plaintiff served the defendant with written notice stating the time and place of the deposition. Upon receipt of the notice, the defendant's attorney called the plaintiff's attorney to tell him that the defendant would not appear at the deposition. The plaintiff's attorney demanded that the defendant appear as noticed. Neither the defendant nor the defendant's attorney appeared at the deposition. The plaintiff's attorney has moved for sanctions.
Is the court likely to impose sanctions?

choices.A: No, because the defendant had already been deposed in the action.
choices.B: No, because the plaintiff failed to serve a subpoena to compel the defendant's attendance.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant received written notice of the deposition.
choices.D: Yes, because the plaintiff is entitled to take up to 10 depositions.

questions.explanation:
Leave of court for oral or written deposition
Court's leave* or parties' stipulation required to conduct deposition when:
  • deposition exceeds 10-deposition limit
  • deposition sought before parties' initial planning conference or
  • deponent already deposed in action
*Leave of court is always required when deponent is in prison.

An oral deposition is a method of discovery in which the deposing party conducts an oral examination of another party or nonparty (deponent) under oath and outside of court. To compel the attendance and testimony of a party deponent, the deposing party must provide the party deponent with written notice. If the party deponent fails to attend, the federal court may impose sanctions.

Notice may be provided and the deposition conducted without the court's leave (ie, permission) or the parties' stipulation unless:

  • the deposition exceeds the 10-deposition limit (which includes both oral and written depositions)
  • the deposition is sought before the parties' initial planning conference* or
  • the deponent was already deposed in the action.

Here, the plaintiff sought to conduct an oral deposition of the defendant after the defendant had already been deposed in the action. Since the plaintiff failed to obtain the court's leave and the parties did not stipulate to the second deposition, the plaintiff's written notice to the defendant was improper (Choice C). As a result, the defendant was not required to attend the deposition, and the court is unlikely to impose sanctions.

*Leave of court or the parties' stipulation is not required for an oral deposition conducted before the initial planning conference if the deposing party certifies (and provides supporting facts) in the notice that the deponent is expected to leave the U.S. and be unavailable for examination.

(Choice B) A subpoena is required to compel a nonparty deponent's attendance at an oral deposition. But a party deponent can be compelled to attend through written notice.

(Choice D) Although the plaintiff was entitled to take up to 10 depositions, leave of court or a stipulation between the parties was required before the plaintiff could depose the defendant a second time.

📌 Educational Objective

A party may provide notice of and conduct an oral deposition without the court's leave or the parties' stipulation unless (1) the deposition exceeds the 10-deposition limit, (2) the deposition is sought before the initial planning conference, or (3) the deponent was already deposed in the case.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 30(a) (when court's leave or parties' stipulation required for oral deposition).

原告向被告送达了书面通知，说明了庭外取证的时间和地点。收到通知后，被告的律师致电原告律师，告知被告不会出席该次庭外取证。原告律师要求被告按通知出席。被告及其律师均未出席该次庭外取证。原告律师已动议要求制裁。

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为被告在该诉讼中已经被取证过。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为原告未能送达传票以强制被告出席。

zh-choices.D: 会，因为原告有权进行最多10次庭外取证。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第二次口头证言（oral deposition）已经超出一般可直接通知就开的范围，必须先拿到法院许可或双方同意；没有这个前提，未出庭不能拿来罚。

三秒认题路径：

已被讯问 → 又想再问 → 无许可/同意 → 无需出庭 → 不罚

核心法律规则

口头证言（oral deposition）是庭外发现程序，当事人（party deponent）通常只需收到书面通知（written notice）就要到场，不需要传票（subpoena）。

但如果这次证言是同一案件中的第二次证言（already deposed in the action），就不能只靠通知，必须先有法院许可（leave of court）或双方stipulation。

所以本题里，原告想再审问被告，但被告已经被问过一次；没有许可也没有同意，通知本身就不成立，被告没义务出席，法院通常不会罚。

核心判例： 无需依赖单独判例记忆；直接抓 Fed. R. Civ. P. 30(a) 的三道门槛：超过10次、太早、已被问过。

思维导图

第一步
先看：被告是party deponent，所以通常written notice就够，不用传票。
第二步
但这里是第二次口头证言，不是第一次开问。
第三步
第二次证言→要么court's leave，要么双方同意。
卡死结论
没许可 + 没同意 = 不必出席，所以不能罚。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：都已经发了written notice，对方不来当然该罚。

但考试真正问的是：这份通知有没有程序资格把第二次证言启动起来；没有leave of court或stipulation，通知就不够。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「对方主观上有没有故意不到场」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 already been deposed 触发第二次证言限制；没有法院许可或双方同意，原告的通知不成立，所以被告不到场，法院不太会罚。

❌ 概念混淆 | 传票错位误判

✕ B: 把subpoena当成当事人出庭前提了。

❌ 事实误判 | 通知即罚偷换

✕ C: 只看written notice，漏掉“第二次证言”这个门槛。

❌ 法律适用 | 次数上限误用

✕ D: 把up to 10理解成“第10次一定能做”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看证言对象是不是当事人，再查有没有“已被问过”这个例外，最后再决定能不能罚。

考场速记

记忆口诀：当事人证言先看“通知”，但第二次证言先看“许可/同意”。

一句话背熟：party 可通知，already deposed 要先批准；没有批准，就不能因为不来而罚。
