questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An employee brought a federal diversity action against his former employer, a chemical manufacturing company, seeking damages for injuries sustained on the job. During discovery, the employee's attorney served the company with notice of a written deposition she intended to conduct of one of the company's former managers. The employee's attorney attached the questions she intended to have the court officer ask the manager at the deposition. Eight days later, the company sent the manager and the employee the questions it wanted the officer to ask the manager on cross-examination. The employee's attorney served written objections to the form of the cross-examination questions four days after they were served. Twelve days later, the employee's attorney served the questions she wanted the officer to ask on redirect. Six days after service of the redirect questions, the company served its objections to the redirect questions and the questions it wanted the officer to ask on recross-examination.
Which of the following events was untimely?

choices.A: Service of the cross-examination questions.
choices.B: Service of the objections to the form of the cross-examination questions.
choices.C: Service of the redirect-examination questions.
choices.D: Service of the recross-examination questions.

questions.explanation:
Service of questions and objections in written depositions

Party requesting deposition
Other parties
Direct questions
& notice of deposition
Cross-questions
& objections to direct questions
Redirect questions
& objections to cross-questions
Recross questions*
& objections to redirect questions
≤ 14 days
≤ 7 days
≤ 7 days
*Objections to recross questions must be served ≤ 7 days after service of recross questions.

A written deposition is a method of discovery in which an officer asks a deponent questions and records the responses under oath and outside of court. The party requesting the deposition must serve the deponent and all other parties with written notice and a copy of the questions to be asked on direct examination (direct questions). The other parties may then serve the deponent and all other parties with responsive questions as follows:

  • Cross-questions – questions to be asked during cross-examination must be served within 14 days after service of the notice and direct questions (here, they were timely served 8 days later) (Choice A).
  • Redirect questions – questions to be asked during redirect must be served within 7 days after service of the cross-questions (here, they were untimely served 12 days later).
  • Recross-questions – questions to be asked during recross must be served within 7 days after service of the redirect questions (here, they were timely served 6 days later) (Choice D).

Therefore, service of the redirect-examination questions in this case was untimely.

(Choice B) A party must serve any written objections to the form of a question within the time required for serving a responsive question. This means that objections to the company's cross-questions were due at the same time as the redirect questions—7 days after service of the cross-questions. Therefore, the employee's attorney timely served written objections to the form of the cross-questions 4 days after they were served.

📌 Educational Objective

For a written deposition, (1) cross-questions must be served within 14 days after service of direct questions, (2) redirect questions must be served within 7 days after service of cross-questions, and (3) recross-questions must be served within 7 days after service of redirect questions. Objections are due at the same times.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 31 (depositions by written questions).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 32 (objections to form of questions in written depositions).

zh-choices.B: 对交叉询问问题形式之异议的送达。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery, disclosures, sanctions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：书面证言（depositions by written questions）里，转问（redirect questions）必须在对方交叉问题送达后 7 days 内送达，所以超期的那一步才是错的。

三秒认题路径：

直接问题 → 交叉问题 → 转问问题 → 递转问问题 → 先看 14 / 7 / 7

核心法律规则

书面证言（depositions by written questions）里，发起方先送达 直接问题（direct questions） 和通知；其他当事人可以再送达 交叉问题（cross-questions），期限是 14 days。转问（redirect questions）必须在交叉问题送达后 7 days 内送达；递转问（recross questions）也一样，必须在转问送达后 7 days 内送达。书面异议（objections to form）的期限和对应问题期限一样，跟着同一条时间线走。

核心判例： 本题以 Fed. R. Civ. P. 31 和 32 的期限为准，直接卡住“谁超期、谁没超期”。

思维导图

Day 0
发起方送达
直接问题 + 通知
Day 8
对方送达
交叉问题
8 天内，timely
Day 12
发起方送达
对交叉问题的书面异议
跟 7 天窗一致，timely
Day 20
转问问题
应在交叉问题后 7 days 内送达
这里拖到 12 天，超期
Day 26
对方送达
递转问 + 异议
在转问后 6 天，timely

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然前面的交叉问题和异议都来得很顺，后面的转问也差不多能过关。

但考试真正问的是：每一轮都有自己的 独立期限（deadline），不是“前面没超期，后面就自动没事”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「过程看起来顺不顺」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干显示 redirect questions 在交叉问题后隔了 12 天才送达，超过 7 days，所以这一步才是超期。

❌ 事实误判 | 期限算错

✕ A: 把 8 days later 当成超期，但交叉问题本来就有 14 天。

❌ 法律适用 | 异议时点错位

✕ B: 以为书面异议要等到更晚，其实它跟对应问题同窗送达。

❌ 概念混淆 | 递转问当转问

✕ D: 把 recross questions 也当成超期，但它是 6 天内送达，正好在窗内。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓顺序，再逐段对照 14 / 7 / 7 的期限表，最后只盯“哪一步超窗”。

考场速记

记忆口诀：14-7-7，先 direct → cross → redirect → recross；看到书面证言就先数窗，不要先看故事背景。

UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
for the
Northern District of Texas
Dallas Division
John Smith, Plaintiff, - v. - Jane Doe, Defendant.
Case No. 9:87-cv-6543-O JURY TRIAL DEMANDED
COMPLAINT FOR CIVIL NEGLIGENCE
I. Basis for Jurisdiction

1. Diversity jurisdiction exists because Plaintiff is a citizen of Minnesota, Defendant is a citizen of Texas, and the amount in controversy is $100,000.

II. Statement of Negligence Claim
  1. On October 1, 2019, Plaintiff was driving southbound on Red Street.
  2. At approximately the same time, the Defendant was driving northbound on Red Street.
  3. Defendant negligently swerved across the center lane and hit Plaintiff's automobile, causing Plaintiff to suffer severe personal injuries.
III. Demand for Relief

5. The Plaintiff seeks $100,000 in compensatory damages.

Dated this 12th day of December 2019. /s/ Bob T. Schmoe Bob T. Schmoe Bar No. 7654321 Benson, Dean & Wasson, P.C. 1600 UWorld Avenue Dallas, TX 12345 (555) 555-5555 bobschmoe@BDW.com

A complaint is the initial pleading that starts a civil action and states the basis for the plaintiff's claim. A complaint filed in federal court must contain all of the following:

  • Caption with the court's name, a title, the parties, a file number, and a designation as a "complaint"
  • Short and plain statement showing the grounds of the court's subject-matter jurisdiction (Choice C)
  • Short and plain statement of the claim showing that the plaintiff is entitled to relief
  • Demand for the relief (ie, remedy) the plaintiff seeks (Choice A)
  • Signature, address, phone number, and email address of the plaintiff's attorney (or unrepresented plaintiff) (Choice D)

The statement of the claim need only contain enough facts for a court to plausibly infer that a claim for relief exists. Detailed, specific facts are unnecessary unless the claim alleges fraud or mistake (neither of which applies here). Therefore, the patient's attorney need not include in the complaint a detailed statement of the claim showing that the patient is entitled to relief.

📌 Educational Objective

A complaint filed in federal court must contain (1) a caption with the court, title, and parties, (2) a short and plain statement of the court's jurisdiction, (3) a short and plain statement of the claim showing that the plaintiff is entitled to relief, (4) a demand for relief, and (5) the attorney's or unrepresented plaintiff's signature and contact information.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 8–11 (pleading requirements).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Complaint

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦民诉里，complaint（起诉状）必须写什么、又不用写什么。

三秒认题路径：

看“complaint” → 找必备项 → 看“NOT need” → 删掉多余细节 → 选 B

核心法律规则

考场直接用的规则

Complaint（起诉状）是启动民事诉讼的最初 pleading（诉状），考场意思：它要先把门打开，不是把案子一次讲完。

联邦法院的起诉状只需要 short and plain statement（简明陈述）：法院管辖权、请求救济、以及足够让主张“看起来成立”的事实。

所以，detailed statement（详细陈述）不是一般要求；除非是 fraud（欺诈） 或 mistake（错误），否则不必把细节写满。

核心判例： 这里按 notice pleading 走，重点是“给对方和法院一个基本通知”，不是写成证据清单。

思维导图

起诉状里到底要“简写”还是“详写”？
必写：管辖基础 → 请求救济 → 简明事实
看题干：“NOT need” 盯的是多写的那一项
卡死点：普通 negligence complaint 不要求 detailed statement
结论：能删掉“详细陈述” → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是诉讼开始，当然要把事实写得越细越好。

但考试真正问的是：Rule 8 要的是“够用的简明陈述”，不是完整故事书。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上够不够」，而不是「细节写得漂不漂亮」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干问的是 NOT need，而联邦起诉状只要简明陈述，不要求把主张写成详细版。

❌ 法律适用 | 救济写错层级

✕ A: 把 demand for relief 当成可省略项了，但它正是起诉状必备内容。

❌ 事实误判 | 把简写看没了

✕ C: 忽略 subject-matter jurisdiction 这一必写项，题干已经直接给了它。

❌ 概念混淆 | 签名信息混成选项

✕ D: 把 attorney's address 误当可缺项；联邦规则要求律师联系信息。

这题建议用什么方法？

先背“必备四件套”再看题干里的 NOT need，遇到 complaint 直接做删项题。

考场速记

记忆口诀：complaint 先看 jurisdiction、relief、short and plain statement、signature/contact info；“详细陈述”通常不是必须。

一句话记住：起诉状要“够通知”，不要“写成卷宗”。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A pedestrian was struck in a crosswalk by a truck and severely injured. The pedestrian brought a federal diversity action against the driver of the truck, alleging the following in the complaint: "On January 15, 2019, on Broad Street in City A, located in State B, the defendant negligently drove a motor vehicle, striking the plaintiff. As a result, the plaintiff was physically injured, lost wages or income, suffered physical and mental pain, and incurred medical expenses of $100,000."
The truck driver has moved to dismiss the action for failure to state a claim, arguing that the complaint lacks sufficient detail.
Is the court likely to grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because the complaint alleges facts showing plausible entitlement to relief.
choices.B: No, because the pedestrian has not had an opportunity to conduct discovery.
choices.C: Yes, because the complaint fails to allege facts showing probable entitlement to relief.
choices.D: Yes, because the complaint uses the term "negligently," which is a legal conclusion.

questions.explanation:
Specificity of pleadings
Claim Pleading requirements
General rule
  • Complaint – short & plain statement of claim showing plaintiff is entitled to relief
  • Answer – short & plain statement of admissions, denials, defenses & claims against other parties
Fraud/mistake/mental
condition
  • Malice, intent, knowledge, or other mental condition may be alleged generally
  • Circumstances giving rise to fraud/mistake must be stated with particularity
Conditions precedent
  • Assertion that conditions precedent occurred may be alleged generally
  • Denial that conditions precedent occurred must be stated with particularity
Damages
  • General damages may be alleged generally
  • Special damages must be specifically stated

A complaint is the pleading that starts a civil lawsuit and states the basis for the plaintiff's claim. It generally must contain a short and plain statement of the claim showing that the plaintiff is entitled to relief.* The statement of the claim need only contain enough facts for a court to plausibly infer that a claim for relief exists. A court may dismiss a complaint for failure to state a claim if the complaint does not satisfy this low standard.

Here, the pedestrian's complaint sets forth that the truck driver negligently struck the pedestrian on a particular date (January 15, 2019) and at a specific location (Broad Street in City A, located in State B). It then lists the damages that the pedestrian seeks to recover. Therefore, the complaint alleges facts showing plausible entitlement to relief, and the court will likely deny the truck driver's motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim.

*Detailed, specific facts are unnecessary unless the claim alleges fraud or mistake (neither of which applies here).

(Choice B) Discovery is the pretrial phase of a lawsuit that occurs after the pleading phase in which the parties are compelled to disclose information related to the case. Although the pedestrian has had no opportunity to conduct discovery, the court will deny the truck driver's motion because the complaint sets forth a plausible claim for relief.

(Choice C) Plausible entitlement to relief is a lower standard than probable entitlement to relief. The higher standard of probable entitlement to relief is only used in situations where a preliminary injunction is sought (not seen here).

(Choice D) A plaintiff can state legal conclusions in a complaint. Therefore, the fact that the pedestrian's complaint uses the legal term "negligently" does not render the complaint defective.

📌 Educational Objective

A complaint must generally contain a short and plain statement of the claim showing that the plaintiff is entitled to relief. The statement of the claim need only contain enough facts for a court to plausibly infer that a claim for relief exists.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 8 (complaint requirements).
  • Bell Atl. Corp. v. Twombly, 550 U.S. 544, 555–56 (2007) (holding that a complaint must contain a short and plain statement containing enough facts for the court to plausibly infer that a claim for relief exists).

一名行人在人行横道上被一辆卡车撞倒，伤势严重。该行人对卡车司机提起了联邦多元管辖权诉讼，在诉状中指称如下：“2019年1月15日，在B州的A市Broad Street，被告因过失驾驶机动车撞倒原告。因此，原告身体受伤、损失了工资或收入、遭受了身心痛苦，并产生了10万美元的医疗费用。”

卡车司机以诉状未能陈述有效的诉讼请求为由，请求法院驳回该诉讼，其理由是诉状缺乏足够的细节。

法院是否可能批准该动议？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为诉状指称的事实表明，其有合理的理由获得救济。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为行人还没有机会进行证据开示。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为诉状未能指称显示其很可能获得救济的事实。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为诉状使用了“过失地”一词，这是一个法律结论。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Pleadings

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：诉状（complaint）只要写到足以让法院“合理推断”原告有救济权利，就能过关，不需要把证据写满。

三秒认题路径：

起诉状 → Rule 8 → plausible → 不是 probable → 不能驳回

核心法律规则

诉状（complaint）的门槛是short and plain statement：只要写出一些事实，让法院能合理推断原告可能有权救济，就够了。这个标准叫plausible entitlement to relief，考场意思：先让案子活下来，不是先证明你已经赢了。

fraud/mistake 才需要特别细；普通negligence（过失）不用把每个证据都写进起诉状。

核心判例： Bell Atl. Corp. v. Twombly — 起诉状只需提供足够事实，让法院能“合理推断”有可救济的请求。

思维导图

看到“motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim” → 先问：起诉状够不够写到“合理可推断”就行？
YES：有日期 + 地点 + 司机撞人 + 伤害/医疗费 → 事实够具体，案件先活。
卡死点：不是问“证据够不够多”，而是问“能不能合理推断有请求权”。
NO：如果只是空喊“他有责任”，没有任何可识别事实，才容易被打掉。
答案落点：法院通常拒绝驳回，选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然还没做 discovery，原告当然还没把证据拿全，应该先驳回。

但考试真正问的是：起诉状本身有没有写到足够事实，让法院先相信“这案子有得打”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「证据现在有没有全部拿到手」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干写了 日期、地点、撞人经过和损害，足以让法院合理推断有救济请求，所以不会因为“细节不够多”而驳回。

❌ 事实误判 | 先后顺序偷换

✕ B: 把 discovery 当成起诉门槛了，程序顺序看反了。

❌ 法律适用 | 标准门槛抬高

✕ C: 把 probable entitlement 误当成普通起诉标准，命题人就等你抬高门槛。

❌ 概念混淆 | 术语当结论

✕ D: 看到 negligently 就以为是空话；其实普通过失可以直接写进起诉状。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓 Rule 8 的低门槛，再看题干有没有“日期+地点+行为+损害”这四个起诉骨架。

考场速记

记住一句：complaint 不是证据目录，只要够让法院“合理推断”就能过。遇到起诉状是否充分，先找 plausible，别把标准误抬成 probable。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A woman died with a life insurance policy worth $50,000. The woman had named "my son" as the sole beneficiary of the policy proceeds. The woman's three sons, two of whom are domiciled in State A and one of whom is domiciled in State B, individually filed claims with the insurance company to recover the proceeds of the woman's policy. The insurance company, which is incorporated and has its principal place of business in State B, brought a statutory-interpleader action in federal court against all three sons. The sons have moved to dismiss for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
Will the court likely grant the sons' motion to dismiss?

choices.A: No, because federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction over actions involving life insurance policies.
choices.B: No, because there is minimal diversity between the sons and the amount-in-controversy requirement is satisfied.
choices.C: Yes, because the amount in controversy does not exceed $75,000.
choices.D: Yes, because there is not complete diversity between the insurance company and the sons.

π = stakeholder; Δ = claimants

An interpleader action is available in federal court when multiple persons claim an interest in the same property (known as the "stake"). This action allows the possessor of the stake (the "stakeholder") to avoid multiple liability by joining the claimants to litigate the stake's ownership among themselves. There are two types of interpleader, each with distinct subject-matter jurisdiction requirements that must be satisfied before a court can hear the dispute:

  • Rule interpleader requires an amount in controversy that exceeds $75,000 and complete diversity between the stakeholder and the claimants—ie, they must be citizens of different states.*
  • Statutory interpleader requires an amount in controversy of at least $500 and minimal diversity between the claimants—ie, at least two claimants must be citizens of different states.

Here, the insurance company filed a statutory-interpleader action in federal court against the three sons. The amount-in-controversy requirement is satisfied because the policy is worth $50,000. Additionally, minimal diversity exists between the claimants since two sons are domiciled in State A while one son is domiciled in State B. Therefore, the court has subject-matter jurisdiction over the action and will deny the sons' motion to dismiss.

*Subject-matter jurisdiction can also be established in a rule-interpleader action if the claim presents a federal question (not seen here).

(Choice A) Federal and state courts share jurisdiction over both state and federal law claims unless the Constitution or Congress expressly provides federal courts with exclusive jurisdiction. Actions involving life insurance policies are not actions over which federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction.

(Choice C) For most federal civil actions arising from state law, including rule-interpleader actions, subject-matter jurisdiction requires an amount in controversy that exceeds $75,000. However, statutory-interpleader actions only require an amount in controversy of at least $500.

(Choice D) Rule interpleader requires complete diversity between the stakeholder and the claimants, but statutory interpleader only requires minimal diversity between the claimants.

📌 Educational Objective

Subject-matter jurisdiction for statutory interpleader requires an amount in controversy of at least $500 and minimal diversity between the claimants—ie, at least two claimants must be citizens of different states.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 22 (rule interpleader).
  • 28 U.S.C. § 1335 (statutory interpleader).
  • 7 Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 1710 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining the subject-matter jurisdiction requirements for rule and statutory interpleader).
questions.zh-question:
一名女性去世，留下一份价值50,000美元的人寿保险单。该女性指定“我的儿子”为保单收益的唯一受益人。该女性的三个儿子，其中两人居住在A州，一人居住在B州，分别向保险公司提出索赔，要求获得该女性保单的收益。该保险公司在B州注册成立且主要营业地也在B州，其在联邦法院对这三个儿子提起了法定互诉（statutory-interpleader）诉讼。儿子们以缺乏属事管辖权为由，请求驳回诉讼。

法院是否可能批准儿子们的驳回请求？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为联邦法院对涉及人寿保险单的诉讼拥有专属管辖权。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为儿子们之间存在最低限度的多元性，且争议金额要求已满足。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为争议金额未超过75,000美元。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为保险公司与儿子们之间不存在完全的多元性。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Diversity jurisdiction

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：法定 interpleader（statutory interpleader） 的联邦管辖门槛，只看至少 $500 和claimants 之间的 minimal diversity，不是要求 stakeholder 和所有人完全多元。

三秒认题路径：

多人抢同一笔钱 → interpleader → 先看法定型 → $500 + 最低多元 → 不能驳回

核心法律规则

Interpleader（第三方权利人争夺同一“stake”） 的作用是让持有这笔钱的人，把所有主张人拉到同一案子里，避免重复赔付。考试先分两种：rule interpleader 要求 超过 $75,000 加上 stakeholder 与 claimants 完全多元；statutory interpleader 只要 至少 $500，再加 claimants 之间的 minimal diversity。

所以这题只要看到两个索赔人来自不同州，就够了；不需要保险公司和每个儿子都不同州。minimal diversity 的考场意思：只要至少两名 claimants 是不同州公民，联邦法院就能进门。

核心判例： 本题主要靠 statutory interpleader 规则本身；记住它和 rule interpleader 最大区别就是门槛低、看 claimants 之间的最低多元。

思维导图

先分类型：这是 statutory interpleader，不是普通 diversity 诉讼。
问题1：金额够吗？
本题保单 $50,000 ＞ $500，所以金额门槛直接过。
问题2：看谁和谁多元？
不是看保险公司 vs. 三个儿子是否完全多元，而是看 claimants 之间 有没有至少两人来自不同州。
事实落点：
两个儿子在 State A，一个儿子在 State B → claimants 之间有 minimal diversity。
结论：
联邦法院有 subject-matter jurisdiction，所以不准驳回，选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是多元管辖，就得看保险公司和三个儿子之间有没有complete diversity。

但考试真正问的是：这是statutory interpleader，规则本来就改成了claimants 之间的 minimal diversity，而且金额只要 $500。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的钱有没有被多人争抢」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 $50,000 已超过 $500，且两名儿子在 State A、一名在 State B，满足 minimal diversity，所以法院不会驳回。

❌ 概念混淆 | 专属管辖误判

✕ A: 把 life insurance 误当成联邦专属案件，看到 exclusive jurisdiction 就选错。

❌ 法律适用 | 金额门槛误搬

✕ C: 把普通 diversity 的 $75,000 硬搬到法定 interpleader 上。

❌ 事实误判 | 完全多元偷换

✕ D: 盯着 insurance company vs. sons 的关系，偷换成了 complete diversity 标准。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认出是法定 interpleader，再按“金额门槛 → claimants 最低多元”两步秒杀。

考场速记

记住一句：statutory interpleader = $500 + minimal diversity between claimants；rule interpleader 才是 $75,000 + complete diversity。

口袋口诀：“法定互争，五百起步；看索赔人，不看持有人。”

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An engaged couple broke up one month before their planned wedding. Upon the breakup, the man asked the woman to reimburse him for the costs associated with the wedding and to return the engagement ring that had belonged to his great-grandmother. The woman, who had moved to another state after the breakup, refused to return the ring.
The man sued the woman in a federal district court to recover the expenses and the engagement ring, which totaled over $100,000. He seeks to possess the ring pending the outcome of the litigation on the merits.
Which of the following provisional remedies would most likely accomplish the man's goal?

choices.A: Garnishment.
choices.B: Receivership.
choices.C: Replevin.
choices.D: Temporary restraining order.

questions.explanation:
Provisional remedies*
Preliminary
injunction		 Court order commanding or prohibiting specified action while the case is pending
Temporary
restraining order		 Court order commanding or prohibiting specified action for 14 days or until preliminary-injunction hearing can take place (whichever occurs first)
Attachment Seizure of person's property to secure or satisfy future judgment
Replevin Seizure of personal property in defendant's possession that is transferred to plaintiff's possession pending outcome of suit
Garnishment Court order directing third party to hold indebted party's assets (eg, wages) until further judicial notice
Receivership Appointment of neutral third party to manage & administer disputed assets/property

*A federal court can issue any provisional remedy provided under the law of the state where the court is located.

Provisional remedies are temporary remedies issued before trial that are designed to maintain the status quo until a final judgment is rendered. Such remedies include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Garnishment – a court order directing a third party (eg, bank or employer) to hold onto an indebted party's assets (eg, employee's wages) until the court provides further notice (Choice A)
  • Receivership – a court order appointing a neutral third party (ie, receiver) to manage and administer disputed assets and/or property (often used against companies in bankruptcy proceedings) (Choice B)
  • Temporary restraining order – a court order commanding or prohibiting specified action for 14 days or until a preliminary-injunction hearing can take place—whichever occurs first
  • Replevin – a court order seizing property possessed by the defendant and transferring it to the plaintiff pending the outcome of the lawsuit

Here, the man (plaintiff) seeks to possess his great-grandmother's ring for the duration of his suit against the woman (defendant). Since a court order of replevin would force the woman to physically turn over the ring to the man pending the outcome of the litigation—not just for 14 days or until a preliminary-injunction hearing occurs—replevin would best accomplish the man's goal (Choice D).

📌 Educational Objective

Provisional remedies are temporary remedies that maintain the status quo until a final judgment is issued. Replevin is a provisional remedy that allows the court to seize property possessed by the defendant and transfer it to the plaintiff pending the outcome of the lawsuit.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 64 (provisional remedies).

一对订婚的伴侣在计划婚礼前一个月分手。分手后，男方要求女方赔偿他与婚礼相关的费用，并归还那枚曾属于他曾祖母的订婚戒指。女方在分手后已搬到另一个州，并拒绝归还戒指。

男方向联邦地区法院提起诉讼，要求女方赔偿费用并归还订婚戒指，总价值超过10万美元。他寻求在实体诉讼结果出来之前占有该戒指。

以下哪种临时补救措施最有可能实现男方的目标？

zh-choices.A: 扣押令 (Garnishment)。
zh-choices.B: 财产接管 (Receivership)。
zh-choices.C: 返还动产之诉 (Replevin)。
zh-choices.D: 临时限制令 (Temporary restraining order)。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Miscellaneous

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：法院在审理前能不能用临时救济（provisional remedy），先把对方手里的具体财物交到原告手上。

三秒认题路径：

要先拿到物 → 物在被告手里 → 要移交原告 → 选能取物的救济 → replevin

核心法律规则

Replevin（返还占有令）考场意思：把被告现在拿着的动产先交给原告，等官司打完再说谁最终赢。

Garnishment（扣押第三人财产）考场意思：卡住的是第三方手里的钱或工资，不是把物直接从被告手里拿走。

Receivership（接管人制度）考场意思：是找中立第三人管理争议财产，不是把标的物直接转给原告。

Temporary restraining order（临时限制令）考场意思：是命令或禁止某个行为，重点是行为，不是把戒指这种物直接移交。

核心判例： 本题依 Fed. R. Civ. P. 64 的思路看州法临时救济；能直接把被告占有的戒指交给原告的，就是 replevin。

思维导图

戒指在被告手里 争点：能不能先拿回
→
原告要“现在占有” 不是只要钱赔偿
→
返还型救济 直接移交给原告
先问：原告要的是“先拿到物”还是“先冻住钱/命令行为”？
要先拿到物：看 replevin → 把被告占有的动产转给原告。
只想保全资产：看 garnishment / attachment → 先锁财产，不直接交物。
只想禁止行为：看 TRO / injunction → 管行为，不管占有。
卡死结论：题干要的是“把戒指交到原告手里”，所以不是 TRO，也不是 garnishment，而是 replevin。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：戒指是婚约财物，先发个TRO把它“冻结”住就行。

但考试真正问的是：原告要的不是“别动它”，而是“先把它交给我”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的东西有没有还在原地」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 seeks to possess the ring pending the outcome，说明他要的是先把被告手里的戒指交到自己手上；这正是 replevin。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 third party 扣押错看成直接取回戒指了。

❌ 法律适用 | 管理对象错位

✕ B: 这是找中立人管财产，不是把戒指交给原告。

❌ 事实误判 | 物转行为偷换

✕ D: prohibiting 只能禁动作，不能完成交付占有。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看原告想要的是“占有转移”还是“行为限制”，再对照救济类型秒选。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“要先拿到物，找 replevin；要先冻资产，找 garnishment；要禁行为，找 TRO。”

reason.en: Specifies the category of legal relief sought before a final judgment on the merits.

reason.en: Identifies the disputed item as personal property rather than real property or money damages.
reason.zh: 将争议标的明确为个人动产，而非不动产或金钱赔偿。

keywords.text: possess the ring pending the outcome

reason.en: Signals the plaintiff's desire to hold the physical property while the lawsuit is active.
reason.zh: 表明原告在诉讼进行期间持有该有形财产的意图。

reason.en: Indicates that federal procedural rules apply, which incorporate state law provisional remedies.
reason.zh: 表明适用联邦诉讼程序规则（其引入了州法规定的暂时性救济）。

reason.en: Incorrect because it is used to seize assets held by third parties (like wages or bank accounts) rather than direct property from a defendant.
reason.zh: 错误，因为它是用于扣押第三方持有的资产（如工资或银行账户），而非直接从被告处收回特定财产。

reason.en: Incorrect because it appoints a neutral third party to manage disputed property, rather than granting possession directly to the plaintiff.
reason.zh: 错误，因为它是指派中立第三方管理争议财产，而非直接将占有权交给原告。

reason.en: Correct because it allows the court to seize personal property from the defendant and transfer possession to the plaintiff during the lawsuit.
reason.zh: 正确，因为它允许法院扣押被告占有的动产，并在诉讼期间将占有权移交给原告。

reason.en: Incorrect because it only prohibits or commands action for a limited duration and does not transfer physical possession of personal property to the plaintiff.
reason.zh: 错误，因为其仅在有限时间内禁止或要求实施某种行为，并不将动产的实际占有权转移给原告。

highlights.text: possess the ring pending the outcome of the litigation on the merits

reason.en: This is the core objective of the plaintiff that directly matches the definition and purpose of replevin.
reason.zh: 这是原告的核心目标，直接对应 replevin（占有物返还）的定义和目的。

highlights.text: provisional remedies

reason.en: Points the analysis to pre-trial remedies designed to maintain the status quo or protect assets.
reason.zh: 将分析指向旨在维持现状或保护资产的审前救济手段。

highlights.text: return the engagement ring

reason.en: Identifies that the case involves a specific item of personal property, which is necessary for a replevin remedy.
reason.zh: 明确本案涉及一件特定的动产，这是适用 replevin 救济的必要前提条件。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A homeowners' association sued a federal agency in a federal district court to enjoin the agency from issuing a license to a fracking company to drill near the homeowners' association's neighborhood. An environmental group that owns a park in the neighborhood seeks to join and fully participate in that case to obtain the same remedy as the homeowners' association.
What action should the environmental group take to achieve its goal?

choices.A: File a motion to intervene as a matter of right.
choices.B: File a motion to join as an indispensable party.
choices.C: File a motion to permissibly intervene.
choices.D: File an amicus brief.

questions.explanation:
Intervention
(FRCP 24)
Intervention of
right		 • On timely motion, court must permit intervention when either:
◦ nonparty's interest in case not adequately represented by existing parties & deciding case may impair nonparty's ability to protect that interest
◦ federal statute gives unconditional right to intervene
Permissive
intervention		 • On timely motion, court may permit intervention when either:
◦ nonparty's claim or defense shares common question of law or fact with main action
◦ federal statute gives conditional right to intervene
• Court must consider whether intervention will unduly delay or prejudice adjudication of original parties' rights
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

The environmental group (nonparty) seeks to fully participate in the suit between the homeowners' association and the federal agency. A nonparty can join and fully participate in a pending suit to protect his/her interest by filing a motion to intervene under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 24. There are two types of intervention:

  • Intervention of right – the court must permit intervention when (1) the nonparty's interest is inadequately represented by the existing parties and (2) deciding the case may impair the nonparty's ability to protect that interest
  • Permissive intervention – the court may permit intervention when the nonparty's claim or defense shares a common question of law or fact with the main action*

The environmental group likely cannot intervene as a matter of right since the homeowners' association will adequately represent the group's interest in its park (Choice A). This is because both entities seek to enjoin the federal agency from issuing a fracking license near the neighborhood. But since both claims share common questions of law and fact, the group should file a motion to permissibly intervene in the case.

*Intervention is also allowed when a federal statute gives a person an unconditional or conditional right to intervene (not seen here).

(Choice B) Only a party may file an FRCP 19 motion to join an indispensable party. But the group is not indispensable because (1) complete relief can be provided to the existing parties, (2) the group can protect its park through future litigation, and (3) no threat of inconsistent obligations exists since the entities seek the same remedy.

(Choice D) An amicus (ie, friend-of-the-court) brief is a legal document filed by a nonparty that provides the court with relevant information to help it decide the disputed issues. But amicus briefs do not allow the nonparty to fully participate in the case and are most commonly filed in appeals.

📌 Educational Objective

A nonparty may intervene (1) as a matter of right, if the nonparty's interest is inadequately represented and a decision may impair the nonparty's ability to protect that interest or (2) permissively, if the nonparty's claim or defense shares a common question of law or fact with the main action.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 14 (intervention).
questions.zh-question:
一个业主协会在联邦地区法院起诉一个联邦机构，请求法院下达禁令，禁止该机构向一家水力压裂公司颁发在其社区附近进行钻探的许可证。一个在该社区拥有一座公园的环保组织，寻求加入并完全参与该案件，以获得与业主协会相同的救济。

该环保组织应采取何种行动以实现其目标？

zh-choices.A: 提起一项作为权利的参加诉讼动议。
zh-choices.B: 提起一项作为不可或缺的当事人加入的动议。
zh-choices.C: 提起一项经许可参加诉讼的动议。
zh-choices.D: 提交一份法庭之友意见书。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Intervention

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：非当事人想进场并全程参与，应该走 介入（intervention），而不是硬塞成 不可或缺当事人（indispensable party） 或只交 amicus brief。

三秒认题路径：

非当事人 → 想加入 → 共通争点 → 介入申请 → 选 C

核心法律规则

FRCP 24 讲的是 介入（intervention）：非当事人如果想加入正在进行的诉讼，可以申请 介入权（intervention of right） 或 许可介入（permissive intervention）。

介入权（intervention of right） 要看两步：现有当事人没有充分代表你的利益，而且判决会妨碍你保护该利益。许可介入（permissive intervention） 则更宽，只要你的主张或抗辩和主案有共同法律或事实问题，法院就可以让你进来。

这题里，环保组织和业主协会都想阻止联邦机构发牌，所以共同争点很明显；但协会已经在打同一场仗，环保组织要靠的是 许可介入（permissive intervention），不是 介入权（intervention of right）。

核心判例： 这题不靠特定判例取胜，直接用 FRCP 24：有共同争点就先想许可介入。

思维导图

非当事人想“全程参加”这场官司？
先看：是不是在找 介入（intervention），而不是 amicus brief。
再分：
介入权（intervention of right）
要件1：现有当事人代表得不够？
要件2：判决会不会妨碍你保护利益？
本题卡死：协会已在做同一件事，利益代表不差。
许可介入（permissive intervention）
关卡：你的主张和主案有没有共同法律/事实问题？
本题通过：两边都在阻止同一张 fracking license。
终点：能进场，但走的是 C：许可介入

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然环保组织也想要同样的禁令，那它是不是当然能 as a matter of right 进来？

但考试真正问的是：现有原告已经把同一目标打出来了，环保组织并不是非靠 介入权（intervention of right） 才能保护利益；题眼在“能不能以共同争点申请加入”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的利益有没有重叠」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 双方都在阻止同一许可，说明存在共同法律与事实问题，所以非当事人应走许可介入。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 不是自动当然介入；adequately represented 这个点反而削弱介入权。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ B: 你把 indispensable party 搬错了，题目要的是加入诉讼，不是强拉必需当事人。

❌ 事实误判 | 题干条件偷换

✕ D: amicus brief 只能帮忙说话，不能让它全程参与案件。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看非当事人想要“加入并参与”还是只是“帮忙发声”，再用共同争点快速锁定许可介入。

考场速记

记住：介入权（intervention of right） 看“代表不够＋会受影响”，许可介入（permissive intervention） 看“有共同争点＋法院愿不愿意”。

口诀：先问“我是不是要进场”，再问“是不是同一场仗”，最后再分 intervention of right 还是 permissive intervention。

A.text: intervene as a matter of right

reason.en: Incorrect because submitting a brief does not allow full participation as a party.
reason.zh: 错误，因为提交陈述书不允许其作为当事人全面参与诉讼。

label.zh: 参加诉讼的目的与相同救济

reason.en: Focuses the question on the correct motion or procedure for the nonparty to enter the case.

highlights.text: owns a park in the neighborhood

reason.en: Establishes that the environmental group has an interest related to the property or transaction.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An electrician and a plumber filed separate diversity actions against a construction company in which they both claim that the company failed to pay them the amount specified in their contracts. The company defended on the ground that the electrician and plumber failed to complete their work on time. The electrician served a request for admission on the company, requesting that the company admit that it repeatedly denied contractors such as the electrician access to the construction site. The company did not respond to the request.
Forty-five days after the electrician's request was served, the plumber asked the court during a pretrial conference to enter an order conclusively establishing the fact that the company repeatedly denied contractors access to the construction site. The plumber relied on the company's failure to timely respond to the electrician's request for admission.
Is the court likely to enter the order?

choices.A: No, because the construction company has sixty days to respond to the electrician's request for admission.
choices.B: No, because the plumber cannot rely on the construction company's failure to respond to the request for admission in the electrician's action.
choices.C: Yes, because the construction company's failure to respond to the electrician's request for admission within 30 days after service is treated as an admission.
choices.D: Yes, because the court has the authority to enter orders at pretrial conferences that will expedite litigation.

questions.explanation:
Effect of response to request for admission
(FRCP 36)
Written response
(due within 30 days of service)
Fail to respond
Admit matter
Matter conclusively
established
Deny matter
Explain lack of admission/denial
Object to request
Matter not conclusively
established

In a request for admission, a party requests that another party admit the truth about matters within the scope of discovery that relate to facts, the application of law to facts, opinions about either, or the genuineness of documents. The party served with such a request must serve a written response within 30 days that:

• admits the matter
• specifically denies the matter in whole or in part
• explains why the matter cannot be admitted or denied or
• objects that the matter falls outside the scope of discovery.

A party's failure to adequately respond within 30 days results in the matter being admitted and conclusively established in the pending action. However, it does not serve as an admission for any other purpose and cannot be used against the party in another proceeding.

Here, the electrician and the plumber filed separate actions against the construction company. The electrician then served the company with a request to admit that it repeatedly denied contractors access to the construction site. The company's failure to respond within 30 days after the request was served results in the matter being established in the electrician's action (Choice A). However, the plumber cannot rely on the company's failure to respond in the electrician's action, so the court is unlikely to enter the plumber's requested order (Choice C).

(Choice D) At a pretrial conference, a federal court has broad authority to consider matters and enter appropriate orders that will help expedite litigation, improve the trial's quality, and facilitate settlement. Here, an order establishing that the company repeatedly denied contractors access to the construction site would be improper since the plumber cannot rely on the company's failure to respond in the electrician's action.

📌 Educational Objective

A party's failure to adequately respond to a request for admission within 30 days after the request is served results in the matter being admitted and conclusively established in the pending action. However, it does not serve as an admission for any other purpose and cannot be used against the party in another proceeding.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 36 (requests for admission).
  • 8B Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2264 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining the effect of failing to respond to a request for admission).
questions.zh-question:
一名电工和一名水管工分别对一家建筑公司提起了独立的多元管辖权诉讼（diversity actions），他们都声称该公司未能支付其合同中规定的款项。该公司辩称，电工和水管工未能按时完成工作。电工向该公司送达了一份承认请求（request for admission），要求该公司承认其曾多次拒绝电工等承包商进入施工现场。该公司未对该请求作出回应。

在电工的请求送达四十五天后，水管工在一次庭前会议上请求法院下达一项命令，以确凿地认定该公司曾多次拒绝承包商进入施工现场这一事实。水管工的依据是该公司未能及时回应电工的承认请求。

法院是否可能下达该命令？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为建筑公司有六十天的时间来回应电工的承认请求。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为在电工的诉讼中，水管工不能依赖建筑公司未能回应承认请求这一事实。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为建筑公司未在送达后30天内回应电工的承认请求，这被视为一种承认。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为法院有权在庭前会议上下达旨在加快诉讼进程的命令。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery Devices

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：请求承认（request for admission）的失权只在同一案件里生效，不能拿去别的案件里当作自动成立的事实。

三秒认题路径：

请求承认 → 30天不答 → 仅本案成立 → 换案不能用 → 选否

核心法律规则

把规则说成考场动作

请求承认（request for admission）要求对方承认某个事实、法律适用事实、意见，或文件真伪；收到后30天内必须书面回应，否则该事项在当前案件里会被视为承认并 conclusively established。

但这份“默认承认”不能用于其他诉讼（another proceeding）。所以这题里，电工那案子里没答，不代表水管工这个案子里也能直接拿来当已成立事实。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 36 — 不答的后果只锁定在被送达的那一案，不能跨案搬运。

思维导图

Day 0
电工送达请求承认
Day 30
公司不回应 → 仅在电工案内视为承认
Day 45
水管工在pretrial conference想直接借用
结论关卡
不能跨案使用 → 法院不该下该命令

考点陷阱

你可能会想：公司都没答了，admitted 不就自动成立吗？

但考试真正问的是：这个默认承认能不能被另一个案件拿来直接当事实。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 电工案里的不回应 只会让该案事实成立，不能被水管工拿来跨案证明，所以法院不太会下这个命令。

❌ 事实误判 | 六十天偷换

✕ A: 你把 sixty days 硬塞进来，但题目明写是30天。

❌ 法律适用 | 跨案搬运

✕ C: 把电工案的默认承认直接搬到水管工案，命题人就在骗你忽略“仅本案有效”。

❌ 概念混淆 | 预会议权能误判

✕ D: 预审会议权力很大，但不能拿来造出一个本来无权跨案使用的事实。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看证据后果只绑定哪一案，再判断有没有被偷换成“另一案也能用”。

考场速记

记住一句：request for admission 的“不答=承认”，只在同一 pending action 里生效；换案就失效。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A sailor filed a diversity action against a defendant in a federal district court to recover damages for injuries sustained in a boating accident. The district court ordered the attorneys for both parties to attend the first pretrial conference, but the sailor's attorney failed to appear. This was the first and only hearing that the attorney failed to attend. As a result, the district court entered an order dismissing the sailor's action with prejudice. The court also ordered the sailor to pay the expenses incurred by the defendant for attending the conference. The sailor immediately appealed.
What is the sailor's best argument for persuading the appellate court to reverse the dismissal?

choices.A: The dismissal was unreasonable because the attorney had not shown a pattern of noncompliance or disobedience.
choices.B: The dismissal was unwarranted because the sailor was also ordered to pay the defendant's expenses.
choices.C: The district court committed clear error when it dismissed the case before trial.
choices.D: The district court may sanction a party only when it fails to obey a pretrial order.

questions.explanation:
Sanctions for noncompliance with
pretrial conference or order
(FRCP 16)
Sanctionable conduct
  • Failure to attend pretrial conference
  • Substantially unprepared for conference
  • No good-faith participation in conference
  • Failure to obey pretrial order
↓
Required sanction
Payment of reasonable expenses unless:
  • noncompliance substantially justified or
  • award of expenses is unjust
↓
Permissible sanctions
  • Dismiss action in whole or in part
  • Strike pleadings in whole or in part
  • Hold in contempt of court
  • Issue default judgment
  • Prohibit use of evidence
  • Stay further proceedings
(Mnemonic: D-SHIPS)

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

Pretrial conferences are designed to improve the quality of trial, facilitate settlement, and expedite litigation. To underscore the importance of these conferences, a federal court typically must order* a party and/or attorney to pay the other party's reasonable expenses when the party or attorney:

• failed to attend a pretrial conference
• was substantially unprepared for the conference
• did not participate in good faith in the conference or
• failed to obey a pretrial order.

In addition to ordering the payment of expenses, the court may impose sanctions on the noncompliant party or attorney (Choice B). The court has discretion to decide which sanction to impose, but the sanction must be reasonable under the circumstances—ie, the punishment must fit the violation. Otherwise, an arbitrary or unreasonable sanction will be reversed on appeal for abuse of discretion.

Here, the district court dismissed the sailor's action with prejudice because the sailor's attorney failed to attend the initial pretrial conference. Dismissal of an action is one of the harshest sanctions and is appropriate to punish a pattern of disobedience or noncompliance (not seen here). Therefore, the sailor's best argument to reverse the dismissal is that this sanction was unreasonable under the circumstances.

*A court should not order the payment of the other party's reasonable expenses when (1) the noncompliance was substantially justified or (2) the payment would be unjust.

(Choice C) A district court's factual findings in a bench trial are reviewed for clear error and will only be reversed if no reasonable judge would have made such a finding. But here, the district court's discretionary decision to sanction the sailor's attorney and dismiss the sailor's action with prejudice before trial will be reviewed for abuse of discretion.

(Choice D) A district court may sanction a party if it failed to attend, did not participate in good faith, or was substantially unprepared for a pretrial conference—not just when it failed to obey a pretrial order.

📌 Educational Objective

A federal court must order the payment of the other party's reasonable expenses and may impose reasonable sanctions on any attorney or party who (1) failed to attend a pretrial conference, (2) was substantially unprepared for the conference, (3) did not participate in good faith in the conference, or (4) failed to obey a pretrial order.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(f) (pretrial conference sanctions).
  • 6A Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 1531 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining when sanctions are appropriate for failure to comply with pretrial conference or order).
questions.zh-question:
一名水手在联邦地区法院对一名被告提起了多元管辖权诉讼（diversity action），要求赔偿因船只事故所受的伤害。地区法院命令双方律师参加首次审前会议，但该水手的律师未能出席。这是该律师第一次也是唯一一次未能出席的听证会。因此，地区法院下达了一项命令，以有既判力的方式（with prejudice）驳回了该水手的诉讼。法院还命令该水手支付被告因参加会议而产生的费用。该水手立即提起了上诉。

该水手说服上诉法院推翻该驳回裁定的最佳论点是什么？

zh-choices.A: 该驳回裁定是不合理的，因为该律师并未表现出持续不遵守或不服从的行为模式。
zh-choices.B: 该驳回裁定是不正当的，因为该水手同时也被命令支付被告的费用。
zh-choices.C: 地区法院在审判前驳回案件时犯了明显错误（clear error）。
zh-choices.D: 地区法院仅当一方当事人未能遵守审前命令时，才可对其进行制裁。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery Scope and Limits

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：预审会议（pretrial conference）缺席后，法院能不能用驳回且带有偏见（dismissal with prejudice）这种重罚，以及上诉时要抓“是否过重”。

三秒认题路径：

缺席会议 → 16(f) → 可罚 → 罚要合理 → 过重就撤

核心法律规则

联邦民事诉讼规则 FRCP 16(f) 允许法院因为没参加预审会议（pretrial conference）、准备不足、未善意参与，或不服从预审命令（pretrial order）而制裁当事人或律师。

除了要求支付对方的合理费用（reasonable expenses），法院还可以加更重的制裁，但前提是罚要和违规相称，不能随手上最狠的招。

所以这题的关键不是“能不能罚”，而是“dismissal with prejudice 对一次性缺席是否太重”。

核心判例： 题目材料对应 FRCP 16(f) 的制裁逻辑：法院可罚，但重罚必须合理；对首次、单次缺席直接驳回，通常太狠。

思维导图

先看违规类型：是否属于 16(f) 可罚行为？
是：未出席预审会议
进入制裁分析：法院可以罚，但罚要“合理”
再看法院选了什么制裁？
轻罚：支付对方合理费用 → 通常稳
重罚：dismissal with prejudice → 只适合更严重、反复的不配合
本题是“第一次、唯一一次缺席” → 没有模式性违抗 → 重罚过头
上诉怎么打？
主攻：这次制裁unreasonable
别选：把它说成事实认定错误或只盯费用命令
结论：可撤的是“驳回太重”，不是“法院有权处罚”

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然律师没来，法院都已经判了，那就应该支持这个dismissal with prejudice。

但考试真正问的是：第一次违纪就直接上最狠制裁，是不是过重、是否滥用了裁量权。

这题看的是“制裁是否合理”，不是看当事人有没有犯错。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 首次且唯一一次缺席预审会议，却被直接 dismissed with prejudice；这像是罚过头了，最强 аргумент 就是“没有持续违抗模式，所以制裁不合理”。

❌ 事实误判 | 费用命令偷换

✕ B: 把 expenses 当成驳回理由，但付费用不妨碍再加别的制裁。

❌ 法律适用 | 复审标准错位

✕ C: 想用 clear error，但这题是裁量制裁，重点不是事实认定。

❌ 概念混淆 | 触发条件缩窄

✕ D: 把可罚情形缩成只剩 pretrial order，漏掉了缺席和不善意参与。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓程序姿态：看 16(f) 有没有权罚，再问重罚是否与这次单次违纪相称。

考场速记

记忆口诀：D-SHIPS = Dismiss、Strike、Hold in contempt、Issue default judgment、Prohibit evidence、Stay proceedings。

看到预审会议违纪，先背一句：可以罚，但罚要合理；第一次就驳回，通常太重。

reason.en: The proceeding which the attorney failed to attend, triggering the court's authority to sanction.

reason.zh: 表明律师的未出席是个别事件，而非持续的不合规行为模式。

label.zh: 不合规或不服从的模式

reason.en: A pattern is typically required to justify the extreme sanction of dismissal with prejudice.

reason.en: Paying expenses is a standard sanction and does not preclude other reasonable sanctions.
reason.zh: 支付费用是一项标准制裁，并不排除法院施加其他合理的制裁。

reason.en: Distractor representing an incorrect standard of review; sanctions are reviewed for abuse of discretion.
reason.zh: 干扰项，代表了错误的审查标准；法院施加的制裁应按‘滥用自由裁量权’标准进行审查。

D.text: fails to obey a pretrial order

reason.en: Narrowly states only one ground for sanctions, omitting failure to attend a conference.
reason.zh: 狭隘地只列出了施加制裁的一种理由，忽略了未出席会议这一情况。

highlights.text: first and only hearing that the attorney failed to attend

reason.en: This key fact shows the lack of a pattern of disobedience, making dismissal with prejudice unreasonable.
reason.zh: 这一关键事实表明不存在持续不服从的模式，使得有偏见驳回诉讼的制裁显得不合理。

highlights.text: dismissing the sailor's action with prejudice

reason.en: Dismissal with prejudice is a harsh sanction of last resort, generally requiring severe or repeated misconduct.
reason.zh: 有偏见驳回是最后的严厉制裁手段，通常要求存在严重或重复的不当行为。

highlights.text: failed to appear

reason.en: The event that permitted the court to issue Rule 16(f) sanctions in the first place.
reason.zh: 最初允许法院依据联邦民事诉讼规则第16(f)条施加制裁的事件。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A consumer filed a class action in federal court on behalf of millions of users of a social media site for $100 million, claiming that the corporation that owns the site shared the users' data without their consent. The court certified the class action after determining that common questions of law and fact predominated and that the class action was the best method to fairly and efficiently adjudicate the dispute. Notice was sent by email to users of the social media site, informing them of their right to opt out of the class action. However, due to a technical error, a certain group of users was never sent the notice. The class eventually reached a settlement with the corporation, and the court entered an order dismissing the class action with prejudice.
Two months later, the group of users who never received notice of the first class action filed an identical class action against the same corporation in federal court. The corporation moved to dismiss.
How will the court likely rule on the corporation's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because email is not an appropriate means to send notice of a class action.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the group had no opportunity to opt out of the first class action.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because notice of the first class action was appropriately provided under the circumstances.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the first class action was dismissed with prejudice.

questions.explanation:
Adequate notice for class action
Contents Notice must clearly & concisely state in plain language:
  • nature of action
  • definition of class
  • claims, issues, or defenses
  • class member may appear through attorney
  • court will exclude member who opts out of class
  • time & manner for opting out and
  • binding effect of class judgment
Delivery Court must provide notice by most practical means—including individual notice to reasonably identifiable members
Costs Plaintiff bears cost of notifying members of class action

A federal court has the power to certify (ie, authorize) the following types of class actions:

  • Prejudicial risk – separate actions would create a risk of (1) inconsistent decisions regarding the parties or (2) impairing absent class members' interests
  • Common question – common questions of law or fact predominate over individual questions, and a class action is the best method to fairly and efficiently adjudicate the dispute (as seen here)
  • Final equitable relief – injunctive or declaratory relief is appropriate because the opposing party's actions generally apply to the whole class

In a "common question" class action, adequate notice must be provided to all class members because they have the right to opt out of the class action and sue on their own behalf.* Notice must be provided by the most practical means under the circumstances, including U.S. mail, email, or other reasonable means. A class member who receives notice but fails to opt out cannot pursue a subsequent suit involving the same claim.

(Choice A) Here, notice of the first class action against the corporation was appropriately provided by email to users of the social media site (Choice A). However, a group of users never received this notice due to a technical error and had no opportunity to opt out of the first class action. As a result, the group may pursue a subsequent class action against the corporation involving the same claim, and the court will likely deny the corporation's motion to dismiss (Choice C).

*In "prejudicial risk" and "final equitable relief" class actions, notice is not required because class members do not have a right to opt out. Instead, a court has the discretion to provide notice and an opportunity to opt out of such class actions.

(Choice D) The court order dismissing the first class action with prejudice means that the members of that class action cannot sue on the same claim in the future. However, it does not prevent the group from asserting the same claim since the group was not provided with notice and had no opportunity to opt out.

📌 Educational Objective

In a "common question" class action, adequate notice must be provided to all class members because they have the right to opt out of the class action. A class member who receives such notice but fails to opt out cannot pursue a subsequent suit involving the same claim.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(c)(2) (notice requirements for "common question" class action).
  • 7AA Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 167; 1786 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining the notice requirements for a "common question" class action).
questions.zh-question:
一名消费者代表数百万社交媒体网站用户在联邦法院提起集体诉讼，索赔1亿美元，声称拥有该网站的公司未经用户同意分享了他们的数据。法院在确定法律和事实上的共同问题占主导地位，并且集体诉讼是公平有效地裁决该争议的最佳方法后，认证了该集体诉讼。通知通过电子邮件发送给该社交媒体网站的用户，告知他们有权选择退出该集体诉讼。然而，由于技术错误，某一群用户从未收到该通知。该集体最终与公司达成了和解，法院下达了命令，以有既判力地（with prejudice）驳回了该集体诉讼。

两个月后，那群从未收到第一次集体诉讼通知的用户，在联邦法院对同一家公司提起了完全相同的集体诉讼。该公司动议驳回起诉。

法院很可能会如何裁定该公司的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为电子邮件不是发送集体诉讼通知的适当方式。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为该群体没有机会选择退出第一次集体诉讼。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为在当时的情况下，第一次集体诉讼的通知已经适当送达。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为第一次集体诉讼被有既判力地驳回了。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：共同争议类（common question）集体诉讼里，某些成员没收到通知、也没机会退出时，能不能再就同一请求另起一案。

三秒认题路径：

共同争议类 → 要可退出 → 没收通知 → 没法退出 → 可再起诉

核心法律规则

共同争议类（common question class action）里，成员有退出权（right to opt out），所以法院必须用最实际的方式发出足够通知，常见就是邮件或其他合理方式。充分通知（adequate notice）的考试意思：你得先知道这案子，再决定要不要离开它。

如果某个成员收到了通知但没退出，他以后通常不能再就同一主张单独起诉；但如果他根本没收到通知、也就没机会退出，preclusion 就很难套上去。

这里的关键不是“法院有没有发过邮件”，而是“这个具体成员有没有真的收到、能不能退出”。

核心判例： 依据 Fed. R. Civ. P. 23(c)(2) 的通知规则，本题锁定结论：没收到通知、没机会退出的成员，不会被前案和解当然挡住。

思维导图

先看这类集体诉讼是共同争议类（common question）吗？
是成员有退出权（opt out） → 法院要发充分通知（adequate notice）
通知到了 能退出却没退 → 不能再就同一请求重提
通知没到 也就没法退出 → 不被前案绑定，可再起诉
本题事实：邮件本来可行，但这组人因技术错误根本没收到。
结论 他们没有真实退出机会 → 法院应驳回被告的驳回动议

考点陷阱

你可能会想：前案都已经with prejudice 了，后案当然完了。

但考试真正问的是：这批成员有没有拿到通知、从而有机会退出；如果连退出机会都没有，前案的终局效力不一定能挡住他们。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的通知是不是曾经被系统发过」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 never received this notice，所以这组人没有退出机会；在可退出的共同争议类里，没通知就不能把他们挡在同一请求之外。

❌ 概念混淆 | 通知方式误判

✕ A: 把 email 直接说成不行，忽略了题干其实问的是这批人有没有收到通知。

❌ 法律适用 | 适当送达误判

✕ C: 只盯着“邮件能用”这半句，漏掉了这组成员根本没收到。

❌ 事实误判 | 终局效力偷换

✕ D: 把 with prejudice 当成对所有人当然封死，但题干这组人从没被通知过。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定是否是可退出的共同争议类，再看每个成员有没有真正收到通知。

考场速记

记忆口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉常用口诀；但本题更要记住：可退出的集体诉讼里，没收到通知 = 没机会退出 = 通常还能另起同案。

question_analysis.skill_tested: determine binding effect of class action judgment

reason.en: Identifies the specific procedural context of the litigation.
reason.zh: 确认诉讼的特定诉讼程序背景。

keywords.text: common questions of law and fact predominated

reason.en: Triggers notice and opt-out requirements that must be met to bind class members.
reason.zh: 触发必须满足以约束集体成员的通知和退出权要求。

reason.en: Crucial fact showing that this group's due process rights were not satisfied.

keywords.text: dismissing the class action with prejudice

reason.en: Normally bars future litigation, but only for bound class members.
reason.zh: 通常禁止未来的诉讼，但仅限于受约束的集体成员。

reason.en: Procedural mechanism to assert claim preclusion.
reason.zh: 主张诉讼系属/既判力的程序机制。

A.text: email is not an appropriate means

reason.en: Incorrectly claims email is invalid; Rule 23 allows notice by email if practical.
reason.zh: 错误地声称电子邮件无效；民诉规则第23条允许在可行时通过电子邮件通知。

B.text: had no opportunity to opt out

reason.en: Correct legal basis for denying the motion to dismiss because the group is not bound.
reason.zh: 驳回该驳回起诉申请的正确法律依据，因为该群体不受原判决约束。

C.text: notice of the first class action was appropriately provided

reason.en: Misapplies the rule by ignoring that notice must actually reach identifiable members to bind them.
reason.zh: 错误适用规则，忽略了通知必须实际送达可识别的成员才能约束他们。

reason.zh: 该抗辩不能成立，因为既判力只拘束收到通知的集体成员。

highlights.text: common questions of law and fact predominated and that the class action was the best method to fairly and efficiently adjudicate the dispute

reason.zh: 触发第23(c)(2)(B)条规定的强制性通知和退出权要求。

highlights.text: due to a technical error, a certain group of users was never sent the notice

reason.en: Establishes that this specific group was not notified and retains the right to sue.
reason.zh: 确定该特定群体未被通知，并保留起诉权。

highlights.text: dismissing the class action with prejudice

reason.en: Represents the judgment that would normally bind the parties but does not bind this group.
reason.zh: 代表通常会约束各方当事人的判决，但此处不约束该群体。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A shopper brought a federal diversity action in federal court against a grocery store for negligence based on a slip and fall on the grocery store's premises. The shopper's complaint alleged that the grocery store negligently failed to clean a liquid spill on the floor—a spill that its employees were aware of. The failure to clean the spill caused the shopper to slip and fall, resulting in permanent injuries to her leg. The grocery store's answer contained a general denial, stating that it denied every allegation in the complaint.
After the shopper received the grocery store's answer, she immediately filed a motion for summary judgment. In support of her motion, the shopper submitted three affidavits—two from other shoppers and one from a former employee of the store, each fully supporting the shopper's version of the event. The grocery store did not submit any affidavits or other evidence in opposition to the motion.
Should the court grant the shopper's motion for summary judgment?

choices.A: Yes, because the grocery store failed to submit evidence showing a genuine issue of fact for trial.
choices.B: Yes, because the evidence, when viewed in the light most favorable to the shopper, demonstrates the lack of a genuine dispute.
choices.C: No, because the general denial in the grocery store's answer is sufficient to demonstrate a genuine dispute for trial.
choices.D: No, because the shopper failed to meet the burden of persuasion.

questions.explanation:
Burden of proof for summary judgment
Movant proves:
No genuine dispute of material
fact & entitled to JMOL by:
  • pleadings
  • affidavits/declarations
  • discovery or
  • other materials
Burden shifts to nonmovant
Nonmovant proves either:
Specific disputed facts by:
  • affidavits/declarations
  • discovery or
  • other materials
Summary judgment denied
Additional discovery needed
to establish essential facts by:
  • affidavits/declarations
Consideration of summary
judgment postponed
JMOL = Judgment as a matter of law.

A motion for summary judgment requests that the court enter judgment without a full trial because (1) there is no genuine dispute of material fact and (2) the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. This motion may be filed at any time until 30 days after the close of discovery. The movant must support this motion with admissible facts contained in pleadings, affidavits, declarations, discovery materials, or other materials containing admissible evidence.

Once the movant satisfies this initial burden, the burden shifts to the nonmovant to avoid summary judgment by:

  • showing specific disputed facts through affidavits, declarations, discovery materials, or other materials containing admissible evidence or
  • requesting that the court postpone consideration of the motion until additional discovery can take place, and including an affidavit or declaration that describes the desired discovery and why it is needed.

Here, the shopper (movant) supported her motion for summary judgment with three affidavits in which witnesses supported the shopper's version of events. This likely satisfied the shopper's initial burden of proof, so the burden shifted to the grocery store (nonmovant). But the grocery store failed to submit any evidence in opposition to the motion that showed a genuine issue of fact for trial. Therefore, the court should grant the shopper's motion.

(Choice B) When considering a motion for summary judgment, the court must view all facts in the light most favorable to the nonmovant (the grocery store)—not the movant (the shopper).

(Choice C) A nonmovant responding to a motion for summary judgment must support the response with evidence and cannot rely on the pleadings (e.g., answer). That is because pleadings are general, and the nonmovant is required to show specific disputed facts.

(Choice D) The burden of proof is composed of the burden of production and the burden of persuasion. The shopper met both burdens here by supporting her summary judgment motion with three affidavits.

📌 Educational Objective

Once a movant satisfies its burden of proof in a motion for summary judgment, the burden shifts to the nonmovant, who must support its opposition with evidence demonstrating a genuine dispute of material fact.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 56 (summary judgment).
questions.zh-question: 一名顾客在联邦法院对一家杂货店提起了基于多元管辖权的联邦诉讼，指控该店因其店内的滑倒事故存在过失。该顾客的诉状（complaint）声称，杂货店过失地未能清理地板上的液体泼洒物——其员工对此是知情的。未能清理泼洒物导致该顾客滑倒，造成其腿部永久性损伤。杂货店的答辩状（answer）包含一项概括性否认（general denial），声明其否认诉状中的所有指控。在顾客收到杂货店的答辩状后，她立即提交了一份即决判决动议（motion for summary judgment）。为支持其动议，该顾客提交了三份宣誓书（affidavits）——两份来自其他顾客，一份来自该店的一名前员工，每份都完全支持该顾客对事件的说法。杂货店没有提交任何宣誓书或其他证据来反对该动议。法院是否应批准该顾客的即决判决动议？

zh-choices.A: 是的，因为杂货店未能提交证据表明存在可供审理的真实事实争议（genuine issue of fact）。
zh-choices.B: 是的，因为当以最有利于顾客的方式审视证据时，证据表明不存在真实争议（genuine dispute）。
zh-choices.C: 否，因为杂货店答辩状中的概括性否认足以表明存在可供审理的真实争议。
zh-choices.D: 否，因为该顾客未能履行说服责任（burden of persuasion）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Adjudication without trial

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：简易判决（summary judgment）里，movant 先用宣誓书把事实争议推到对方身上后，nonmovant 不能只靠 general denial，必须拿证据出来。

三秒认题路径：

先看 summary judgment → movant 先举证 → 对方要反证 → 只写答辩不够 → 直接判给动议方

核心法律规则

简易判决（summary judgment）的门槛是：没有 material fact 的真实争议，而且动议方有权拿到 judgment as a matter of law。考场意思：先由 movant 用诉状、affidavits、declarations、discovery 材料把初始负担做完。

一旦 movant 做到这一步，burden shifts 到 nonmovant；对方必须拿出具体争议事实，或者说明还需要额外发现。考场意思：只写 general denial 不算证据，不能挡住 summary judgment。

核心判例： Celotex 规则下，nonmovant 不能空着手硬扛；本题的 grocery store 没有提交任何反证，所以法院应当准许动议。

思维导图

movant 先交了 3 份 affidavit，把“店员知道地上有液体”这件事顶上台面了吗？
YES：初始负担已完成 → burden shifts to nonmovant
nonmovant 有没有拿证据证明“有真实争议”或要补充 discovery？
没有：只交 general denial → 不能制造 trial issue
结论：grant summary judgment → 选 A
有：才可能 deny summary judgment 或 postponement。
NO：如果 movant 自己没证据，法院不会替她补。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告在 answer 里已经否认了，所以应该算有争议。

但考试真正问的是：有没有能进法庭的证据，去说明“真的存在可审理的事实争议”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里 three affidavits 已把 movant 的初始负担做完，而 grocery store 没交任何反证，法院当然可以直接判给她。

❌ 概念混淆 | 光看最有利

✕ B: 把“最有利于非动议方”错用到 movant 身上了。

❌ 法律适用 | 答辩当证据

✕ C: 以为 general denial 就能自己造出争议。

❌ 事实误判 | 负担偷换

✕ D: 把“证明责任”说成还压在 shopper 身上，忽略了 burden 已经转移。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看 movant 是否已完成初始举证，再看 nonmovant 有没有拿出具体反证。

考场速记

记住一句：summary judgment 不是看谁更会写否认，而是看谁能拿出证据。

口诀：“先动议方举证，再看非动议方反证；只有 general denial，不够挡 summary judgment。”

question_analysis.skill_tested: Applying summary judgment burden-shifting rules

reason.en: The procedural mechanism being tested, which requires showing no genuine dispute of material fact.
reason.zh: 被测试的程序机制，要求证明不存在实质性事实的真实争议。

reason.en: Evidentiary support submitted by the movant to satisfy their initial burden.
reason.zh: 动议人提交的证据支持，用以满足其初始举证责任。

reason.en: The defendant's pleading assertion, which is insufficient by itself to defeat a supported summary judgment motion.
reason.zh: 被告的答辩主张，其本身不足以击败有证据支持的简易判决动议。

keywords.text: did not submit any affidavits or other evidence

reason.en: Trigger that shifts the outcome, as the nonmovant cannot rely solely on pleadings.
reason.zh: 导致案件结果的关键事实，因为非动议人不能仅依赖诉状陈述。

reason.en: Correctly identifies that the nonmovant failed to meet its shifted burden of production.
reason.zh: 正确指出非动议人未能满足转移后的提供证据责任。

B.text: light most favorable to the shopper

label.zh: 错误的审查标准利益归属

reason.en: Misstates the standard; facts must be viewed in the light most favorable to the nonmovant.
reason.zh: 错误表述了审查标准；事实必须以最有利于非动议人的视角进行审查。

C.text: general denial in the grocery store's answer

reason.zh: 错误地暗示仅凭起诉状/答辩状即可击败有宣誓陈述书支持的简易判决动议。

D.text: failed to meet the burden of persuasion

reason.en: Incorrectly claims the movant failed to carry the burden when they did so through affidavits.
reason.zh: 错误地声称动议人未能承担说服责任，而实际上动议人已通过宣誓书完成了该责任。

highlights.text: The grocery store's answer contained a general denial, stating that it denied every allegation in the complaint.

reason.en: Shows the grocery store only denied allegations in its pleadings and did not introduce evidence.
reason.zh: 表明杂货店仅在诉状答辩中否认了指控，并未引入证据。

highlights.text: In support of her motion, the shopper submitted three affidavits—two from other shoppers and one from a former employee of the store, each fully supporting the shopper's version of the event.

label.zh: 动议人的初始证据支持

reason.en: Demonstrates the shopper satisfied her initial burden of production, shifting the burden to the defendant.
reason.zh: 证明购物者已满足其初始举证责任，从而将责任转移给被告。

highlights.text: The grocery store did not submit any affidavits or other evidence in opposition to the motion.

label.en: nonmovant's failure to respond with evidence
label.zh: 非动议人未能提交证据进行反驳

reason.en: This failure means there is no genuine dispute of material fact, requiring the court to grant summary judgment.

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A franchisee sued a franchisor in a federal court in State A for breach of contract. The franchisee is domiciled in State B, and the franchisor's headquarters and principal place of business are in State A. The franchisee's complaint included one line about subject-matter jurisdiction that stated: "The court has subject-matter jurisdiction over this suit." In response, the franchisor filed a motion to dismiss for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
Upon reviewing the motion and the complaint, the judge issued an order to show cause to the franchisee's attorney to explain why the attorney should not be sanctioned for failing to adequately plead subject-matter jurisdiction. At the show-cause hearing, the franchisee's attorney arrived with an amended complaint to substitute for the original complaint. The judge accepted the amended complaint and denied the franchisor's motion to dismiss. The judge also imposed sanctions against the franchisee's attorney in the amount of $2,000, payable to the court.
The case proceeded, the jury returned a verdict in favor of the franchisee, and the judge issued a final judgment consistent with the verdict.
The franchisee's attorney then filed an appeal related to the court's imposition of sanctions.
What is the appellate court's likely response?

choices.A: Affirm the order imposing sanctions.
choices.B: Vacate the order imposing sanctions, because the judge accepted the amended complaint.
choices.C: Vacate the order imposing sanctions, because the judge acted sua sponte.
choices.D: Vacate the order imposing sanctions, because the judge failed to allow 21 days to pass before imposing sanctions.

questions.explanation:
Representations to court(FRCP 11(b))

Every pleading, motion, or other document filed must be signed by attorney (or unrepresented party), thereby certifying that:

  1. document is presented for proper purpose—not to harass, cause unnecessary delay, or needlessly increase cost of litigation
  2. claims, defenses & legal contentions are warranted by existing law or by nonfrivolous argument for revising or establishing law
  3. factual assertions have or will have evidentiary support and
  4. factual denials are warranted by evidence or reasonably based on belief/lack of information
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A court can impose sanctions on a law firm (default), attorney, or party if the court finds that they violated one of the provisions of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 11(b)—shown above. Sanction proceedings can be initiated by:

• an opposing party's motion – which requires that party to serve the motion on the violator but refrain from filing it with the court for 21 days to allow the violation to be corrected (ie, safe-harbor rule) or

• on the court's own initiative (ie, sua sponte) – which requires the judge to issue an order to show cause on the violator but does not require the judge to apply the safe-harbor rule.

Here, the franchisee's complaint simply alleged that the federal court "has subject-matter jurisdiction over this suit." The complaint did not include the grounds supporting this assertion as required by FRCP 8—eg, by providing the facts that established subject-matter jurisdiction. This means that the franchisee's jurisdictional claim was not warranted by law and violated FRCP 11(b)(2). As a result, the judge had the authority to initiate sanction proceedings sua sponte and impose sanctions after the show-cause hearing (Choices C & D).

Such sanctions should be sufficient to deter the violator's conduct in the future—eg, a $2,000 fine payable to the court (as seen here). However, the sanctions order can be appealed. The appellate court will then review the sanctions order for abuse of discretion, thereby giving great deference to the trial court's ruling and only reversing that ruling if it was unreasonable or arbitrary. Therefore, the appellate court will likely affirm the order imposing sanctions.

(Choice B) The judge's acceptance of the amended complaint does not negate the judge's power to sanction the attorney for his deficient original complaint.

📌 Educational Objective

A court can impose sanctions for violating Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 11(b). Sanction proceedings can be initiated by (1) an opposing party, who must give the violator 21 days to correct the violation, or (2) the court, which need not give the violator time to do so.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 11(c) (sanctions for violating this rule).
  • Cooter & Gell v. Hartmarx Corp., 496 U.S. 384, 405 (1990) (establishing that abuse of discretion is appropriate appellate standard of review for Fed. R. Civ. P. 11 sanctions).
questions.zh-question:
一名特许经营人在A州的联邦法院就违约起诉了一名特许人。该特许经营人定居于B州，而该特许人的总部和主要营业地均在A州。该特许经营人的起诉状中包含一行关于属事管辖权的陈述：“本法院对本案具有属事管辖权。”作为回应，该特许人以缺乏属事管辖权为由，提出了驳回动议。

在审查了该动议和起诉状后，法官向特许经营人的律师发出了一份说明理由令，要求其解释为何不应因未能充分陈述属事管辖权而受到制裁。在说明理由听证会上，特许经营人的律师带着一份修改后的起诉状到场，以取代原起诉状。法官接受了修改后的起诉状，并驳回了特许人的驳回动议。法官还对特许经营人的律师处以2000美元的制裁，该款项需支付给法院。

案件继续进行，陪审团作出了有利于特许经营人的裁决，法官也作出了与该裁决一致的最终判决。

特许经营人的律师随后就法院的制裁决定提起了上诉。

上诉法院可能的回应是什么？

zh-choices.A: 维持处以制裁的命令。
zh-choices.B: 撤销处以制裁的命令，因为法官接受了修改后的起诉状。
zh-choices.C: 撤销处以制裁的命令，因为法官是依职权行事。
zh-choices.D: 撤销处以制裁的命令，因为法官在处以制裁前未给予21天的期限。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Rule 11

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：Rule 11 sanctions（11规则制裁）能不能在法院自行发起（sua sponte）后被上诉法院维持。

三秒认题路径：

11制裁 → 法院主动 → 无21天 → 终局后上诉 → 维持

核心法律规则

联邦民事诉讼规则 Rule 11（第11规则）要求，提交的诉状、动议或其他文件要有正确目的、法律依据和事实依据。考场上你要记住：如果是对方起诉式制裁，通常要先给 21-day safe harbor（21天安全港）；但如果是法院自己启动 sua sponte 制裁，法官只需要发出 order to show cause（要求说明理由令），不用等21天。

这题里，原告律师对 subject-matter jurisdiction（标的管辖权） 只写了一句空话，没有写出支撑事实，所以问题出在 Rule 11(b)(2)：主张没有被法律和事实支撑。法院后来接受修改后的诉状，不会把原来那次违规自动洗掉。

核心判例： Cooter & Gell v. Hartmarx Corp. — Rule 11制裁上诉时适用 abuse of discretion，所以只要原审没乱来，上诉法院通常会维持。

思维导图

先看：这是不是在打 Rule 11 sanctions（第11规则制裁） 的上诉？
入口 1：如果是对方动议 → 先有 21-day safe harbor（21天安全港）。
本题不是这个入口，因为制裁是法院自己发起。
入口 2：如果是法院 sua sponte → 只需 order to show cause（要求说明理由令）。
所以“没等21天”这条不能救律师。
再看违规点：诉状只说“法院有管辖权”→ 没写支撑事实 → Rule 11(b)(2) 出问题。
最后看上诉结果：原审有裁量，复审看 abuse of discretion。
没有明显不合理 → 答案是：维持制裁。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：法官都接受了修改后的诉状，而且案件最后原告也赢了，那就不该再罚律师了。

但考试真正问的是：原始诉状有没有违反 Rule 11，以及法院能不能对这次违规单独制裁。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以这里不要被“后面改正了”“最后赢了”带跑；sanctions 盯的是当时那份文件是否合格，不是整场案子最后谁赢。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 只写一句“法院有管辖权”，没有事实支撑，正好踩中 Rule 11(b)(2)；法院后来改收诉状，也不取消原先制裁，所以上诉法院多半维持。

❌ 概念混淆 | 修改抵消误判

✕ B: 把 amended complaint 当成能抹掉原始违规。

❌ 法律适用 | 自行启动误判

✕ C: 误以为 sua sponte 反而不能罚人。

❌ 事实误判 | 安全港偷换

✕ D: 看到 21 days 就套进来，但那是对方动议的安全港。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是谁启动制裁，再查有没有 21-day safe harbor（21天安全港），最后看上诉标准是不是 abuse of discretion。

考场速记

记忆口诀：对方动议要等21天，法院自己发起不用等；Cooter & Gell 告诉你，Rule 11 制裁上诉看 abuse of discretion，所以原审只要不离谱，通常就会维持。

reason.zh: 律师为纠正管辖权缺陷而提交的修改后的诉状。

reason.zh: 上诉法院因尊重下级法院的自由裁量权而维持原处罚决定。

reason.zh: 错误地暗示法官不能依职权主动发起第11条处罚程序。

D.text: failed to allow 21 days to pass

reason.en: Incorrectly applies the 21-day safe-harbor rule, which only governs party-filed motions.
reason.zh: 错误地适用了仅适用于当事人动议的21天安全港规则。

reason.en: Triggers court-initiated Rule 11 sanctions, which do not require a 21-day safe harbor.
reason.zh: 触发法院主动发起的第11条处罚，该程序不需要21天的安全港期。

reason.en: Shows court-ordered monetary sanctions payable to the court, which is permissible under court-initiated proceedings.
reason.zh: 展示了向法院支付的罚金处罚，这在法院主动发起的程序中是被允许的。

highlights.text: filed an appeal related to the court's imposition of sanctions

reason.en: Frames the legal question: what standard of review the appellate court will use to evaluate the sanctions.
reason.zh: 界定了法律问题：上诉法院在评估该处罚时将使用何种审查标准。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An attorney representing a defendant filed an answer in which he truthfully asserted that, after a reasonable opportunity for further investigation, it was likely that the evidence would show that the statute of limitations had expired with respect to the plaintiff's claim. The defendant's attorney signed the answer and included his email address and telephone number, but he did not attach an affidavit attesting to the truthfulness of the assertions in the answer. At a pretrial conference, the defendant's attorney asserted that he now had evidence establishing that the statute of limitations had expired. In fact, the defendant's attorney knew that the evidence eliminated the statute of limitations as a defense. The plaintiff's attorney served a motion for sanctions under Rule 11 on the defendant's attorney, but she did not file the motion with the court until a month later.
May the court impose sanctions under Rule 11 on the defendant's attorney?

choices.A: No, because the defendant's attorney truthfully asserted the statute-of-limitations defense in the answer that he signed.
choices.B: No, because the plaintiff's attorney failed to timely file her sanctions motion with the court.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant's attorney failed to attach an affidavit to the answer attesting to the truthfulness of the assertions in the answer.
choices.D: Yes, because the defendant's attorney presented the statute-of-limitations defense at the pretrial conference.

questions.explanation:
Representations to court
(FRCP 11(b))
Every pleading, motion, or other document filed must be signed by attorney (or unrepresented party), thereby certifying that:
  1. document is presented for proper purpose—not to harass, cause unnecessary delay, or needlessly increase cost of litigation
  2. claims, defenses & legal contentions are warranted by existing law or by nonfrivolous argument for revising or establishing law
  3. factual assertions have or will have evidentiary support and
  4. factual denials are warranted by evidence or reasonably based on belief/lack of information
FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

Attorneys (or unrepresented parties) may be sanctioned for violating FRCP 11, which requires an attorney to sign every pleading, motion, or other document filed with the court. By presenting the signed paper to the court, the attorney certifies that, to the best of his knowledge, information, and belief, all factual assertions have (or will have) evidentiary support.* "Presenting" a paper includes signing it, filing it, submitting it, or later advocating a position asserted within it.

Here, the defendant's attorney filed a signed answer (i.e., pleading) asserting that later evidence would likely show that the statute of limitations had expired for the plaintiff's claim. At the pretrial conference, he stated that his evidence established that it had expired (i.e., "presented" the answer by later advocating a defense asserted in it). But he did not make this assertion to the best of his knowledge, information, and belief because he knew that the evidence did not support it. Therefore, the court may impose sanctions under Rule 11 on the defendant's attorney.

*This is why the defendant's attorney cannot be sanctioned under Rule 11 for the initial filing of the answer—at that time, the attorney truthfully asserted that further investigation would likely provide evidentiary support for his statute-of-limitations defense.

(Choice A) The defendant's attorney is not subject to sanctions for filing an answer that truthfully asserted his belief that future evidence would likely show that the statute of limitations had expired. But he can be sanctioned for later advocating that position even though he knew that it was unsupported by the evidence.

(Choice B) A motion for sanctions under Rule 11 must first be served on the opposing party, who is entitled to 21 days to correct or withdraw the pleading. If this period passes without correction or withdrawal (as seen here, since one month passed), the motion may be filed with the court and will be considered timely.

(Choice C) FRCP 11 does not require the signer to attach an affidavit to the answer attesting to the truthfulness of the assertions within it.

📌 Educational Objective

An attorney violates FRCP 11 by presenting a signed paper containing a factual assertion that the attorney knows does not and will not have evidentiary support. Presenting a paper includes signing it, filing it, submitting it, or later advocating a position asserted within it.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 11 (setting out the signature requirement, its effect, and sanctions for failure to comply).
questions.zh-question:
一名代表被告的律师提交了一份答辩状，其中他如实主张，经过合理进一步调查的机会后，证据可能表明原告的诉讼请求已超过诉讼时效。被告律师签署了答辩状，并附上了他的电子邮件地址和电话号码，但他没有附上宣誓书证明答辩状中主张的真实性。在一次庭前会议上，被告律师主张他现在有证据证明诉讼时效已过期。事实上，被告律师知道该证据消除了诉讼时效作为一项抗辩。原告律师向被告律师送达了Rule 11下的制裁动议，但直到一个月后才向法院提交该动议。
法院是否可以根据Rule 11对被告律师施加制裁？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为被告律师在他签署的答辩状中如实主张了诉讼时效抗辩。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为原告律师未能及时向法院提交她的制裁动议。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为被告律师未能将宣誓书附在答辩状上，以证明答辩状中主张的真实性。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为被告律师在庭前会议上提出了诉讼时效抗辩。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Rule 11

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：Rule 11（联邦民事诉讼规则11）里，律师后来在庭前会议上继续主张一个自己明知没证据支撑的抗辩，法院能不能罚他。

三秒认题路径：

签字答辩 → 后来主张 → 明知不实 → 规则11 → 可制裁

核心法律规则

Rule 11（联邦民事诉讼规则11）要求律师签署的诉状、动议或其他提交法院的文件，必须有合适目的，且事实主张要有或将有证据支持。这里的关键是：presenting 不只包括签字和递交，也包括之后继续替文件里的立场“站台”。

所以，律师一开始真诚地写“以后调查也许能找到证据”，通常还不挨罚；但如果后来明知证据根本不支持，仍在庭前会议上坚持这个抗辩，就等于把一个无证据支持的立场继续推给法院，能触发制裁。

核心判例： Rule 11 的标准在这里不需要背大案名；抓住官方规则本身就够了——presenting 包括 later advocating，所以后来明知失实还继续主张，会被罚。

思维导图

先看：这是不是“文件刚签完就罚”的题？
NO：题目不是罚初次签字本身，而是罚后来的庭前表态。
再看：律师后来有没有继续主张答辩里的立场？
YES：庭前会议上说“现在有证据证明诉讼时效已过”。
关键卡口：这句话是不是 to the best of his knowledge, information, and belief？
NO：律师其实知道证据并不支持这个抗辩。
卡死点：later advocating（后来继续主张） + 明知无证据 → Rule 11 可制裁
结论：初次答辩不罚，后来坚持错误立场要罚。
答案：选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：律师一开始在 answer 里写得还算诚实，而且还等过了一个月才提 sanctions motion，所以应该不能罚。

但考试真正问的是：他后来在 pretrial conference 里明知证据不支持，还继续把这个抗辩当真去主张，这已经是 later advocating。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 pretrial conference 时律师仍继续主张时效抗辩，而他已知道证据不支持，属于 Rule 11 的后续“presenting”，所以可制裁。

❌ 概念混淆 | 初次签字误判

✕ A: 把“最初答辩真诚”当成永久免罚，漏掉了后来继续主张这一步。

❌ 法律适用 | 通知期限误判

✕ B: 看到 one month later 就以为太晚；其实 21 天安全港已经过了，仍可提交法院。

❌ 事实误判 | 额外宣誓偷加

✕ C: 乱塞 affidavit 这道门槛，但 Rule 11 根本不要求给答辩再附宣誓书。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓 Rule 11 的“后来继续主张”再看安全港，别被“最初写得真诚”带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“先签字，后主张；明知假，照样罚。” 看到 Rule 11，先想 presenting 不只是一开始递交，还包括后来在庭上继续替它站台。
