questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A federal court in State A properly certified a class action against a company incorporated in State A for fraudulently marketing annuities to customers in violation of federal law. The certification was based on the predominance of common questions of law. The court subsequently rendered a judgment in favor of the company.
One member of the class who received proper notice of the action and did not elect to opt out initiated a lawsuit against the company in federal court in State B. The class member's suit seeks damages stemming from the company's fraudulent marketing of an annuity that she purchased from the company through its sales representative based in State B. The class member is domiciled in State B. The company has moved to dismiss this suit on the grounds that the class member's claim is precluded by the judgment in the class action.
How should the court rule?

choices.A: For the class member, because she did not expressly agree to be a member of the class action.
choices.B: For the class member, because she did not have minimum contacts with State A.
choices.C: For the company, because a judgment in this type of class action is enforceable against all members of the class.
choices.D: For the company, because the class member did not opt out of the class action.

questions.explanation:
Notice and binding effect of class action suits
Types of class actions

Prejudicial risk

Separate actions create risk of inconsistent decisions OR impairing absent members' interests

Final equitable relief

Opposing party's actions generally apply to whole class so injunctive or declaratory relief is appropriate

Common question

Common questions predominate over individual questions AND class action is best method to resolve dispute

Notice optional (since class members cannot opt out)
Notice required (since class members can opt out)

Binding effect

Class members not opting out bound by final judgment or court-approved settlement, compromise, or voluntary dismissal

A class action is a lawsuit in which one person, or a small group of people, is authorized to represent the interests of a larger group. A federal court has the power to certify (i.e., authorize) the following types of class actions:

  • Prejudicial risk – separate actions would create a risk of (1) inconsistent decisions regarding the parties or (2) impairing absent class members' interests
  • Final equitable relief – injunctive or declaratory relief is appropriate because the opposing party's actions generally apply to the whole class
  • Common question – common questions of law or fact predominate over individual questions, and a class action is the best method to fairly and efficiently adjudicate the dispute

Although a valid judgment generally binds all members of the class in a "prejudicial risk" or "final equitable relief" class action, an exception applies to "common question" class actions (Choice C). In a common-question class action, a valid judgment is not binding on any class member who opted out of the lawsuit.

Here, the State A federal court properly certified the class action against the company based on the predominance of common questions of law. The court later rendered a judgment in the company's favor. The class member subsequently filed a suit in State B federal court against the company on the same grounds as the class action, and the company moved to dismiss it. Because the class member did not opt out of the class action, the State A court's judgment is binding on her. Therefore, the court should rule for the company and dismiss the class member's suit.

(Choices A and B) A class member who does not opt out of a common-question class action is bound even if the class member did not expressly agree to be a member of the class action or lacks minimum contacts with the state in which the class action was decided.

📌 Educational Objective

In a class action that was certified based on predominating common questions of law or fact, a valid judgment is not binding on any class member who opted out of the lawsuit.

📚 References
  • Fed. Rule Civ. P. 23 (class actions).
questions.zh-question:
A州的一家联邦法院正式认证了一项针对一家在A州注册成立的公司的集体诉讼，理由是该公司欺诈性地向客户推销年金，违反了联邦法律。该认证是基于共同法律问题的主导性。法院随后作出了有利于该公司的判决。

该集体诉讼的一名成员收到了该诉讼的适当通知，但未选择退出（opt out）。她随后在B州的联邦法院对该公司提起了一项诉讼。该集体成员的诉讼旨在寻求损害赔偿，源于她通过该公司在B州的销售代表购买的一份年金，而该公司对该年金进行了欺诈性推销。该集体成员的住所地在B州。该公司已动议驳回此诉讼，理由是该集体诉讼的判决阻却（precluded）了该集体成员的索赔。

法院应如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 支持该集体成员，因为她没有明确同意成为集体诉讼的成员。
zh-choices.B: 支持该集体成员，因为她与A州没有最低限度联系（minimum contacts）。
zh-choices.C: 支持该公司，因为此类集体诉讼的判决对所有集体成员均可强制执行。
zh-choices.D: 支持该公司，因为该集体成员没有选择退出（opt out）该集体诉讼。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：按共同问题认证（common-question class action）后，没选择退出（opt out）的成员会不会被既判力（preclusion）绑定。

三秒认题路径：

集体诉讼 → 共同问题认证 → 收到通知 → 没退出 → 受判决约束

核心法律规则

先抓规则，再看结论

共同问题 class action（common-question class action）里，法院会发通知，成员通常可以选择退出（opt out）；选择退出（opt out）的人不受判决绑定，没退出的人会被最终判决（final judgment）约束。

这里题干说的是按共同问题（predominance of common questions）认证，而且这个成员已经收到通知却没有退出，所以她后面再起诉同一索赔，法院可以用既判力把她挡回去。

核心判例： Fed. R. Civ. P. 23 的共同问题 class action 规则——没退出的成员，会被有效判决绑定。

思维导图

先问：这是不是 共同问题 class action（common-question class action）？
是法院会给通知，成员可以 opt out
没退出
→ 最终判决绑定，不能再就同一请求重复起诉
退出了
→ 不受该判决约束
常见误区
以为“我没亲自签字”就不受影响：错，opt out 才是关键。
结论：选 D，公司胜诉

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她没有明确同意加入诉讼，也没在 State A 打官司，怎么会被绑定？

但考试真正问的是：在 共同问题 class action 里，关键不是“有没有亲笔同意”，而是“有没有收到通知后选择退出”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干已给出 收到通知却没退出，共同问题 class action 的有效判决会绑定她，所以公司可以主张既判力。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“没亲自签字”当成免责条件，漏了 opt out 才是关键。

❌ 事实误判 | 诉讼地偷换

✕ B: 拿 State A 的管辖接触点做文章，但绑定力看的是 class notice 和退出，不是她和 State A 的最低联系。

❌ 法律适用 | 绝对化绑定误判

✕ C: 说“所有成员都必然受约束”太满了，真正限定词是 not opting out。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认 class action 类型，再只盯通知与退出；别被当事人同意和管辖接触点带偏。

考场速记

记住：共同问题 class action = 通知 + 可退出 + 不退出就绑定。看到成员后来又起诉，先问他当初有没有 opt out。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A motorcyclist from State A, who suffered severe injuries in an automobile collision with a driver from State B, filed a complaint against the driver in federal court. In her complaint, the motorcyclist sought to recover special damages for her medical expenses by requesting that the driver pay "my medical expenses." Fifteen days after being served with process, the driver filed a motion for a more definite statement. The motion alleged that the complaint failed to state with specificity the medical expenses incurred by the motorcyclist and set forth the details that needed to be included.
Will the driver likely succeed on his motion for a more definite statement?

choices.A: No, because claims for damages may be alleged generally.
choices.B: No, because the driver has yet to conduct discovery.
choices.C: No, because the driver must file an answer before he can make this motion.
choices.D: Yes, because the motorcyclist failed to specifically state her claim for special damages.

questions.explanation:
Specificity of pleadings
Claim Pleading requirements
General rule • Complaint – short & plain statement of claim showing plaintiff is entitled to relief
• Answer – short & plain statement of admissions, denials, defenses & claims against other parties
Fraud/mistake/mental condition • Malice, intent, knowledge, or other mental condition may be alleged generally
• Circumstances giving rise to fraud/mistake must be stated with particularity
Conditions precedent • Assertion that conditions precedent occurred may be alleged generally
• Denial that conditions precedent occurred must be stated with particularity
Damages • General damages may be alleged generally
• Special damages must be specifically stated

A complaint is a pleading that initiates the plaintiff's lawsuit. It generally must contain a short and plain statement of the claim showing that the plaintiff is entitled to relief. However, there are special pleading requirements for certain claims, including compensatory damages. There are two main types of compensatory damages:

  • General damages – the natural and necessary results of a wrongful act that do not have a fixed value and may be alleged generally (eg, pain and suffering)
  • Special damages – the natural, but not necessary, results of a wrongful act that have a fixed value and must be specifically stated (eg, medical expenses)

When a complaint includes claims for special damages that do not contain the requisite specificity, the defendant may file a motion for a more definite statement that identifies the pleading's defects and the details needed to cure them.

Here, the motorcyclist's complaint sought to recover special damages for her medical expenses by requesting that the driver pay "my medical expenses." But the motorcyclist failed to specifically state her medical expenses—eg, "the accident caused me to suffer medical expenses totaling $100,000." Therefore, the driver will likely succeed on his motion for a more definite statement.

(Choice A) Claims for general damages may be alleged generally. But the motorcyclist's claim is for special damages, which must be specifically stated (not seen here).

(Choice B) Discovery is the pretrial phase of the lawsuit during which the parties are compelled to disclose information related to the case. Although the driver will likely learn more about the motorcyclist's medical expenses when discovery later occurs, this does not excuse the motorcyclist's failure to state her claim for medical expenses with the requisite specificity.

(Choice C) FRCP 12 allows a defendant to make several motions before filing an answer—including a motion for a more definite statement (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

General damages (eg, pain and suffering) do not have a fixed value and may be alleged generally in a complaint. Special damages (eg, medical expenses) do have a fixed value and must be specifically stated in the complaint.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 9(g) (pleading special damages).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(e) (filing a motion for a more definite statement).
  • 22 Am. Jur. 2d Damages §§ 42–43 (2022) (defining general and special damages).
questions.zh-question:
来自A州的摩托车手在与来自B州的司机发生汽车碰撞中受重伤，向联邦法院对该司机提起了诉讼（complaint）。在她的诉讼（complaint）中，摩托车手请求司机支付“我的医疗费用”，以追讨其医疗费用的特殊损害赔偿（special damages）。在收到送达（served with process）15天后，司机提交了一份要求更明确陈述的动议（motion for a more definite statement）。该动议（motion）声称，诉讼（complaint）未能具体说明摩托车手产生的医疗费用，并列出了需要包含的详细信息。
司机是否可能在其要求更明确陈述的动议（motion for a more definite statement）中获胜？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为损害赔偿（damages）的请求可以概括性地主张。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为司机尚未进行证据开示（discovery）。
zh-choices.C: 否，因为司机必须在提出此动议（motion）之前提交答辩（answer）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为摩托车手未能具体说明其特殊损害赔偿（special damages）的请求。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Pleadings

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：特殊损害（special damages）在起诉状里必须写得具体，像“我的医疗费”这种太笼统，法院可以要求补到更明确。

三秒认题路径：

起诉状 → 特殊损害 → 必须具体 → 太笼统 → 可补正

核心法律规则

起诉状（complaint）通常只要写简短且明确的救济请求（short and plain statement）。但特殊损害（special damages）不一样，必须具体写出来，考场意思：你得把数额或细节摆出来，不能只说“我的医疗费”。

一般损害（general damages）可以概括写，比如疼痛和精神损害；特殊损害（special damages）是有固定价值、但不一定必然发生的损失，比如医疗费，考场意思：这类钱要让对方一眼看懂你在要什么。如果没写具体，被告可用要求更明确陈述的动议（motion for a more definite statement）来逼原告补清楚。

核心判例： 本题不靠复杂判例展开，直接看 FRCP 9(g)：特殊损害必须特别列明，所以“my medical expenses” 不够。

思维导图

先看原告诉求的是哪类损害？
一般损害可概括写 → 例如疼痛与痛苦 → 不会卡在具体数额上
特殊损害必须具体写 → 例如医疗费、固定金额
只写“my medical expenses” → 没有具体数额/细节 → 触发 motion for a more definite statement
结论被告会赢这个动议 → 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：反正以后还能 discovery，被告迟早知道医疗费多少。

但考试真正问的是：起诉状当下写得够不够具体，不是以后会不会查到。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干只写 my medical expenses，这是特殊损害但没写具体数额或细节，所以被告可要求补成更明确的陈述。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把一般损害的宽松规则套到 special damages 上了。

❌ 事实误判 | 事后补救偷换

✕ B: 盯着 discovery 误以为以后知道了就行。

❌ 法律适用 | 程序顺序误判

✕ C: before he can make this motion 这句话是错的，12(e) 可以先于答辩提出。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清损害类型，再问“这类损害能不能只概括写”。

考场速记

记忆口诀：一般损害（general damages）可以笼统写，特殊损害（special damages）必须写具体；看到“医疗费”就先想：有没有数额、有没有细节。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
In a class action lawsuit, the representative members of the certified classes reached a settlement agreement with the defendant. The court held a fairness hearing on the proposed settlement at which a member of one of the certified classes who was not a named representative of the class voiced objections. The court, finding that the settlement was adequate and fair, approved the settlement.
Can the objecting class member appeal the court's approval of the settlement?

choices.A: No, because the objecting class member was not a named representative of the class.
choices.B: No, because the objecting class member was only permitted to voice his objections at the fairness hearing.
choices.C: Yes, because any member of a class that has been certified has the rights of a party during the litigation of the class action lawsuit.
choices.D: Yes, because the representative members of the class no longer represent the objecting member's interests.

questions.explanation:
Notice and binding effect of class action suits
Types of class actions
Prejudicial risk
Separate actions create risk of inconsistent decisions OR impairing absent members' interests
Final equitable relief
Opposing party's actions generally apply to whole class so injunctive or declaratory relief is appropriate
Common question
Common questions predominate over individual questions AND class action is best method to resolve dispute
Notice optional (since class members cannot opt out)
Notice required (since class members can opt out)
Binding effect
Class members not opting out bound by final judgment or court-approved settlement, compromise, or voluntary dismissal

A class action is a lawsuit in which the court authorizes a single person or a small group of people to represent the interests of a larger group. Any certified (i.e., authorized) class action can be settled. But a class member who is not a named representative may object to a proposed settlement. If the settlement is later approved over the objection, that class member's interests are considered to diverge from those of the class representatives. The objecting class member is then permitted to appeal the court's approval of the settlement.*

Here, the court approved a class action settlement after a hearing in which the class member, who was not a named representative, objected to the proposed settlement. Because that objection resulted in the objecting member's interests diverging from the interests of the representative members, the representative members no longer represent the objecting member's interests. Therefore, the objecting member can appeal the court's approval of the settlement.

Although class members in "prejudicial risk" and "final equitable relief" class actions do not have the right to opt out, they do have the right to appeal if they objected to the proposed settlement.

(Choices A and B) Any objecting class member who is not a named representative may appeal the court's approval of a class action settlement. Further, the actions available to an objecting class member are not limited to voicing those objections at the fairness hearing; in fact, doing so permits the class member to take the additional action of appealing the court's approval of the settlement.

(Choice C) In general, only the named representatives of a class have the rights of a party during litigation (e.g., receiving service of pleadings).

📌 Educational Objective

Class actions may be settled with court approval. When a class member who is not a named representative objects to a proposed settlement and it is approved by the court, the class member may appeal the approval because the member's interests are considered to diverge from the interests of the named representatives.

📚 References
  • Fed R. Civ. Pro. 23(e) (settlement, voluntary dismissal, or compromise of class actions).
  • Devlin v. Scardelletti, 536 U.S. 1, 14 (2002) (explaining that the interests of a class member who is not a named representative diverge from those of the named representatives upon objecting to a proposed settlement, allowing the class member to appeal the court's approval of the settlement).
questions.zh-question: 在集体诉讼中，已认证类别的代表成员与被告达成了和解协议。法院就拟议的和解举行了公平听证会，其中一名已认证类别的成员（他不是该类别的指定代表）提出了异议。法院认定该和解充分且公平，批准了该和解。提出异议的类别成员可以对法院批准和解的决定提起上诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为提出异议的类别成员不是该类别的指定代表。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为提出异议的类别成员只被允许在公平听证会上表达异议。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为任何已认证类别的成员在集体诉讼的诉讼过程中都享有当事人的权利。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该类别的代表成员不再代表提出异议成员的利益。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：已认证的集体诉讼（certified class action）里，非指定代表的类成员（non-named class member）对和解提出异议后，能不能自己上诉法院批准和解。

三秒认题路径：

已认证集体诉讼 → 和解获批 → 成员异议 → 代表利益分离 → 可以上诉

核心法律规则

集体诉讼和解（class action settlement）要经法院批准；如果非指定代表的类成员（non-named class member）对和解提出异议，而法院还是批准了，考试上就把这名成员看成和代表人的利益已经分开了。此时他虽然不是名义代表，也可以就批准和解这个裁定上诉。

指定代表（named representative）才是一般诉讼中真正代班的人，考点不在“他是不是 party”，而在“他一旦反对和解，能不能继续被代表”。

核心判例： Devlin v. Scardelletti — 不是名义代表的类成员在提出异议后，可以上诉法院对和解的批准。

思维导图

先看：这是已认证集体诉讼里的和解批准吗？
是：进入 Rule 23(e)，法院可以批准和解。
再问：这个成员是不是非指定代表，而且已经在fairness hearing里提出异议？
如果是：异议后，他与代表人的利益已经分开，不再只是“被动跟着走”。
结论：他可以appeal法院批准和解。
别被这句骗：“只能在听证会上说话” ≠ 不能上诉

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他不是 named representative，所以没有上诉资格。

但考试真正问的是：他已经对和解提出异议，和代表人的立场不一样了，所以可以自己上诉。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的争议有没有在听证会上讲过」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 异议后仍被法院批准的和解，触发 Devlin 规则：类成员与代表利益分离，因此可上诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 代表身份误判

✕ A: 把“不是代表人”当成“不能上诉”，错把代表资格和救济资格混为一谈。

❌ 法律适用 | 听证即终局误判

✕ B: 以为 fairness hearing 只能发言，不能再追求上诉。

❌ 事实误判 | party权利偷换

✕ C: 把“已认证”偷换成“每个成员都像当事人一样有完整诉讼权利”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓集体诉讼中“谁在代表谁”，再看异议后代表利益是否分离。

考场速记

记忆口诀：类成员先异议，利益一分离，就能自己上诉。

顺手记： Rule 23(e) 下，非指定代表反对和解后，通常可以直接挑战批准结果。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A plaintiff sued a defendant in a federal district court for negligently causing an accident in which the plaintiff suffered severe injuries. The defendant answered the complaint and denied liability.
The plaintiff served a request for admission on the defendant. The plaintiff requested that the defendant admit that the defendant failed to stop at the intersection where the collision occurred. The defendant did not respond to the request. At the final pretrial conference two months later, the plaintiff claims that the defendant's failure to stop at the intersection should be deemed conclusively established at trial.
Is the plaintiff correct?

choices.A: No, because the defendant denied liability in his answer to the complaint.
choices.B: No, because the defendant did not admit that he failed to stop at the intersection.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant failed to respond to the request for admission.
choices.D: Yes, but only if the plaintiff demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant failed to stop at the intersection.

questions.explanation:
Effect of response to request for admission (FRCP 36)
Written response (due within 30 days of service)
Fail to respond
Admit matter
Matter conclusively
established
Deny matter
Explain lack of admission/denial
Object to request
Matter not conclusively
established

A request for admission seeks to expedite litigation and decrease costs by alleviating the need to prove undisputed matters at trial. In this method of discovery, a party requests that another party admit the truth about matters within the scope of discovery that relate to facts, the application of law to facts, opinions about either, or the genuineness of documents. The party served with the request must then serve a written response* within 30 days that:

  • admits the matter
  • specifically denies the matter in whole or in part
  • explains why the matter cannot be admitted or denied or
  • objects that the matter falls outside the scope of discovery.

An admission or a failure to adequately respond within 30 days results in the matter being admitted and conclusively established in the action unless the admission is later withdrawn or amended.

Here, the plaintiff requested that the defendant admit that he failed to stop at the intersection where the collision occurred. The defendant did not admit this fact, but he failed to respond before the final pretrial conference that took place two months after the request was served. As a result, the plaintiff is correct that the defendant's failure to stop at the intersection should be deemed conclusively established at trial (Choice B).

*Alternatively, a party served with a request for admission may move for a protective order or ask for an extension of time to respond to the request.

(Choice A) The defendant's denial of liability in the answer to the complaint does not serve as a denial to the plaintiff's request for admission.

(Choice D) To prevail at trial, the plaintiff must prove each element of negligence by a preponderance of the evidence. But the plaintiff need not satisfy this burden to conclusively establish a fact in a request for admission. The plaintiff simply needs to show that the defendant failed to respond to the request (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A party's admission or failure to adequately respond to a request for admission within 30 days after being served with the request results in the matter being conclusively established in the action.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 36 (requests for admission).
  • 8B Charles Alan Wright, Arthur R. Miller & Richard L. Marcus, Federal Practice and Procedure § 2259 (3d ed. 2020) (responses to requests for admissions).
questions.zh-question:
一名原告在联邦地区法院起诉一名被告，指控其因过失造成了一场事故，导致原告受重伤。被告对起诉状作出了答辩，并否认了其责任。

原告向被告送达了一份请求承认书。原告请求被告承认，被告在发生碰撞的交叉路口未曾停车。被告未对该请求作出回应。两个月后，在最终审前会议上，原告主张，被告未在交叉路口停车这一事实应被视为在审判中已确定无疑地成立。

原告的主张是否正确？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为被告已在其对起诉状的答辩中否认了责任。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为被告并未承认其未在交叉路口停车。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为被告未对请求承认书作出回应。
zh-choices.D: 是，但仅当原告以优势证据证明被告未在交叉路口停车时才正确。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：请求承认（request for admission） 在 30天 内不回应，会不会让事实被最终确定（conclusively established）。

三秒认题路径：

请求承认 → 30天未答 → 视为承认 → 事实锁死 → 选 C

核心法律规则

根据 联邦民事诉讼规则第36条（Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 36），request for admission 要求对方在收到后 30 天内书面回应；回应可以是承认、明确否认、解释为什么不能承认或否认，或者提出异议。未及时回应（fail to respond） 的后果很重：该事项通常就被当作承认，conclusively established。

所以这题里，原告不用再自己去证明“被告没停在路口”；题干已经给了关键事实：被告两个月都没回应。这就够把该事实锁进案子里。

核心判例： 本题不靠专门判例展开，直接按 FRCP 36 的文本规则判断：逾期不答，就按承认处理。

思维导图

Day 0
送达 request for admission
触发 30 天答复期
Day 30 内
正常做法：承认 / 否认 / 解释无法承认否认 / 提异议
两个月后
被告仍fail to respond
卡死：视为承认
试图上庭时
该事实已被conclusively established
不必再重新证明
答案
原告正确 → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告在答辩状里已经否认责任了，所以原告的请求承认就没用了。

但考试真正问的是：他有没有在 30天 内对这份 request for admission 做出书面回应。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

也别把本题和“原告在审判中要证明过失”混在一起；这里问的是 发现程序（discovery） 的效果，不是实体责任最终谁赢。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 两个月未回应，而 FRCP 36 规定逾期不答就按承认处理，所以该事实被直接锁定。

❌ 概念混淆 | 答辩当回应

✕ A: 把答辩里的否认当成这份 request 的回应了。

❌ 事实误判 | 忽略未答

✕ B: 只盯着“没承认”，漏掉了关键的“did not respond”。

❌ 法律适用 | 举证门槛搬错

✕ D: 把审判时的证明责任搬到请求承认上了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看有没有逾期未答，再直接套 FRCP 36 的“视为承认”规则。

考场速记

记忆口诀： Request for admission 先看 30 天；没答就按承认，事实直接锁死。

顺手记：本题不是比谁在实体上更有理，而是比谁在 discovery 期限内做了回应。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An employer believed that a former employee had disclosed the employer's trade secrets. As a result, the employer sued the employee in federal court for infringement of trade secrets. The employer sought to conduct an oral deposition of the employee. The employer's attorney sent the employee's attorney written notice of the deposition. On the day of the deposition, the employee and the employee's attorney arrived at the designated location, but the employer and the employer's attorney failed to attend.
What should the federal court do upon request?

choices.A: Award the employee the reasonable expenses of attending the deposition.
choices.B: Dismiss the employer's claim against the employee.
choices.C: Enter a protective order that prohibits a future deposition of the employee.
choices.D: Hold the employer in contempt of court.

questions.explanation:
Remedies for failure to attend oral deposition
Who failed to attend?
Deposing party
Require deposing party to pay other parties'
reasonable expenses of attendance
Nonparty deponent
Not served
with subpoena
Require deposing party to pay other parties'
reasonable expenses of attendance
Served
with subpoena
Hold nonparty in contempt of court
Party deponent
Impose sanctions on party deponent

A deposition is a discovery method in which a party conducts a written or oral examination* of someone (deponent) under oath and outside of court. The party seeking to conduct an oral deposition (deposing party) must provide notice to all other parties. When the deponent is a party, such notice compels the attendance of the party.

If parties that were given notice attend a deposition and the deposing party does not attend, then the deposing party is liable for the reasonable expenses of attendance (including attorney's fees) incurred by the parties that attended. The federal court should therefore, upon request, award the employee the reasonable expenses of attending the deposition.

*An oral deposition is preferred and more common because an attorney can question the deponent in real time and adjust his/her questions based on the deponent's answers.

(Choice B) A court may impose sanctions (eg, dismissing a claim) on a party who fails to attend his/her own deposition. But here, sanctions are unwarranted because the employer failed to attend the employee's deposition—not its own.

(Choice C) A protective order is a court order issued to protect a person from whom discovery is sought from annoyance, embarrassment, oppression, undue burden, or undue expense. Here, there is no indication that any such harm will result from a future deposition, so the court is unlikely to issue a protective order.

(Choice D) A court may hold a nonparty deponent in contempt of court for failing to comply with a subpoena that compels his/her attendance at a deposition (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A deposing party must provide notice of an oral deposition to all other parties. If parties that were given notice attend a deposition and the deposing party does not attend, then the deposing party is liable for the reasonable expenses of attendance, including attorney's fees, incurred by the parties that attended.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 30(g) (failure to attend deposition or serve subpoena).
questions.zh-question:
雇主认为一名前雇员披露了雇主的商业秘密。因此，雇主在联邦法院起诉该雇员侵犯商业秘密。雇主寻求对该雇员进行口头取证 (oral deposition)。雇主的律师向雇员的律师发出了书面取证通知。在取证当天，雇员及其律师抵达了指定地点，但雇主及其律师未能出席。
联邦法院应请求如何处理？

zh-choices.A: 判给雇员出席取证的合理费用。
zh-choices.B: 驳回雇主对雇员的诉讼请求。
zh-choices.C: 发布保护令 (protective order)，禁止未来对该雇员进行取证 (deposition)。
zh-choices.D: 裁定雇主藐视法庭 (contempt of court)。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery, disclosures, sanctions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：口头证言（oral deposition）里，发起取证的一方（deposing party）自己没到场时，法院要不要让他赔对方的出席费用。

三秒认题路径：

发起取证 → 自己缺席 → 对方到场 → 赔合理费用 → 选 A

核心法律规则

在 口头证言（oral deposition）里，发起取证的一方要先把通知送给其他当事人；通知到位后，出席就被强制了，所以对方来了而你没来，法院可以命你赔对方的 合理出席费用（reasonable expenses of attendance），通常还包括律师费。

这里考场意思很简单：题干不是在问“能不能惩罚被询问的人”，而是在问“发起方爽约后，谁来买单”。

核心判例： 本题主要锁定 Fed. R. Civ. P. 30(g) 的规则：发起证言的一方缺席，要赔到场方的合理费用。

思维导图

谁没来？先看“发起取证的一方”还是“被询问的人”
本题事实律师已送达通知，但 deposing party 没到；员工和律师到了。
卡死结论：不是叫对方受罚，而是让发起方赔 reasonable expenses
再分三种缺席场景
1
发起方缺席 → 赔出席费用
2
非当事人没被传票送达 → 仍然是发起方赔出席费用
3
非当事人已被传票送达却不到 → 才可能 contempt
答案入口：题干只写“员工到了、雇主没到”，所以直接落到 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然员工是被告，雇主没来是不是该直接 sanctions、dismiss，甚至对员工发 protective order。

但考试真正问的是：谁是缺席的 deposing party，以及对方是否已经被通知并到场。

这题看的是“程序上谁该付钱”，不是“谁在实体上更可恶”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里 员工和其律师已到场，但发起证言的雇主没到；按规则，法院应让雇主赔对方的合理出席费用。

❌ 法律适用 | 终局惩罚错位

✕ B: 把 dismiss 套到对方没来的场景了，题干缺的是发起方，不是员工。

❌ 概念混淆 | 保护令乱套

✕ C: 看到 protective order 就联想未来风险，但这里没有保护员工免受骚扰的事实。

❌ 事实误判 | 传票条件偷换

✕ D: contempt 主要是给没遵守传票的非当事人用的，本题没写员工被传票送达。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“谁缺席”，再看对方是否已通知到场；只要发起方爽约，先想费用补偿。

考场速记

记忆口诀：发起取证的人没到，先赔到场费；只有非当事人被传票还不来，才谈 contempt。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An individual filed an action against an acquaintance seeking damages resulting from an alleged assault and battery. Prior to trial, the acquaintance deposed a witness to the altercation. At the deposition, which was attended by the individual, the witness stated that the individual was the initial aggressor. At trial, the individual called the witness to the stand. The witness testified that the acquaintance was the initial aggressor. On cross-examination, after the witness repeated her direct testimony, the acquaintance sought to introduce the witness's deposition testimony to impeach her trial testimony that the acquaintance was the initial aggressor. The individual objected.
Should the court allow this use of the witness's deposition testimony?

choices.A: No, because deposition testimony cannot be used unless the deponent is unavailable.
choices.B: No, because the witness is not a party in this action.
choices.C: Yes, because the deposition is being used to impeach the witness's trial testimony.
choices.D: Yes, because the deposition was conducted by the party seeking to use the witness's deposition testimony.

questions.explanation:
Use of Depositions at Trial
Party-
Deponent		 All or part of deposition may be used against party if:
  • party was present or represented at deposition or had reasonable notice of it
  • it is used to extent it would be admissible under Federal Rules of Evidence if deponent were present & testifying and
  • use is otherwise allowed by Federal Rules of Civil Procedure*
Nonparty-
Deponent		 Any party may use deposition:
  • to contradict or impeach deponent's trial testimony or
  • for any other purpose allowed by Federal Rules of Evidence
Unavailable
Witness		 Party may use deposition of witness, whether or not a party, for any purpose if court finds that:
  • witness is dead
  • witness is more than 100 miles from hearing or trial or is outside United States, unless it appears that absence was procured by party offering deposition
  • witness cannot attend or testify because of age, illness, infirmity, or imprisonment
  • party offering deposition could not procure witness's attendance by subpoena or
  • on motion & notice, exceptional circumstances make it desirable in interest of justice & with due regard to importance of live testimony in open court to permit deposition to be used
*An adverse party may use for any purpose the deposition of a party or anyone who, when deposed, was the party's officer, director, managing agent, or designee.

A deposition is a discovery method in which a party conducts a written or oral examination of another party or a nonparty under oath and outside of court. Since a deposition is conducted under oath, it may be used at trial by a party in various circumstances (see table above)—including to impeach the deponent's trial testimony.

Here, the witness stated at her deposition that the individual was the initial aggressor but testified at trial that the acquaintance was the initial aggressor. For that reason, the acquaintance sought to introduce the witness's deposition testimony to impeach her trial testimony. And since this is a permissible use of deposition testimony, the court should allow it.

(Choice A) Deposition testimony can be used against an available, testifying witness for purposes of impeachment (as seen here).

(Choice B) Both parties and nonparties may be impeached at trial with their deposition testimony.

(Choice D) Use of deposition testimony is not confined to the party who conducted the deposition.

📌 Educational Objective

Since a deposition is conducted under oath, it may be used at trial to impeach the deponent's trial testimony.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 32(a)(2) (providing that depositions can be used for impeachment).

某个人对一位熟人提起诉讼，寻求因一起据称的攻击和殴打（assault and battery）所造成的损害赔偿。庭审前，该熟人对一名争执的证人进行了庭外取证（deposed）。在该庭外取证（deposition）中，该个人出席了，证人陈述说该个人是最初的攻击者。庭审时，该个人传唤该证人出庭作证。证人作证说该熟人是最初的攻击者。在交叉询问中，在证人重复了其直接证词后，该熟人试图引入该证人的庭外取证（deposition）证词，以弹劾（impeach）其庭审证词，即该熟人是最初的攻击者。该个人提出了异议。
法院是否应允许如此使用该证人的庭外取证（deposition）证词？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为除非被取证人（deponent）无法出庭，否则庭外取证（deposition）证词不能被使用。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为该证人不是本诉讼的当事人（party）。
zh-choices.C: 应允许，因为该庭外取证（deposition）正被用于弹劾（impeach）该证人的庭审证词。
zh-choices.D: 应允许，因为该庭外取证（deposition）是由试图使用该证人庭外取证（deposition）证词的当事人（party）进行的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Discovery, disclosures, sanctions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：证人庭外口供（deposition）能不能拿来弹劾（impeach）她的庭审证言。

三秒认题路径：

庭外口供 → 庭上变口 → 弹劾用途 → 允许使用 → 选 C

核心法律规则

只要证词是在宣誓（under oath）下作出的，口供（deposition）就能在庭审中用来弹劾（impeach）该证人的相反证言。这里不要求证人“不在场”，因为题目问的不是完整实质采纳，而是最常见的impeachment用途。

所以本题的关键不是“她是不是当事人”，而是“她前后说法打不打架”。联邦民事诉讼规则（Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 32(a)(2)）允许把口供拿来戳破庭上证词。

核心判例： Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 32(a)(2) — 口供可以用于弹劾，所以只要前后证言矛盾，法院就应允许用来攻击可信度。

思维导图

先看用途：这份口供现在是拿来干什么？
是用来弹劾（impeach）庭审证词
口供与庭审说法相反 → 允许用
证人庭外说：individual先动手
证人庭上说：acquaintance先动手
一旦前后打架，口供就能直接砸可信度
终点：法院应允许使用该口供
不要先钻进别的门：是否“不在场”不是这道题的门槛
题目不是在问完整采纳规则
只问弹劾用途 → 不需先证明 unavailable

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是庭外口供，就得先证明证人unavailable才能用。

但考试真正问的是：这份口供是不是拿来戳穿她在庭上的相反说法。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 deposition 与庭审证词正面冲突，最典型就是拿来弹劾（impeach）证人可信度，所以法院应允许。

❌ 事实误判 | 不必先失踪

✕ A: 把unavailable当成弹劾前提了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 当事人限定

✕ B: 误以为只有当事人证言才可被口供攻击，证人也一样能被弹劾。

❌ 法律适用 | 取证方误认

✕ D: 以为必须是原先那一方先做口供才能用，规则根本不看谁先录。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯用途，再问有没有前后矛盾；只要是弹劾，先别被“不在场”带跑。

考场速记

口供先看用途：能不能用，先问是不是拿来弹劾（impeach）；只要是庭外说法打庭上说法，就能上场。

记忆口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely”是中间上诉题的口诀；但这题不是上诉题，记住口供弹劾只看前后矛盾。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
An investor who purchased shares of a corporation's stock filed a class action lawsuit against the corporation seeking damages in excess of $75,000 based on violations of federal securities law. The investor sought certification of the class of investors who bought or sold shares in reliance on misrepresentations that materially affected the corporation's stock price. Among the issues that the class would have to establish in order to recover is that the misrepresentations were material. The investor showed that the issue of materiality was common to all of the investors and that this issue predominated over issues that affected individual members of the class. The investor did not present evidence that the misrepresentations were material.
Is the court prohibited from certifying the class under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(b)(3)?

choices.A: No, because the investor is seeking damages in excess of $75,000.
choices.B: No, because the investor showed that the issue of materiality was common to all of the investors and predominated over issues affecting individual members of the class.
choices.C: Yes, because the investor failed to establish a likelihood of success on the issue of materiality.
choices.D: Yes, because the investor is not also seeking injunctive or declaratory relief.

questions.explanation:
Class action certification requirements

Case satisfies prerequisites
  • Numerosity – joinder of all members is impracticable
  • Commonality – class shares common questions of law or fact
  • Typicality – named parties' claims or defenses are typical of class AND
  • Adequacy – named parties will protect class's interests
+
Case is suitable type of class action
  • Prejudicial risk to parties or absent class members if separate actions
  • Final equitable relief is appropriate because opposing party's actions apply to whole class OR
  • Common questions of law or fact predominate & class action is best method to resolve dispute
=
Certification permitted

A court may certify a class action as one of the three types identified in Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 23(b)*:

  • Prejudicial risk (FRCP 23(b)(1)) – when separate actions would create a risk of inconsistent decisions regarding the parties or impairing absent class members' interests
  • Final equitable relief (FRCP 23(b)(2)) – when injunctive or declaratory relief is appropriate because the opposing party's actions generally apply to the whole class
  • Common question (FRCP 23(b)(3)) – when common questions of law or fact predominate over individual questions and a class action is the best method to fairly and efficiently adjudicate the dispute

Here, the investor filed a class action lawsuit and sought certification of a class of investors who bought or sold shares in reliance on misrepresentations that materially affected a corporation's stock price. The investor showed that the issue of materiality was common to all the investors and that this issue predominated over issues affecting individual investors—i.e., satisfied the requirements of a common-question class action. Therefore, the court is not prohibited from certifying the class under FRCP 23(b)(3).

*Certification also requires satisfaction of the four prerequisites—numerosity, commonality, typicality, and adequacy—for class representatives to sue or be sued on behalf of all members.

(Choice A) In a class action based on diversity jurisdiction, at least one class representative must have a claim that meets the statutory jurisdictional amount (i.e., exceeds $75,000). But this class action is based on federal question jurisdiction since it arises from a violation of federal securities law.

(Choice C) Class certification concerns whether a lawsuit should proceed as a class action. The likelihood of success on the underlying claims is not at issue. As a result, the investor does not need to establish a likelihood of success on the issue of materiality for the court to certify the class under Rule 23(b)(3).

(Choice D) A class action cannot be certified under FRCP 23(b)(2) unless it seeks final injunctive or declaratory relief. But this limitation does not apply to common-question class actions under FRCP 23(b)(3).

📌 Educational Objective

Certifying a common-question class action under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(b)(3) is appropriate when common questions of law or fact predominate over individual questions and a class action is the best method to fairly and efficiently adjudicate the dispute.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 23 (class actions).
questions.zh-question: 一名购买了某公司股票的投资者，以违反联邦证券法为由，对该公司提起了集体诉讼（class action lawsuit），要求获得超过75,000美元的损害赔偿。该投资者寻求对那些因依赖实质性影响公司股价的虚假陈述（misrepresentations）而买卖股票的投资者进行集体认证（certification of the class）。集体要获得赔偿，必须证明的问题之一是虚假陈述的“重要性”（materiality）。该投资者表明，重要性问题对所有投资者而言是共同的，并且该问题压倒了影响集体中个体成员的问题。但该投资者并未提供证据证明这些虚假陈述具有重要性。根据《联邦民事诉讼规则》23(b)(3)（Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(b)(3)），法院是否被禁止认证该集体？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该投资者正在寻求超过75,000美元的损害赔偿。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该投资者表明重要性问题对所有投资者而言是共同的，并且压倒了影响集体中个体成员的问题。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该投资者未能证明在重要性问题上胜诉的可能性（likelihood of success）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该投资者并未同时寻求禁令性救济（injunctive relief）或宣告性救济（declaratory relief）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：FRCP 23(b)(3) 的“共同问题是否占主导”，而不是原告能不能证明自己已经赢了。

三秒认题路径：

集体诉讼 → 23(b)(3) → 共同问题 → 占主导 → 可认证

核心法律规则

答题时只抓这条规则

共同问题（common questions）要对全体成员都一样，而且个别问题（individual questions）不能压过它；考场意思：如果大家争的核心问题是同一件事，类案就更适合一起审。

FRCP 23(b)(3)看的是“要不要按集体案处理”，不是看原告现在证据有多强；考场意思：认证阶段不要求先证明胜诉，只要看案件结构适不适合 class action。

此外，numerosity, commonality, typicality, adequacy 这四个前提也要满足；这题材料已经给了共同性和典型的主轴，所以关键不在“先证明实体赢面”。

核心判例： 本题的规则就是 FRCP 23(b)(3) 的标准：common questions 只要predominate，就可以认证，不需要先证明材料性已经成立。

思维导图

先看：这是不是在问“能不能认证 class action”？
是进入 FRCP 23(b)(3)：看 common questions 是否 predominate，且 class action 是否是最佳方法。
本题事实所有投资者都围绕同一件事——misrepresentations 是否 material。
卡死点题干已经说这点对全体成员都一样，而且压过个别问题；所以不需要先证明原告已经把 materiality 证实到胜诉标准。
结论法院不被禁止认证 class → 选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然题目说原告“没有证明”材料性，那是不是就不能认证？

但考试真正问的是：认证时看不看共同问题是否占主导，不是先不先判定实体输赢。

这里不是“先把案子赢下来再谈认证”，而是“先看案件结构适不适合一起审”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干已经给出 materiality 对全体投资者都共通且压过个别问题，所以 23(b)(3) 的门槛已过，法院不被禁止认证。

❌ 事实误判 | 管辖门槛偷换

✕ A: 这是把 $75,000 当成 class 认证门槛了。

❌ 法律适用 | 胜诉标准错位

✕ C: 认证阶段不是先考 likelihood of success。

❌ 概念混淆 | 23(b)(2) 套错

✕ D: 这是把 injunctive relief 的限制硬搬到 23(b)(3) 了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定 23(b)(3) 的“共同问题主导”门槛，再排除把实体胜诉、金钱管辖和 23(b)(2) 混进来的干扰。

考场速记

记住：23(b)(3) 记的是“共同问题压过个别问题”，不是“原告先证明自己一定赢”。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉记忆法；但这题不是上诉，是 class 认证，所以先看 predominance。

questions.subject: Civil Procedure
questions.question:
A husband and wife from State A divorced. As part of their divorce settlement, the husband agreed to keep the wife as the sole beneficiary of his employer-sponsored life insurance policy worth $100,000. A court entered this settlement agreement as part of its divorce decree.
The husband remarried and moved with his second wife to State B. The husband then revised his life insurance policy to name the second wife as the sole beneficiary.
When the husband later died, the first and second wife each filed claims with the life insurance company to recover the proceeds from his policy. The insurance company, which is incorporated and has its principal place of business in State B, wants to avoid paying the proceeds twice.
If the insurance company files suit in federal district court, what procedure should the insurance company use to avoid double liability?

choices.A: Class action.
choices.B: Intervention.
choices.C: Rule interpleader.
choices.D: Statutory interpleader.

questions.explanation:
Diversity jurisdiction in interpleader actions

Rule interpleader

Complete diversity between π and Δs
πState A
> $75,000
in controversy→
Δ1State B
Δ2State B
Δ3State C

Statutory interpleader

Minimal diversity between Δs
πState A
≥ $500
in controversy→
Δ1State A
Δ2State B
Δ3State A
π = stakeholder; Δ = claimants

Interpleader is a procedure used when multiple persons claim an interest in the same property (ie, the stake)—like the wives claiming an interest in the same life insurance proceeds here. It allows the possessor of the stake (ie, stakeholder) to avoid multiple liability by joining the claimants to litigate the ownership of the stake among themselves. There are two types of interpleader with distinct subject-matter jurisdiction requirements that must be met before a federal court can hear the dispute:

  • Rule interpleader – requires that (1) the action involve a federal question or (2) the amount in controversy exceed $75,000 and complete diversity exist between the stakeholder and the claimants—ie, they must be citizens of different states
  • Statutory interpleader – requires an amount in controversy of at least $500 and minimal diversity between the claimants—ie, at least two claimants are citizens of different states

Here, rule interpleader is unavailable because the insurance company (stakeholder) from State B is not completely diverse from the wives (claimants) from States A and B (Choice C). But subject-matter jurisdiction exists under statutory interpleader because the wives are diverse and the amount in controversy exceeds $500. Therefore, the insurance company should use statutory interpleader to avoid paying the proceeds twice.

(Choice A) A certified class action allows named parties to sue or be sued on behalf of similarly situated unnamed parties. One requirement for certification is that the class be so numerous that joinder of all members is impracticable, which is not met by the two wives here.

(Choice B) A nonparty may intervene (ie, join) and participate in a pending suit to protect his/her interests. But here, there would be no need for the insurance company to intervene since it would protect its interests as a party to the suit if one is filed.

📌 Educational Objective

Diversity jurisdiction for rule interpleader requires complete diversity between the stakeholder and the claimants and an amount in controversy that exceeds $75,000. But statutory interpleader only requires minimal diversity between the claimants and an amount in controversy of at least $500.

📚 References
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 22 (rule interpleader).
  • 28 U.S.C. §§ 1335, 1397, 2361 (statutory interpleader).
  • State Farm Fire & Cas. Co. v. Tashire, 386 U.S. 523, 530–31 (1967) (explaining the minimal diversity requirements for statutory interpleader).

该保险公司应采用何种程序来避免双重责任？

zh-choices.B: 第三方诉讼。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Civil Procedure: Pretrial Procedures - Joinder of parties & claims

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：保险公司作为 stakeholder 面对两名主张同一笔保险金的 claimants，应选哪种 interpleader（利害关系人诉讼） 来避免双重付款。

三秒认题路径：

同一钱款 → 两人来要 → 想免双赔 → 看多方程序 → 选法定 interpleader

核心法律规则

只记这条就够做题

Rule interpleader（规则 interpleader） 要求 complete diversity（完全多元），也就是 stakeholder（持有争议财产的一方） 和所有 claimants（主张人） 不能同州；争议金额还要超过 $75,000。

Statutory interpleader（法定 interpleader） 只要 minimal diversity（最低限度多元）——两名主张人里至少有两人来自不同州——再加上争议金额至少 $500 就够了。

所以这题里，保险公司和其中一名妻子都在 State B，不满足规则 interpleader 的完全多元；但两名妻子分别来自 State A 和 State B，法定 interpleader 直接能用。

核心判例： State Farm Fire & Cas. Co. v. Tashire — 说明法定 interpleader 只要主张人之间有最低限度多元即可。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然保险公司已经是当事人，就该走 intervention（介入） 或者 class action（集体诉讼）。

但考试真正问的是：谁能把两个互相争钱的人拉到同一个案子里，先把“这笔钱到底归谁”一次解决掉。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的钱有没有先被两边都惦记上」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 两名妻子分别主张同一笔 $100,000 保险金，而她们之间存在最低限度多元，正好符合 statutory interpleader。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则对象错位

✕ A: 把 class action 当成多人分钱工具了，但这里只有两个直接争同一笔钱的人。

❌ 事实误判 | 当事人角色偷换

✕ B: 把保险公司说成要去 intervene，可它本来就是持钱的一方，不是旁观者。

❌ 法律适用 | 完全多元误套

✕ C: 规则 interpleader 卡在 complete diversity，因为保险公司和一名妻子同为 State B。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看谁是 stakeholder，再查规则 interpleader 的完全多元，过不了就立刻切到法定 interpleader。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先想“谁在拿同一笔钱”，再想“能不能用更宽的法定 interpleader”。

口诀补一刀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉的记忆法；但这题不是上诉题，重点还是 minimal diversity 和 $500 门槛。
